title: Lemma 1.1, the local-ring lifting lemma
statement: Let `F ⊂ ℝ` be a number field, `E = F(i)`, `U` its unit vectors (`u ū = 1`), `R = ℤ[U]` the ring they generate. If a maximal ideal `m` of `R` contains a rational prime `p`, there is a conjugation-stable prime `P` of `𝒪_E` above `p` with `R ⊆ 𝒪_{E,P}` and `ker(R → κ_P) = m`.
grade: hand; GPT Astra
rests_text: T2 (Theorem 1.2), the maximal-ideal-to-stable-prime step every later theorem in this file uses.
kernel: superseded in valuation form (M2, 2026-09-25; `plans/M2-derivation.md` §I.9): `HadwigerNelson.UnitRing.inv_mem_iff_forall_valuationSubring` (`Proofs/HadwigerNelson/UnitRing.lean`; Chevalley's domination does the lifting in valuation form); the prime (lying-over) form of this lemma stays row 57's gap.

statement: For every real number field `F`, `E = F(i)`, `R` its unit-vector ring, and every rational prime `p`: `1/p ∈ R` iff no conjugation-stable prime of `E` lies above `p`.

title: Theorem 3.1, the three-colour classification for `√3 ∈ F`
statement: Let `F ⊂ ℝ` be a number field with `√3 ∈ F`. Then `χ(F²) = 3` iff some prime of `F` has residue field exactly `𝔽₃` iff `L(F) = 3`; hence the local–global tightness conjecture holds for every such `F` with `L(F) ≤ 4`.

title: Theorem 4.1, the chain theorem (forced pairs give periods forming an ideal)
statement: Let `F₀ ⊆ F` be real fields, and let a finite unit-distance graph over `F₀` have distinct marked vertices `a, b` forced equal in every proper `k`-colouring; put `δ = b − a`. Then every proper `k`-colouring of `F²` is periodic under the ideal `δR(F)`. In particular, if `1/δ ∈ R(F)` — that is, `1/δ = u₁ + ⋯ + u_m` for unit vectors `u_j` — then `χ(F²) > k`, witnessed by a finite construction: place copy `j` by `z ↦ s_{j-1} + u_j z` (`s_j = δ·(u₁+⋯+u_j)`, `s_m = 1`), chaining the forced-equal pair through `s₀ = 0, s₁, …, s_m = 1`, plus the closing unit edge `0—1`; at most `m(n−1)+1` vertices (`n` the original forcer's vertex count), entirely in `F`.
grade: hand; GPT Astra
rests_text: T4 (the rhombus's `δR`-periodicity is this theorem at `k=3`); T6 (the 18-vertex instance, `k=3`, `m=6`); T7–T9 (the `8/3` chain, `k=4`); FS-48's rhombus-chain table.
kernel: kernel (M2, 2026-09-25; `plans/M2-derivation.md` §I.9, §I.1, §I.4): `HadwigerNelson.Chain.not_colorable_chain` and its three forms (`Proofs/HadwigerNelson/Chain.lean`); the ring form `HadwigerNelson.UnitRing.add_one_le_chromaticNumber_planeOver_of_inv_mem_unitRingOver` (`Proofs/HadwigerNelson/UnitRing.lean`) — in full, less the vertex bound.

title: The 18-vertex, 33-edge instance over `ℚ(√2,√3)`
statement: With `ω = (1+i√3)/2`, `δ = 1+ω`, `u = (−1+2i√2)/3` (`u ū = 1`, `1+u+ū = 1/3`, `δ(1+ω̄) = 3`), the identity `δ(1+ω̄+u+uω̄+ū+ūω̄) = 1` (six unit vectors summing, via T5, to close the chain) gives, after identifying coincident vertices, an 18-vertex, 33-edge unit-distance graph over `ℚ(√2,√3)`: not 3-colourable (exhaustive), 4-colourable, 25 of 33 edges individually critical (a reachability-checked criticality census, not a degenerate refusal). Combined with the dyadic upper bound — the completion `ℚ₂(√2,√3)` has square classes `⟨2,3⟩`, containing neither `−1` nor `−3`, so `F(i)` is unramified there with residue extension `𝔽₄/𝔽₂` and graph `K₄` — `χ(ℚ(√2,√3)²) = 4` exactly, with no Moser spindle in the field (`√11 ∉ F`): the first Moser-free four-chromatic plane in the record.
grade: tools; GPT Astra's construction, verified twice in exact arithmetic
rests_text: T5 (instance, `k=3`, `m=6`); FS-45 D2 (the kernel target); FS-48's table (`d=2` row: "χ=4" for `d ≡ 2 (mod 3)` wall-broken cases).

title: De Grey's 1581-vertex graph forces no pair at five colours, via three exhibited critical vertices
statement: De Grey's 1581-vertex 5-chromatic unit-distance graph is a 1-sum of two 791-vertex halves `A`, `B` sharing exactly the vertex `14`, joined by exactly one cross edge `(11, 802)` (verified exhaustively against `tools/degrey.py`'s output: 7,877 edges, 0 outside the decomposition). Both halves are 4-colourable (`tools/fs25_e4.py`, cadical, re-verified against the edge lists outside the solver: `[A]` all 3,938 edges proper, `[B]` all 3,938 edges proper; both refuse three colours). Gluing gives three critical vertices at four colours — `11`, `802` (delete either and the halves share only `14`, glue by matching palettes there) and `14` (delete it and the halves share no vertex, glue by *dis*agreeing across `(11,802)`) — each independently confirmed by the solver on the deletion itself. Since a forced-equal pair at five colours has at most two critical vertices at four colours (`CriticalSet.encard_criticalSet_le_two_of_forces`, row 48, `plans/M54-derivation.md` M54-T1, kernel), and this graph has three, **the graph forces no pair to share a colour in any proper 5-colouring** — the whole forced-equal half of M48's 1,248,990-pair arity-2 sweep, established with no sweep.

title: The periodic quotient of a finite Euclidean plane, identified as one explicit circulant
statement: For `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` prime, identify `𝔽_p² ≅ 𝔽_p(i)`; for a line `ℓ_γ` (kernel of `z ↦ Tr(γz)`, `γ ≠ 0`) missing the unit circle `μ_{p+1}` — equivalently `ν := N(γ)` a non-square in `𝔽_p^×` — the periodic quotient of the plane's colouring along `ℓ_γ` is exactly the circulant graph `Cay(ℤ/p, D)` with `D = { t ∈ 𝔽_p : t² − 4ν is a non-square }`: this is the trace set `Tr{ w : N(w) = ν }`, since every element of the norm-`ν` fibre has `𝔽_p`-degree exactly 2 (it lies off `𝔽_p`, `ν` being a non-square) and `X² − tX + ν` is its minimal polynomial, whose discriminant `t² − 4ν` is a non-square exactly on that fibre. Consequences, each proved from this: `|D| = (p+1)/2` (the fibre's `p+1` elements pair off by conjugation), `D = −D`, `0 ∉ D` (since `−4ν` is a square: `4` is a square, `ν` a non-square, `−1` a non-square as `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`), and `D` is independent of the choice of `ν` up to a dilation (`D_{c²ν} = c·D_ν`, an isomorphism of the circulant) — so `C_p := Cay(ℤ/p, D)` really is one graph per prime. The complement `D^c = { x + ν/x : x ∈ 𝔽_p^× }` is the trace set of the *split* torus at determinant `ν`, of size `(p−1)/2`, giving the combinatorial description `α(C_p) = ` the size of a maximal subset of `ℤ/p` whose differences all take that form.

title: The spectral halving of the periodic-quotient circulant, and its Weil/Hoffman consequence
statement: With `D` as in T2, the circulant's spectrum is exactly half the plane's own, at a rescaled frequency: `λ_{C_p}(a) = ½ · λ_{UD(𝔽_p,2)}(a·γ)` for every `a ∈ 𝔽_p` — because characters of `ℤ/p` pull back to characters of `𝔽_p²` trivial on `ℓ_γ`, and the projection `π` restricted to the unit circle is exactly 2-to-1 onto `D` (a fibre of `Tr` over `t ∈ D` meets the circle in the two roots of `X² − tX + ν`, never in one, since `t² = 4ν` is impossible for `t ∈ D`). So `C_p`'s eigenvalues are the same Kloosterman sums M58 identified for the plane itself (row 53, `λ(c) = −K(1, c/4)`), obeying the identical Weil bound `|λ| ≤ 2√p`, halved to `√p`, giving by Hoffman `χ(C_p) ≥ 1 + (p+1)/(2√p)` with no computation — exceeding 5 from `p ≥ 67`. The **exact** spectrum, computed here (a sum of at most 66 cosines, no numerical delicacy), pushes the crossing to `p = 59`. So of the registered prediction P7 (`χ(C_p) ≥ 6` for every `p ≥ 23`, `plans/M61-local-global-tightness.md`), only `p ∈ {23, 31, 43, 47}` remain open — each now a ≤ 376-variable SAT instance, "genuinely kernel-promotable by `decide` or a short LRAT chain", rather than an open-ended table.

title: The valuation law is the exponent-2 member of the additive-colouring family
statement: For a `K`-object, every additive `k`-colouring's floor is `kΛ` — a nonvanishing additive homomorphism to a group of order `k` identifies every pair whose difference lies in `kΛ` (kernel, `Additive.addMonoidHom_apply_eq_of_sub_eq_nsmul`), sharpened for a non-cyclic target of exponent `e < k` to the strictly larger `eΛ` (kernel, `addMonoidHom_apply_eq_of_sub_eq_exponent_nsmul`). At four colours the residue colouring of Theorem B is exactly the exponent-2 instance of this family: its target is `𝔽₄`'s additive group, `ℤ/2 × ℤ/2`, of exponent 2 — so the valuation law's verdict ("forced ⟹ 2-adic depth ≥ 1", row 59) is the *whole reach* of every additive four-colouring, and **no additive four-colouring can ever separate a pair of 2-adic depth ≥ 2** (using all six `ℤ/4` and two `ℤ/2 × ℤ/2` homomorphisms buys exactly one more level of depth beyond the valuation law's own, and no member of the family buys a second). Consequently a pair at depth ≥ 3 — such as the 16-pair residue measured on the 1,953-point object `object-pth1-vdel28-it2v2-depth1` (13,796 unit edges; `data/m56/kempe-object-pth1-vdel28-it2v2-depth1-k4.json`, reproduced exactly here: 178 pairs at `d² = 64/9`, 11 at `d² = 64/3`, matching the artifact's `F_add = 2,513`, `F_K = 187`, `F_true = 171`, residue `= 16` counts) — cannot be explained or refuted by any arithmetic in this family; the question of whether those 16 pairs are forced belongs to the reconfiguration graph of the colouring space (Kempe swaps), not to the lattice.

title: The `L↔S` involution is an arena isometry
statement: Let `σ` be the Galois automorphism `√3, √11 ↦ −√3, −√11` of `K` (one generator of Parts's order-24 group, identified as such in `plans/M62-derivation.md` M62-T4) and `ρ = ρ₁₅` the type-M rotation. Since `ρρ̄ = 1` and `σ` is in the symmetry group: **`ρσ(L ∪ ρS) = σS ∪ ρ(σL)`** — the arena built from `(L, S)` is isometric to the arena built from `(σS, σL)`. Consequently `refutes(L ∪ ρS) ⟺ refutes(σS ∪ ρσL)` and the two selections have equal weight (`σ` permutes each orbit to one of equal size).

title: The multiquadratic two-colour iff
statement: For a real multiquadratic number field `F` with 2-adic square-class image `V ⊆ ℚ₂^×/ℚ₂^{×2}`: `χ(F²) = 2` if and only if `[−1] ∉ V` and `[3] ∉ V` — equivalently, iff no odd element of `F`'s square-class group is `≡ 3 (mod 4)`. **Sufficiency:** when `[−1] ∉ V`, the extension `E(i)/E` (`E` the 2-adic completion) is ramified exactly when `[3] ∉ V` (the unique unramified quadratic extension of `ℚ₂` is `ℚ₂(√5)`, so `[5] ∈ V` is the case `[3]` need not decide alone — handled explicitly), and a ramified extension puts conjugation in the inertia group, so every unit vector's residue is `1` and a linear functional two-colours the plane. **Necessity:** `[3]` or `[−1] ∈ V` means an odd `e ≡ 3 (mod 4)` lies in `F`'s square-class group, so `ℚ(√e) ⊆ F`, and `[Fischer1990]` Theorem 8 already refuses two colours there.

title: The square-class decomposition
statement: Every real multiquadratic field lies, once `√2` is adjoined, in a compositum of two test-passing fields. Let `W` be the 2-adic square-class group of `D ∪ {2}` for a set `D` of natural numbers. `W` is the sum of two pieces — the classes localizing into `{1,3,2,6}` and those localizing into `{1,3,10,14}` — and **neither piece's 2-adic image contains `[−1]`**. Consequently `ℚ(√d : d ∈ D)` lies in the compositum of the two pieces' fields; if `D ⊇ {3, 11}`, each piece's plane needs at least four colours (a Moser spindle sits in both, since `[3]` localizes into both pieces). Instance: `K(√14)` and `K(√70)` both pass the test, and the plane over their compositum needs **at least five** colours (`√5 = √70/√14` puts a Heule-510-shaped certificate there, reduced through the 11-plane).

title: the period-set structure at levels 2–4
statement: At level 2 (`P₂ = K₄ □ K₄`, the isomorphism `x + εy ↦ (y, y − x)`), every proper 4-colouring is periodic under a nonzero element `δ = δx + εδy` with `δy ≠ 0`: order 4 for the 144 of 576 colourings whose row set is `V₄` (`δ` the graph of an additive automorphism of `𝔽₄`), order 2 for the 432 whose row set is a cyclic group of order 4 (`δ` a single nonzero element) — proved from the classification of sharply transitive sets of `S₄` containing the identity (`V₄` or one of three cyclic groups of order 4). [tools, complete finite enumeration] At levels 3 and 4 the period structure is a complete census (4,896 colourings at level 3, period-group orders `4·3456 + 8·1152 + 16·288`; 1,179,936 at level 4, orders `8·1154304 + 16·23616 + 32·1728 + 64·288`): every colouring has a period in each fixed `μ₃`-triple `2x·{1,ω,ω²}` (`x` ranging over five triples at level 4), no single element and no two of a triple are unavoidable, and the norm-one classes of `x` obey the `μ₃`-triple law while the others (`x ≡ 1 + πω, 1 + πω²` mod `𝔓²`) have counterexamples (2 of 5 triples at level 4, 8 of 21 at level 5).

title: Hoffman-tight Cayley graphs force balanced, gap-free, `H_min`-periodic colourings
statement: Let `Γ = Cay(G,S)` be a `d`-regular Cayley graph on a finite abelian group `G` (`S = −S`, `0 ∉ S`) with least eigenvalue `λ_min`. Call `Γ` **k-tight** if `λ_min = −d/(k−1)` (Hoffman's ratio bound `α ≤ n(−λ_min)/(d−λ_min)` holds with equality). If `Γ` is k-tight, every proper `k`-colouring `C` satisfies: (i) every colour class has exactly `n/k` elements, attaining the ratio bound; (ii) every colour class's indicator lies in `span(1, E_min)` (`E_min` the least eigenspace); (iii) with `H_min := ⋂{ker χ : λ_χ = λ_min}` over the characters of `G`, `C` is `H_min`-periodic — `Forces (addCayley S) k 0 h` for every `h ∈ H_min`; (iv) `C` has no fan gap.
grade: hand; de Bruijn, FS-38 phase D
rests_text: `LEDGER.md` row 67's "Derived" clause; FS38-D2-B (the 2-adic instance); FS38-D3 (the general classifier and its propagation); stubs FS-41 (`forces_of_tight`) and FS-42 (5-tight quotients), both minted from this theorem at the FS-38 close.

title: the 2-adic tower's 4-colourings are pulled back from level 4, for every m ≥ 5
statement: Let `P_m := twoAdicPlane m`, the record's ring-free `addCayley` representation of `Cay(O/𝔓^m, S_m)` (`O = ℤ₂[ω][√3]`, `𝔓² = (2)`; **that `twoAdicPlane m` IS `Cay(O/𝔓^m, S_m)` is [hand], three independent constructions agreeing** — the record's own, an independent ring-axiom build (`build/fs38-d/tower.py`, §0), and T's closed-form circle lists, matching at levels 4 and 5). `P_m` is 4-tight at every level `m ≥ 1` (**re-sourced at FS-86's close:** FS38-L1's tightness half is defective, see its entry; levels 1–8 by the exact table, reproduced independently by FS-86's B2, and every level by FS38-L2's non-strict half, `plans/FS86-derivation.md` FS86-B1-LD), with exactly 45 minimising characters at level 4 whose common kernel is trivial (a finite `decide`: sums of 24 fourth roots of unity). For every `m ≥ 5`: a character of `O/𝔓^m` is either primitive with `|λ| < 2^{m−1}` (FS38-L2–L3) or a pullback of a level-`(m−1)` character with eigenvalue `2λ' ≥ −2^{m−1}`, equality iff the level-`(m−1)` character minimises; hence `λ_min(P_m) = −2^{m−1}` and the minimisers of `P_m` are exactly the pullbacks of the 45 minimisers of `P₄`, so `H_min(P_m) = 𝔓⁴/𝔓^m`. By FS38-D2-A(iii): **every 4-colouring of `P_m` is `𝔓⁴`-periodic**, `Forces (twoAdicPlane m) 4 x y ↔ x − y ∈ 𝔓⁴` and `Separated (twoAdicPlane m) 4 x y ↔ y − x ∈ S_m + 𝔓⁴`, for every `m ≥ 5`; the tower's colouring space is exactly `P₄`'s (1,179,936 colourings); the forcing lives in no natural proper subgroup (18 sub-Cayley graphs of `P₅` down to index 2 are all free at `(0,4)`, verified colourings) and is an extremal property of the whole Cayley graph, transferring freeness only to any finite chunk that maps into it — never forcing.

title: the tight/slack classifier propagates up a tower, and no usable prime above 3 is tight at any k ≤ 7
statement: For a tower `Cay(G_m, S_m)` whose level maps `S_{m+1} → S_m` are onto with constant fibre size: k-tightness of level one propagates to every level (FS38-L1's argument in general form), carrying with it gap-freedom and `H_min`-periodicity of every k-colouring (FS38-D2-A); slackness propagates too. **[Correction, FS-86's close: the tightness half of this propagation rests on FS38-L1's defective half and is false for general towers (FS86-B2-T2); the slack half stands; where tightness at every level is needed, cite FS38-L2's non-strict half (FS86-B1-LD) or FS86-Cx-C12p1.]** The sign of `λ_min + d/(k−1)` at level one classifies the tower — zero is tight, negative is slack — and **this is the correct one-line form of `CLAUDE.md` G54**: a residue plane seals a field's pair compulsions at k colours when it is slack (gap ⇒ free, kernel, row 66) and forces them when it is tight (FS38-D2-A); "no gap at level one" is not the hypothesis that propagates ("gap-freedom above level 2 is not inherited from level one by any local mechanism", since the clique number drops to 3 from level 3 on). [tools, exact character sums, `tightsweep.py`] Computed: tight at 2 (k=4, this file) and at 3 (k=3, the rhombus, row 58); slack at 7 (k=4), 11, 19, 23 (k=5), 83 (k=6). **No usable prime plane above 3** (`p ∈ {7,11,19,23,31,43,47,59,67,71,79,83,103,107}`, `p ≡ 3 mod 4`, `p ≤ 149`) **is k-tight for any k ≤ 7** (closed by T and Poros, the same day, via the Weil cutoff): tightness at `k` needs `(p+1)/(k−1) ≤ 2√p`, which holds only for `p ≤ 13, 31, 61, 97, 139` at `k = 3,4,5,6,7`, and over the committed table `d/|λ_min|` is integral only at `p = 3` (exactly 2.000000), with `p = 31` the nearest miss at `k = 4` (margin `+4.4·10⁻⁵`, the last prime the cutoff could have allowed) and `p = 23` next (`+0.0148` at `k=4`); two scope riders — `k ≤ 7` only, and only the usable primes in the committed table. [tools, exact, solver-free, two engines as a control only] **The 3-adic instance**: `Cay((ℤ/3^m)², {a²+b²=1})` at three colours is 3-tight at levels 1–4 (`λ_min = −2,−6,−18` against `d = 4,12,36`, exactly `−d/2`), four minimising characters throughout, `H_min = 3·(ℤ/3^m)²` from level 2 (confirmed to level 3 on an independent construction), so **every 3-colouring of `UD(ℤ/9,2)` is 3-periodic** — a prediction met with no solver by FS38-D2-A's mechanism; the ℤ/9 asks were run only as a control on the corollary (all eight nonzero fibre differences refused at three colours on two engines, CaDiCaL and Glucose, agreeing; the valuation-0 non-edge control free), never as its test.

title: tightness (and slackness) propagate up a level map with onto, constant-size fibres
statement: If `S_{m+1} → S_m` is onto with fibres of size two, a character `χ` of `O/𝔓^m` pulled back to level `m+1` has eigenvalue `2λ_χ`, and `d_{m+1} = 2d_m`. So if `P_m` is 4-tight, `λ_min(P_{m+1}) ≤ 2λ_min(P_m) = −d_{m+1}/3`; since `P_{m+1}` is 4-colourable (pull back any colouring of `P_m`), Hoffman's bound gives `≥`, so `P_{m+1}` is 4-tight. With `P₁ = K₄` 4-tight (`λ_min = −1 = −3/3`), **every level `m ≥ 1` is 4-tight, balanced, gap-free, with no solver.** The same one-line computation shows `λ_min/d` is non-increasing under pullback, so **slackness propagates up too**: a tower whose level one is slack is slack at every level. **Correction (FS-86's close, 2026-09-25; found by FS-86's B2, confirmed by the owner): the tightness half does not follow.** Four-colourability with Hoffman's bound gives `n/4 ≤ α ≤ n·(−λ)/(d − λ)`, i.e. `λ_min ≤ −d/3` — the same direction as the pull-back bound, so nothing bounds `λ_min(P_{m+1})` from below. **The slack half stands.** The 2-adic tower's tightness at every level survives on other grounds (the exact table at levels 1–8; FS38-L2's non-strict half at every level, `plans/FS86-derivation.md` FS86-B1-LD; D2-B's induction on L2–L3); the general sentence "tightness propagates up a tower with onto, constant-size fibres" is **false**: FS-86's `Λ₅₁₀` has 2-power quotients with constant fibres from level 11, tight at 14 and slack at 24 (FS86-B2-T2). In the unramified quadratic dyadic class the correct statement is FS86-Cx-C12p1.

title: the primitive-character bound
statement: For `m ≥ 2` and `χ` a character of `O/𝔓^m` nontrivial on the top fibre `𝔓^{m−1}/𝔓^m ≅ 𝔽₄`: pairing the two lifts `s₀, s₀(1 + π^{m−1})` of each `s̄ ∈ S_{m−1}` gives `λ_χ = 2·Σ{χ(s₀) : s̄ ≡ a₀ (mod 𝔓)}` for the unique `a₀ ∈ 𝔽₄` with `ψ(a₀) = 1` (`ψ(t) := χ(π^{m−1}t)`, a nontrivial character of `(𝔽₄,+)`), a sum of `2^{m−2}` roots of unity, so `|λ_χ| ≤ 2^{m−1}`, **with equality only if `χ` is trivial on `a₀·M_m`** (`M_m := ⟨t − 1 : t ∈ S_m^{(1)}⟩`, the norm-one units of `O/𝔓^m` congruent to 1 mod `𝔓`). If `M_m ⊇ 𝔓^{m−1}/𝔓^m`, equality forces `χ` trivial on `𝔓^{m−1}` — a contradiction; **so every primitive character has `|λ_χ| < 2^{m−1}`, given that hypothesis on `M_m`** (supplied by FS38-L3 for `m ≥ 5`).

title: the elementary-divisor certificate: `𝔓⁴ ⊆ M` and `𝔓³ ⊄ M`
statement: Let `U₁` be the norm-one units of `O` congruent to 1 mod `𝔓`, `M := ℤ₂-span{t − 1 : t ∈ U₁}`. The image of `M` in `O/𝔓^m` is contained in `M_m` (FS38-L2's subgroup) for every `m` (only this direction is used or claimed — no surjectivity of `U₁ → S_m^{(1)}`). [tools, exact integer arithmetic, independently re-verified on a second code path] Four explicit elements `u ∈ ℤ[ω,√3]`, each `≡ 1 (mod 𝔓)` of odd rational norm, give vectors `t − 1` (`t = u/ū`) whose ℤ-span has 2-adic elementary divisors `1, 2, 4, 4`; since `O ≅ ℤ₂⁴` in this basis and the rational norms are 2-adic units, **`𝔓⁴ = 4O ⊆ M` and `2O = 𝔓² ⊄ M`** — sharp, and located: the second code path (built independently, without clearing denominators) confirms `2π·O = 𝔓³ ⊄ M`, failing on the `ω` and `√3ω` directions and succeeding on `1` and `√3`. Consequently `[O/𝔓^m : M_m] = 32` and **`M_m ⊇ 𝔓^{m−1}/𝔓^m` for `m = 5,6,7,8`, not for `m = 3,4`** (computed at levels 4–8 on both code paths).

title: Transcendence is free: `χ(F(t)²) = χ(F²)`
statement: For any `F ⊆ ℝ` and any `t` transcendental over `F`, `χ(F(t)²) = χ(F²)`.

title: The triple-level certificate's soundness
statement: Fix a prime `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, write `V = 𝔽_p²`, `n = p²`. For an independent set `S ⊆ V` of size `s`, let `Y_S[u,v] = (1/s)·#{z ∈ S : z+u, z+v ∈ S}` (the normalised triple count) and `M_S[u,v] = (1/s)·|S ∩ (S−(v−u))|` (the pair autocorrelation). Averaging `Y_S`, `M_S` over the group `Γ` generated by the point stabiliser `O(2,p)` (order `2(p+1)`), the swap `(u,v)↦(v,u)` and the relabelling `(u,v)↦(−u,v−u)` gives `Γ`-invariant matrices `Ȳ = Y(ȳ)`, `M̄ = M(ȳ)` linear in a vector `ȳ` indexed by `Γ`-orbits of ordered pairs, satisfying: `y_{k₀}=1` at the origin-pair orbit; `y_k=0` on every orbit touching a unit vector; `y_k ≥ 0`; `y_k ≤ y_{d(k)}` (`d(k)` the class orbit of `(0,u)`); `Y(ȳ) ⪰ 0`, `M(ȳ)−Y(ȳ) ⪰ 0`; `trace Y(ȳ) = s`. **Theorem:** given rational `λ_i ≥ 0` (one per inequality row), `ν_j` of either sign (one per equality row), and rational PSD matrices `Z₁, Z₂`, such that `N − trace Y(y) ≡ ⟨Z₁,Y(y)⟩ + ⟨Z₂,M(y)−Y(y)⟩ + Σ_i λ_i c_i(y) + Σ_j ν_j e_j(y)` identically as an affine function of the orbit variables `y`, every independent set `S` has `|S| ≤ N`, hence `α(UD(𝔽_p,2)) ≤ ⌊N⌋`.

title: Any rational PSD pair gives a sound certificate for some N (the rounding is never unsound)
statement: Given ANY rational positive-semidefinite `Z₁, Z₂`, the per-orbit recursion of `plans/FS50-certificate-soundness.md` §5 — for a non-class orbit `k`, `λ^{le_diag}_k = max(0,−a_k)` with `a_k` the "leftover" coefficient after subtracting `Z₁`'s and `Z₂`'s contributions at `k`; for a class orbit `k ≠ k₀`, the same rule against the partial sum `T_k` of `le_diag` multipliers already fixed pointing at `k`; at `k₀`, `N := T_{k₀} − a_{k₀}`; on a killed orbit the equality multiplier is free, `= a_k` — determines nonnegative `λ_i`, arbitrary-sign `ν_j` and a rational `N` making FS50-T1's identity hold exactly, coefficient by coefficient. So a wrongly-chosen or rounded `(Z₁,Z₂)` can only make `N` larger (the certificate weaker); it can never make the certificate unsound.

title: The circulant/Fourier block reformation, sound at any prime
statement: For `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, presenting `Z₁, Z₂` as `Z = Σ_b U_b Z_b U_b^T`, where each block `b` corresponds to a Fourier index `j = 0 … m/2` (`m = p+1`, the rotation group's order) and `U_b`'s columns are cosine/sine weight vectors over the `m` angles of each quadrance circle, reduces the affine identity's per-orbit sums — which naively cost `O(n²)` — to `O(m)` correlation sums `A_{xy}[d] = Σ_t x[t]y[t+d]` per block per ordered pair of circles, because summing `U Z_b U^T` over a rotation orbit slides both weight vectors together. **The reduction's soundness needs no verification of the `U_b`'s correctness**: `Z` is positive semidefinite for ANY choice of `U_b` (it is `Σ_b U_b Z_b U_b^T` with each `Z_b ⪰ 0`), so a wrong or approximate block map can only weaken the identity (via FS50-T2), never make it unsound — this is what lets the certificate exist at `p = 83` (6,889 points, `Z₁,Z₂` each `47`-million-entry matrices that fit in no file) at a cost of about `10⁸` integer operations instead of `n²` ones.
grade: hand; the FS-50 phase E implementer

title: Reflection symmetry halves the block size, losslessly (the real block form)
statement: With the base point of each quadrance circle fixed on a common reflection axis (one per circle type), the angular profile of a `Γ`-invariant matrix satisfies `f_{cc'}(d) = f_{cc'}(a_{c'}−a_c−d)` (`a_c` the reflected base point's angle), which makes the phase `exp(iπj(a_c−a_{c'})/m)·B_j[c,c']` real: the Hermitian Fourier block of size `C = p−1` (which the certificate's wire format carries as a real embedding of size `2C`, i.e. twice its true spectrum) is a diagonal-unitary conjugate of a real symmetric block of size `C`. **The reduction is exactly lossless**: the wire (Hermitian, size `2C`) block's whole spectrum equals the real (size `C`) block's, each eigenvalue doubled — an equality, not an inequality — so solving with the small block loses nothing, and the reduced dual is pushed back onto the unreduced wire form by an explicit congruence `Z_j = T_j W_j T_j^T` before the checker (which is byte-identical throughout this reduction) ever sees it. Any wrong reflection phase can only weaken the certificate (`T^T A T ⪰ 0` again, FS50-T2's fact), never make it unsound.

title: The commutant's block sizes, by dihedral character theory
statement: For `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, the permutation representation of `O(2,p)` (dihedral of order `2(p+1)`) on `V = {0} ∪ (p−1)` circles has character `fix(id) = p²`, `fix(rotation) = 1`, `fix(reflection) = p`; decomposing gives the trivial representation with multiplicity `p` (one per circle plus the origin), the two sign representations (rotation acting by `−1`) each with multiplicity `(p−1)/2` (one per circle of the matching reflection type), and each of the `(p+1)/2 − 1` two-dimensional irreducibles with multiplicity `p−1`. Hence the commutant of a `Γ`-invariant matrix — and so each of the certificate's PSD blocks at `p = 83` — decomposes into **one `83×83`, two `41×41` and forty-one `82×82` blocks**. Check at `p = 11`: `11² + 5² + 5² + 5·10² = 671`, the independently-computed Burnside orbit count on ordered pairs.

title: Consequence: L(K(√7)) = 7
statement: `K(√7) = ℚ(√3,√7,√11)`'s usable primes (row 53's sieve) are exactly 83 and every prime `≥ 103`; FS50-T1's certificate gives `χ(Γ₈₃) ≥ 7` (row 68), and every usable prime `≥ 103` has Kloosterman/Hoffman spectral floor `≥ 8` (row 53, G44's Weil argument). So every usable residue plane of `K(√7)` has `χ ≥ 7`, hence its local bound `L(K(√7)) = 7`; under the local–global conjecture's bold form (G48), `χ(K(√7)²) = 7`, and since `K(√7)` is a subfield of `ℝ`, `χ(ℝ²) = 7` follows *under the conjecture* — the mission's target statement, pinned to the one 6-open field this project has itself built a five-chromatic object in (row 64).

title: Hoffman-tightness forces `(k−1) ∣ (q+1)`
statement: For the finite Euclidean plane `UD(𝔽_q,2)`, `q ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, degree `d = q+1`: if the plane is Hoffman-tight at `k` colours (`λ_min = −d/(k−1)` exactly), then `(k−1) ∣ (q+1)`.
grade:

title: G57: the window's clique split
statement: the window's clique-number split coincides with its field-exclusion split, and no candidate field holds a Moser spindle. (a) **[Krebs2022, prior art, re-verified here by direct search rather than cited]:** `ω(UD(𝔽_q,2)) = 3` iff the characteristic is 3 or 3 is a square in `𝔽_q`, else `ω = 2`; verified at 21 planes spanning both residue classes mod 4 (`q = 5,7,…,83`), 21 of 21 agreeing, so the rule holds uniformly in `q mod 4`, not only at `q ≡ 3 (mod 4)`. (b) **[derived, the one-direction transfer]:** a real number field `F` has `√3 ∈ F` only if every usable residue plane of `F` has `ω = 3` (usability requires `3` to be a square in `𝔽_q`, or the prime ramified with characteristic `3`); so a usable plane with `ω = 2` (triangle-free) certifies `√3 ∉ F`. (c) **[derived, the window instance]:** the eight window members split exactly four and four — `ω = 3` at `{23, 27, 47, 59}` (3 a square, or characteristic 3 at 27) and triangle-free at `{31, 43, 67, 79}` (3 a non-square) — and this split coincides *exactly* with which radicand (`3` or `11`) excludes the member for a field `⊇ K = ℚ(√3,√11)`: the four members excluded only by `√3` (`31,43,67,79`) are precisely the triangle-free four, and the four excluded only by `√11` (`23,27,47,59`) are precisely the four with triangles. **So every field this project has ever built (all contain `K`, hence both `√3` and `√11`) can reach NO window member** (G56's exclusion, re-derived from the clique split rather than only from the direct Legendre-symbol computation), and since the Moser spindle needs both `√3` (its rhombi) and `√11` (the twist `cos θ = 5/6`), **no field whose local bound could be 6 contains a Moser spindle** — every forcer this project holds is a spindle or a relative of one, so over a window field there is nothing to build *from*.
grade: prior art (Krebs2022 Lemma 5.1, Vinh2008 Theorem 13) + derived: the transfer and the window-specific coincidence
rests_text: G56 (the field-level exclusion, row 69); G57 itself (the grokking this entry files); row 69's field-naming table (the strategic redirection of any field-based hunt to `{23,27,47,59}` only); FS-53's own phase C.1 ("C.1's designer must report that split explicitly per candidate").

title: G58: `τ` must fix a colour
statement: For any putative antipodally-symmetric colouring `c(−z) = τ(c(z))` of `UD(𝔽_q,2)` with `τ` an involution of the `k` colours: every rotation fixes the origin, so `c(0) = τ(c(0))`, i.e. `τ` must fix at least one colour. **Consequence:** any candidate `τ` that fixes no colour is refuted with no solver call at all; this accounts for **73 of the 226 rows refused across seven equivariant sweeps (32%)**, including 17 of 43 at `q = 23` and 23 of 59 at `q = 47` — refusals that were never solver evidence, and a filter the tool should apply before paying for a solver call.
grade: hand; the FS-53 phase (product owner / implementer), 2026-09-16
rests_text: G58 itself (the antipodal conjecture — a reading, existence-flavoured, NOT proved by this theorem, which is a one-sided necessary condition only); the recommended fix to the equivariant-sweep tool (filter `τ`-fixed-point-free rows before any solver call); FS-55 (`plans/STUB-antipodal-colouring.md`, minted 2026-09-16 at FS-53's close, which carries this theorem verbatim in its own description).

title: 27 is the unique non-prime window member, and the reciprocity exclusion's eighth case
statement: (a) A prime power `q = p^f` gives a usable residue plane (`q ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, the condition under which `x²+y²=1` is a non-split conic with `q+1` points) **iff `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` and `f` is odd**: `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)` gives `p^f ≡ 1 (mod 4)` for every `f` (never usable); `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` gives `p^f ≡ p (mod 4)` for odd `f`, `≡ 1` for even `f`; `p = 2` gives `q ≡ 0` or `2 (mod 4)` (never usable). Among the odd prime powers `≤ 97` (Weil's cutoff for six-colourability, `5|λ_min| ≥ q+1` failing from `q=98`), only **`27 = 3³`** satisfies this — `25 = 5²` fails twice (`5 ≡ 1 (mod 4)`, and `f=2` even), `49 = 7²` fails once (`f=2` even, though `7 ≡ 3 (mod 4)` is fine); the next candidates, `3⁵=243` and `7³=343`, exceed the cutoff. So 27 is the window's unique non-prime member, "now and for good", and the tooling's prime-only assumption (`--p <PRIME>`) costs exactly this one member. (b) At `q=27`, since `3` is itself ramified there (not a square/non-square question), G56's usual exclusion test does not typecheck; the correct argument, completing the reciprocity exclusion's eighth case, is: `11 ≡ −1 (mod 3)`, and `−1` is a non-square in every `𝔽_q` with `q ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, so `√11 ∉ 𝔽₂₇` and 27 is unusable for any field containing `√11`.

title: The level-3 certificate is sound
statement: For a finite Euclidean plane `UD(𝔽_q,2)` (`q ≡ 3 (mod 4)` a prime power, adjacency = quadrance 1) with automorphism group `Γ` generated by translations, the unit-circle rotations, the reflection and Frobenius: if there exist a rational `N`, matrices `Z` (each presented as `Σ_b U_b Z_b U_bᵀ`, `U_b` any integer matrix, `Z_b` any Gram factor `GᵀG` or PSD dense rational matrix), and nonnegative rationals `λ_K, μ_K` indexed by the canonical forms `K` of independent sets of 2–4 points such that `N − Obj(y) = Σ ⟨Z, A(y)⟩ + Σ_K λ_K y_K + Σ_K μ_K (1 − y_K)` holds identically in the formal unknowns `y_K`, then every nonempty independent set `S ⊆ 𝔽_q²` has `|S| ≤ N`, hence `α(UD(𝔽_q,2)) ≤ ⌊N⌋`.
grade: hand; the certificate agent, 2026-09-16, written up for a reviewer
verdict: closes (re-derived independently here: the averaging step Y1–Y4 is a direct consequence of the group's transitivity on independent sets of a fixed size and F5's translation covariance, and the final inequality is the standard "PSD matrix pairs nonnegatively with PSD matrix" fact applied coordinatewise).
rests_text: row 70's `α(UD(𝔽₂₇,2)) ≤ 141` (hence `χ(Γ₂₇) ≥ 6`) and the re-derivation of the exact values `α(Γ₇) = 14`, `α(Γ₁₁) = 28`; the certificate files `data/fs54/cert-q{7,11,27}-l3-N*.json` and the checker `tools/fs54_l3_cert_check.py`; row 71's `α(Γ₂₃) ≤ 105` (same instrument, `data/fs54/cert-q23-l3-N105.json`, FS-56's Q0); FS54-T5 (W_f) uses the same instrument at the other window members.

title: The period-obstruction bound at `U₆₄`: a dimension-≥8-periodic independent set has ≤ 512 points
statement: If `I ⊆ 𝔽_{4096}` is independent in `U₆₄` and invariant under translation by a dimension-`≥8` `𝔽₂`-subspace `V`, then `|I| ≤ 512`. *The argument:* such an `I` is a union of `V`-cosets, so it is determined by an independent set in the 16-vertex (at `dim V = 8`) cubelike quotient graph; that quotient's independence number is at most 2, because an independent triple `{0,a,b}` in a cubelike graph would span an independent subgroup `{0,a,b,a+b}` of order 4, whose four cosets would give a proper 4-colouring of `U₆₄` — impossible since Hoffman's bound forbids `χ(U₆₄) ≤ 4`. So at most 2 of the 16 vertices of the `V`-quotient can lie in `I`'s image, and each quotient vertex lifts to a `V`-coset of `256 = 4096/16` points, giving `|I| ≤ 2·256 = 512`.
grade: hand; the FS-54 implementer, 2026-09-16; independently reproved by GPT Astra as a control
rests_text: row 70's `U₆₄` entry ("periodic sets ≤ 512 above dimension 8"); the reading that 512 is "a strong attractor" (not itself claimed as a theorem — `α(U₆₄) = 512` is unproved in general, only the periodicity obstruction is).

title: The Fourier-energy stability bound at `U₆₄`: a six-colour class must concentrate on the least eigenspace
statement: A 683-point independent set of `U₆₄` (the size a six-colour class must reach) must carry at least 50.2% of its nontrivial Fourier energy on the 195 characters with `λ = −15` (the energy-weighted mean eigenvalue over an independent set's indicator must equal `−13.008`, forced by the set's size against Hoffman's equality structure); a 586-point set (a seven-colour class) is forced nothing by the same computation. **Measured**: the six KaMIS-found 512-sets carry only 36–44% of their energy there (5–9% on `λ=+13`), well short of what a genuine 683-set would need — consistent with, but not proof of, `α(U₆₄) = 512`.
grade: hand + tools; the FS-54 implementer, 2026-09-16
verdict: closes (the arithmetic — a weighted-mean equation forced by Parseval and the eigenvalue spectrum — is a direct, checkable computation; not independently re-derived line by line here, but the mean-eigenvalue equation is a standard consequence of the Rayleigh quotient at a fixed set size and spectrum, and the KaMIS-set energies are exact Fourier-transform computations, `tools`-grade).
rests_text: row 70's `U₆₄` entry ("the 50.2% Fourier concentration of a 683-set"); the informal case that a six-colouring of `U₆₄`, if it exists, is structurally far from the sets found so far.

title: The 2-adic trichotomy, and the odd-degree corollary
statement: For a real number field `F` and a prime `𝔭` of `F` above 2: (a) if `𝔭` **splits** in `F(i)`, no colouring bound follows from `𝔭`; (b) if `𝔭` **ramifies** in `F(i)/F`, then `χ(F²) ≤ 2` regardless of `N(𝔭)` (conjugation acts trivially on the residue field, so every unit vector `w` satisfies `w² ≡ w·w̄ = 1`, hence `w ≡ 1`, and the linear map `k → 𝔽₂` sending `1 ↦ 1` properly two-colours each coset of the unit-vector group); (c) if `𝔭` is **inert**, the residue graph is `U_Q = Cay(𝔽_{Q²}, μ_{Q+1})`, `Q = N(𝔭)`. **Corollary.** Every real number field of odd degree is 2-colourable: some prime above 2 has odd local degree, so `i ∉ F_𝔭` (`ℚ₂(i)/ℚ₂` is a ramified quadratic extension, hence has even local degree over any field it sits inside with odd degree already forced), giving case (b).
grade: hand; the FS-54 implementer, 2026-09-16; partly prior art
rests_text: row 70's `U_Q` window member `U₆₄` (`6 ≤ χ(U₆₄) ≤ 8`); the field-naming table (§1.5–1.6, corrected in this same milestone); every field-degree argument in FS54-T4 and G56's exclusion; the fields `data/fs54/fields.out`, `data/fs54/quadratic-fields.out`.

title: The structure of `UD(𝔽_{3^f},2)` for `f` odd, general in `f`
statement: For every odd `f` and `q = 3^f`: (i) every edge lies in exactly one triangle, and that triangle is the `𝔽₃`-line `{z, z+u, z+2u}` through its unit direction (in characteristic 3, `2u = −u`, so a line's three points are pairwise unit-distant; a third point `w` off the edge needs `Tr(w) = 1`, whose solutions are the roots of the doubled polynomial `X² − X + 1 = (X+1)²`, giving exactly one point); (ii) the spectrum is integral (every Cayley graph on an elementary abelian 3-group has eigenvalues in `ℤ[ζ₃] ∩ ℝ = ℤ`, `[BridgesMena1982]`), with `λ_a = 3m_a − (q+1)/2` (`m_a` the number of unit directions in the character's kernel hyperplane, each contributing `2` or `−1` to the character sum); hence every eigenvalue is `≡ 1 (mod 3)`. **At `q = 27`** this forbids `λ = −11` (Weil's bound `|λ| ≤ 2√27 = 10.39` already excludes anything below `−10`, and the congruence excludes `−8 < λ < −5`… the next value down from `−8`), so `λ_min ≥ −8`, attained (56 of the 364 hyperplanes hold exactly two directions); `|Aut(UD(𝔽₂₇,2))| = 122{,}472 = 729·56·3` (translations, `O(2,27)`, Frobenius — nothing hidden).
grade: hand; the FS-54 implementer, 2026-09-16, tested at f=3
rests_text: FS54-T1's certificate (the ratio bound `729·8/36 = 162` this spectrum gives, against which the certificate's 141.59 is compared for its "reach"); FS54-T4 (the field-degree argument uses "every plane at `q = 27` has triangles" from clause (i)); the correction to G57 recorded below.

title: A field whose first usable plane is 27, with the wall broken, has even degree ≥ 6
statement: If `F` is a real number field whose smallest usable prime has residue field `𝔽₂₇` and whose 2-adic wall is broken (FS54-T2's clause (c) applies at some prime of odd norm ≤ 25 excluded), then `[F:ℚ]` is even and `≥ 6`.

title: `W_f`: the fractional wall, with no rounding, and its CRT-product closure
statement: For a finite vertex-transitive graph `G` on `n` vertices, `χ_f(G) = n/α(G)` (direct proof: summing the covering constraints over vertices gives `n ≤ α · weight`; conversely translating a maximum independent set through the vertex-transitive group and weighting each of the `n` translates `1/α` gives a fractional colouring of cost `n/α`). Hence `α(U_Q) < Q²/6` proves `χ_f(U_Q) > 6`, hence `χ(U_Q) ≥ 7`, **with no rounding assumption** (the weaker, previously-used reading `χ = ⌈n/α⌉` is a separate, unproved assertion). By Zhang's theorem (vertex-transitive `G, H`: `α(G×H)/|G×H| = max(α(G)/|G|, α(H)/|H|)`, `[Zhang2012]` Thm 1.8) and Zhu's fractional Hedetniemi theorem (`χ_f(G×H) = min(χ_f(G), χ_f(H))` for all finite graphs, `[Zhu2011]`, restated as `[Zhu2025]` Thm 2.4), for a categorical product of norm-one Cayley graphs `χ_f(Π U_{Q_i}) = min_i χ_f(U_{Q_i})`: **if every factor satisfies `α(U_Q) < Q²/6`, the product's independence ratio is also below `1/6` and the product cannot be six-coloured** — closing the "composite ideal" escape hatch with no integral form of Hedetniemi needed.
grade: proof, GPT Astra, 2026-09-16, verified here by recomputation
verdict: closes (re-derived here: the `χ_f = n/α` direct argument is elementary and checks; Zhang's and Zhu's theorems are cited from papers already held and read in full per `BIBLIOGRAPHY.md`'s rows).
rests_text: row 70's window closure ("the wall is proved with no heuristic... closes the product hatch"); FS-56's row 71 use of the same instrument at `q = 23` (`α(Γ₂₃) ≤ 105`); G59's later restatement (dated 2026-09-18, out of this milestone's scope per batch 6a's finding).

title: `U₃₂` is completely rigid at four colours: every maximum independent set is an `𝔽₄`-hyperplane, 44 in total
statement: Let `E = 𝔽_{1024}`, `S = μ_{33}` (the norm-one elements), `U_{32} = Cay(E,+,S)`. (a) **A char-2 Sidon property**: for `u, v ∈ S` with `u+v=d≠0`, `d̄ = d/(uv)`, so `d` determines the unordered pair `{u,v}` as the roots of `X²−dX+d/d̄=0`; a nonzero displacement has at most one such pair in odd characteristic away from antipodal sums, and (specialising to `Q=2^m`) exactly `2` or `0` common neighbours according to `Tr_{𝔽_Q/𝔽_2}(1/N(d))`. (b) **An explicit colouring**: with `β` a primitive 11th root, `S = 𝔽₄^*⟨β⟩`, and `T(x) = Tr_{E/𝔽₄}(x)`, the map `x ↦ T(x)` is a proper 4-colouring with all classes of size 256, so `α(U₃₂) = 256`, `χ(U₃₂) = 4`. (c) **The least eigenspace is exactly `S`**: the nontrivial eigenvalues lie in `{−11,−7,−3,1,5,9}` (Weil), every multiplicity a multiple of 33; the spectral moments (computed combinatorially, without a spectral solve, from closed-walk counts and the Sidon property) force, via the polynomial `P(X)=(X+7)(X+3)(X−5)(X−9)`, `10r_{−11}+r_1=15` with `r_{−11}` a positive integer, so `r_{−11}=1`: `{a≠0 : λ_a=−11} = S` exactly. (d) **Rigidity**: for any maximum independent set `A` (`|A|=256`), Hoffman-tightness plus (c) forces `supp(f̂) ⊆ {0}∪S`; the Sidon property forces the support `B` to satisfy `|B|≤3` and, when nonempty, `B={a,b,a+b}` with the Fourier coefficients pinned to `±1/4`; the sum-product identity of (a) then forces `b/a ∈ 𝔽₄^*`, so **`A` is an `𝔽₄`-hyperplane** `{x : Tr_{E/𝔽₄}(ax)=c}`. There are `33/3=11` directions and 4 translates each: **exactly 44 maximum independent sets, and 11 unordered colour partitions**.
grade: proof, GPT Astra, 2026-09-16, verified here by recomputation
verdict: closes (re-derived here: every step of (a)–(d) is elementary character-sum and linear-algebra reasoning over `𝔽₄`, and the milestone's own verdict table records "every step of the Fourier/Sidon argument read... moments re-derived by hand (991, 959, 63391)").
rests_text: row 70's `U₆₄` window-member discussion (contrast: `U₃₂` is rigid and settled, `U₆₄` is not); §3's consequence (a 6/7-colouring of `U₆₄` cannot be periodic under a dimension-≥8 subspace, since a 16-vertex cubelike quotient of that shape would be 4-colourable — FS54-T10 below); the char-2 Sidon property (a) is reused in FS54-T10 and FS54-T11's arguments.

title: Inert towers keep `λ_min/d`: `λ_min(G_j) = Q^{j−1}·λ_min(G₁)`
statement: Let `O` be a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser `π` and finite residue field of order `Q` (`Q` even or `Q ≡ 3 (mod 4)`), `O_E` its unramified quadratic extension, `A_j = O_E/π^jO_E`, `S_j` the norm-one elements, `G_j = Cay(A_j,+,S_j)`. Then for every `j ≥ 1`: `|A_j| = Q^{2j}`, `d_j = Q^{j−1}(Q+1)`, and `λ_min(G_j) = Q^{j−1}·λ_min(G₁)` — so `1 + d_j/|λ_min(G_j)| = 1 + (Q+1)/|λ_min(U_Q)|`, the Hoffman floor is exactly unchanged at every level. *The argument:* the norm-one conic is smooth over the residue field (a nonzero polar derivative at every unit), giving `Q` lifts per point and the degree formula. Characters trivial on the last layer factor through `A_{j−1}` and inherit eigenvalue `Q·(previous)`; a character nontrivial on the last layer sums to zero over each "tangent line" coset of the last layer unless the character's linear functional vanishes on that tangent, which happens for at most one (odd characteristic) or exactly one (characteristic two) residue point per functional, so such characters have eigenvalue at most `2Q^{j−1}` (odd) or `Q^{j−1}` (even) in absolute value — below `Q^{j−1}λ_min(G₁)` in every case since `λ_min(G₁) ≤ −2` (odd, a 4-cycle) or `≤ −1` (even, an edge). Induction on inherited characters and attainment at a character inherited from `G₁`'s own least eigenspace closes the theorem.
grade: proof, GPT Astra, 2026-09-16, verified here by recomputation; partly prior art
verdict: closes (recomputation confirms the formula at every tested level and ring, odd and Galois).
rests_text: row 70's tower consequences — "any exclusion supplied by Hoffman at the residue level survives every inert prime-power level"; row 75's (FS-66) sibling result for the *split-prime* tower, a different mechanism for a different case (G54's classification distinguishes tight-split towers, forced from depth by the fibre-share inequality, from slack-inert towers, invariant by this theorem); the CRT-product finite-list consequence, `{23,27,31,43,47,59,64,67,79,83}` (FS54-T5's product theorem plus this invariance closes it to a finite residue-size list even allowing arbitrary tower levels).

title: What the local–global conjecture gives, once the wall holds
statement: *If* `W` holds (every `U_Q` at the six open targets has `χ ≠ 6`) *and* the local–global conjecture holds (`χ(F²) = L(F)` wherever `L(F) ≤ 6`, bold form `χ(ℝ²) = 7`), *then*: (1) the conjecture's `L ≤ 6` clause shrinks to `L ≤ 5`, a finite rule read off the conjugation-fixed primes with residue `𝔽₃, 𝔽₇, 𝔽₁₁, 𝔽₁₉` or dyadic (ramified, or inert with `N𝔭 ≤ 32`); (2) the bold form gives `χ(F²) ∈ {2,3,4,5,7}` for every real field, and every six-chromatic finite unit-distance graph extends to a seven-chromatic one over any field containing it; (3) **for `F = ℚ(√167)`, once five is refused at 23**: `L(F) = min(χ(Γ₂₃), χ(Γ₄₃), ≥7)`, so the conjecture predicts `χ(ℚ(√167)²) ≥ 6` **whichever way `W` goes** — 6 by clause (1) if `Γ₂₃` or `Γ₄₃` is six-chromatic, 7 by the bold form otherwise — against a proven lower bound of 3.
grade: derived; the FS-54 implementer, 2026-09-16; CONDITIONAL on the wall and the conjecture, not a theorem of either alone
verdict: closes, as a conditional statement — neither hypothesis is claimed.
rests_text: the entire motivation for FS-56/ℚ(√167) (row 71, FS-59); G59's later restatement of the same conditional (dated 2026-09-18, a different milestone).

title: The symmetric-search reduction is complete: prime-order stabiliser classes suffice
statement: For a finite graph `G` with automorphism group `Aut(G)` a finite solvable group: the maximum, over all subgroups `H ≤ Aut(G)` of prime order, of the largest `H`-invariant independent set equals the maximum, over all independent sets with *any* nontrivial stabiliser, of the set's size. *The argument:* by Cauchy's theorem, a nontrivial finite group's stabiliser contains an element of prime order, hence a subgroup of prime order; conjugating the witnessing independent set by an element carrying that subgroup to a fixed class representative moves the set into the representative subgroup's invariant sets without changing its size. So it suffices to search subgroups up to conjugacy, and, restricted to prime order, up to the finitely many conjugacy classes GAP enumerates.
grade: hand; the FS-54 implementer, 2026-09-16
rests_text: row 70's `α(Γ₂₇) ≥ 117` search (all 15 prime-order symmetry classes checked, `data/fs54/symmetric/`); the reading that every found 117-set is 4-rigid.
kernel: declined — no consumer; a general statement about invariant search over a solvable automorphism group, useful as a design principle but not itself consumed by any held or planned Lean development.

title: Every congruence between subsets of a field plane is an isometry of that plane
statement: Let `F ⊆ ℝ` be a subfield, `Y, Y′ ⊂ F²` with `|Y| ≥ 2`, and `φ` a Euclidean isometry with `φ(Y) = Y′`. Then `φ` is `z ↦ uz + t` or `z ↦ u z̄ + t` with `u, t ∈ F(i)` and `u ū = 1`. *The argument:* every isometry of `ℂ` has one of those two forms with `|u| = 1`; picking `y₁ ≠ y₂ ∈ Y` gives `u = (φ(y₂) − φ(y₁))/(y₂ − y₁)` (or the conjugate-denominator form), which lies in `F(i)` because `F(i)` is closed under complex conjugation (`F` real) and under the field operations; `t = φ(y₁) − u y₁` then also lies in `F(i)`, and `u ū = 1` follows from `|u| = 1` together with `u ∈ F(i)`.
grade: hand; the FS-56 implementer, 2026-09-16
rests_text: FS56-T2 (the finiteness and solvability of the isometry group `T` generates); every consequence of the blow-up (row 71's whole content).
kernel: declined — would need `Isom(ℂ)`'s classification plus a field-closure argument; no consumer beyond FS56-T2, itself declined for want of amenability/Følner infrastructure.

title: The geometric fractional blow-up stays inside the field
statement: For every subfield `F ⊆ ℝ`, every finite `H ⊂ F²`, every family `𝒞` of pairs of congruent subsets of `H` (each of size ≥ 2) and every `ε > 0`, there is a finite `G ⊂ F²` with `χ_f(G) ≥ χ_gf(H; 𝒞) − ε`; hence `χ(F²) ≥ ⌈χ_gf(H; 𝒞)⌉`. *The argument:* MRVZ's Theorem 1 verbatim, with three checks specific to keeping the field: (i) the finite set `T` of isometries realising a pair of `𝒞` is, by FS56-T1, a subset of `F(i) ⋊ (U_F ⋊ ⟨conj⟩)` — translations by `F(i)` (abelian, normal) extended by rotations `U_F` (abelian) extended by order 2 — hence solvable, hence amenable, hence has a right Følner sequence `R_m`; (ii) `G_m = ⋃_{σ∈R_m} σH ⊂ F²` since every `σ ∈ Isom(F²)` by (i); (iii) the near-invariance argument bounding `|R_mT∖R_m|` terms each by `χ_f(G_m) ≤ χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7` (row 33) closes by compactness of the weight-≤7 regular fractional colourings of `H`.
grade: hand; the FS-56 implementer, 2026-09-16, transcribing MatolcsiEtAl2025 Theorem 1 with the field kept
verdict: closes (re-derived here: each of the three field-specific checks is a direct consequence of FS56-T1 plus standard amenability facts — solvable ⟹ amenable is textbook, and a finite union of translates of a finite congruent set by a Følner sequence of a group acting by isometries is the standard blow-up construction).
rests_text: row 71's whole content — FS56-T3 (`χ_f(K²) = 4`), the CRT-consistency check FS56-T3's corollary, and FS56-T5 below (the "hard limit" cap, which uses the SAME field-internal machinery from the other direction).
kernel: declined — "a formal B2 would need amenability and Følner sequences for countable solvable groups" (`plans/FS56-field-blowup.md` § "Dependencies, stated plainly"), infrastructure not held and not currently planned.

title: `χ_f(K²) = 4`, and the finitary independence ratio of `K²` is exactly 1/4
statement: For `K = ℚ(√3,√11)`: `χ_f(K²) = 4`, and every finite unit-distance graph `G ⊂ K²` has independence ratio `α(G)/|G| ≥ 1/4`, with ratios arbitrarily close to `1/4` attained by finite subgraphs. *The argument:* MRVZ's `G27` (their Definition 2, Moser coefficients in `ℤ⁴`) lies in `K²`; their Theorem 3 gives `χ_gf(G27) = 4` from a computer-verified rational dual witness. By FS56-T2, `χ_f(K²) ≥ sup_G χ_f(G) ≥ 4`. By Theorem B (`chromaticNumber_seamPlane`, kernel), `χ_f(K²) ≤ χ(K²) = 4`. For the independence ratio's other direction: MRVZ's Theorem 2 bounds `χ_f(G) ≤ 1/α₁` where `α₁` is the infimum of independence ratios over finite subgraphs, using an independent set of a large cube in the lattice spanned by `G`'s vertices — a lattice inside `K²` — so the infimum over finite `G ⊂ K²` is exactly `1/4`.
grade: hand + cert; the FS-56 implementer, 2026-09-16, with MatolcsiEtAl2025's witness
rests_text: answers `[CranstonRabern2015]`'s conclusion's first question (`CLOSED-QUESTIONS.md` §1.6); FS56-T5's cap (the same value 4.36 caps `χ_f` from above, so `χ_f(K²) = 4` is between the field-blow-up floor and the additive/residue ceiling); `data/fs56/g27/`.
kernel: declined — no fractional-chromatic-number infrastructure exists in `Proofs/`; Theorem B itself is already kernel.

title: The class-sum certificate's weak duality
statement: Fix a subfield `F ⊆ ℝ`, a finite `H ⊂ F²`, a level `k`. Let `y_Y` be rational weights on sets `Y ⊆ H`, `1 ≤ |Y| ≤ k`, such that (i) every congruence class of listed sets with `|Y| ≥ 2` sums to 0, (ii) the singletons sum to `w`, (iii) every independent set `S` of `H` has `Σ_{Y⊆S} y_Y ≤ 1`. Then `χ_gf(H; k) ≥ w`. *The argument:* for any feasible `γ` (a regular fractional colouring whose aggregate `γ̄` is constant on congruence classes of size-≤k sets, 1 on singletons): `Σ_S γ(S) ≥ Σ_S γ(S) Σ_{Y⊆S} y_Y` by (iii) and `γ ≥ 0`; swapping the finite double sum gives `Σ_Y y_Y γ̄(Y)`, and since `γ̄` is constant on each class this is `Σ_classes γ̄_c Σ_{Y∈c} y_Y`, which by (i)–(ii) equals `w · 1 = w` (only the singleton class survives; every size-≥2 class contributes `γ̄_c · 0`).
grade: hand; the FS-56 implementer, 2026-09-16
rests_text: every CERTIFIED verdict `tools/fs56_gf_check.py` prints (the checker's soundness rests on exactly this lemma); FS56-T3's re-verification of `χ_gf(G27) ≥ 4`.
kernel: declined — no consumer beyond the standard-library checker itself.

title: The hard limit for every fractional route: the cap on `χ_f(F²)`
statement: For a subfield `F ⊆ ℝ`: `χ_f(F²) ≤ min(4.36, χ_f(target) at every usable place of F)`. Consequently a finite `H ⊂ F²` can certify four colours via FS56-T2 only if every usable place of `F` has `χ_f(target) > 3` — which fails exactly at a usable `𝔽₃` residue plane (`χ_f(Γ₃) = 3`) or a dyadic place ramified in `F(i)/F` (`χ_f = 2`). For `ℚ(√167)` the cap is `4.36` (its usable places' `χ_f` are all `≥ χ_f(Γ₂₃) ≈ 5.03`); for `ℚ(√11)` and `ℚ(√23)` the cap is `χ_f(Γ₇) = 49/14 = 3.5` (`α(Γ₇) = 14` exactly) — still above the 3-colour threshold. *The argument:* a residue homomorphism `F² → target` pulls a fractional colouring of the target back to one of `F²` of the same weight, so `χ_f(F²) ≤ χ_f(target)` at every usable place; separately, restricting Croft's measurable colouring of `ℝ²` (`[MatolcsiEtAl2025]` (1)) bounds `χ_f(F²) ≤ χ_f(ℝ²) ≤ 4.36`. A finite `H` with `χ_gf(H;k) > 3` would, by FS56-T2, give `χ_f(F²) > 3`, contradicting any usable-place cap at or below 3.
grade: hand; the FS-56 implementer, 2026-09-16
rests_text: row 71's "the route's cap (3 at `𝔽₃`, 3.5 at `𝔽₇`, 4.36)"; the negative finding that FS-56's own search (Q1, below) could not exceed the cap at small height, consistent with but not implied by this theorem; FS-58's registered side target at `ℚ(√11)`/`ℚ(√23)` (a narrower window, `3 < χ_f ≤ 3.5`, than `ℚ(√167)`'s `3 < χ_f ≤ 4.36`).

title: `[DuczVarga2026]`'s augmentation must leave `K`
statement: `[DuczVarga2026]`'s `G29 = G27 ∪ {p, q}` has `χ_gf(G29) > 4.0007`; by FS56-T2, no field containing `G29` can have a four-colourable plane. `G29`'s two new points involve `√5` and `η = i√((415 + 79√33)/8)`, both outside `K = ℚ(√3,√11)` — consistent with Theorem B (`χ(K²) = 4`), and corrects `BIBLIOGRAPHY.md`'s prior row, which had said the augmentation stays "inside the Moser lattice".

title: The checker's soundness obligations: congruence grouping, branch-and-bound exhaustiveness, multiquadratic arithmetic
statement: `tools/fs56_gf_check.py`'s three non-trivial internal obligations each hold: (a) **grouping is sound** — the equal-orientation map test `(z′−a)(y₂−y₁) = (z−y₁)(b−a)` (rotation) or its conjugate form (reflection) decides congruence exactly, because it is equivalent to the existence of `u ∈ F(i)`, `uū=1`, with `z′ = uz + t` on every point of `Y`, which by FS56-T1 is exactly when `Y, Y′` are congruent; (b) **branch-and-bound is exhaustive** — including or excluding each vertex in turn, with the bound "current value plus the positive weights of sets meeting only undecided vertices" an upper bound on every completion, never prunes a feasible optimum; (c) **the multiquadratic arithmetic is sound** — square roots of distinct squarefree pairwise-coprime integers are `ℚ`-linearly independent (Besicovitch), so equality of the integer-vector representation is equality in `F`, and `√a·√b = (∏_{shared primes} d)·√(∏_{symmetric-difference primes})` for coprime squarefree radicands correctly reduces products back into the same basis.
grade: hand + tools; the FS-56 implementer, 2026-09-16
verdict: closes (three short, checkable arguments; each has a negative control recorded and, per `plans/FS56-quadratic-167.md` §D, run — the checker's `--self-test` exercises all three).
rests_text: every CERTIFIED verdict of `tools/fs56_gf_check.py`, hence FS56-T3's re-verification and every future certificate this checker validates (including any future Q1 landing).
kernel: declined — a standard-library Python checker's correctness proof, not a target for formalisation; no stub plans one.

title: The split 3-adic tower is Hoffman-tight at three colours at every level, with the level-1 characters as the unique minimisers
statement: Let `S_m = Cay((O/3^m)², C_m)`, `O = ℤ₃[i]`, `|C_m| = 8·9^{m−1}` (the unit circle over `ℚ(√d)`'s completion at the inert prime 3, `d ≡ 2 (mod 3)`, at level `m`). Its eigenvalues are character means `E_t ψ(αt + β/t)` over `t ∈ (O/3^m)^×`. At level 1 the least is `−4 = −d(S_1)/2` (the eight-point Kloosterman sums; the ratio bound is exactly tight, `81/3`). For `m ≥ 2`, every character primitive at level `m` (not a pullback from level `m−1`) has mean at most `(9/4)·9^{−m/2}` — strictly above `−1/2` — so `S_m`'s least eigenvalue equals `S_1`'s scaled by the covering degree, attained only by the 16 characters pulled back from level 1.
grade: hand
verdict: closes for the hand estimate (i)–(ii); the general-level bound is a standard-technique estimate whose own prior art is unread (see *Prior art* below), not a gap in the argument as stated.
rests_text: FS58-T2 (the pullback conclusion); D3.3's tower screen (no finite level of the tower rules out a chain target `3u`).
kernel: declined — no consumer this milestone names beyond the tools-side chain search; the generalisation to arbitrary level is a hand estimate, not carried into `ThreeAdicBarrier.lean`.

title: Every proper 3-colouring of every level of the split 3-adic tower is pulled back from level 1, hence affine
statement: By FS58-T1's tightness and G54's Theorem D2-A (`FS38-D2-A`: a Hoffman-tight `k`-colouring is balanced, gap-free, and its Fourier support lies on the minimising eigenspace), every proper 3-colouring of `S_m` (any `m`) is pulled back from `S_1`. `S_1`'s eight proper 3-colourings (origin pinned to 0, one neighbour to 1) are, by exhaustive solver enumeration, each affine (`x ↦ σ(L(x))` for an `𝔽₃`-linear form `L`) — **[tools, verified for `m ≤ 3`]** — so every 3-colouring at any level of the tower is affine. (A short supporting fact used implicitly: since `Hom(O_{(3)}², ℤ/3) = Hom((O/3)², ℤ/3)`, every *additive* 3-colouring of the whole 3-integral lattice is automatically a pullback from level 1 too — D3.6.)
grade: derived (row 72's Theorem-A framework; FS38-D2-A); tools confirms level 1's colourings are exhaustively affine
verdict: closes — for the "pulled back from `S_1`" half (FS58-T1 + FS38-D2-A); the "hence affine" half is a *tools*-grade fact about `S_1` specifically (exhaustive at `m ≤ 3` only, not a hand proof that `S_1`'s 3-colourings are affine from its Fourier support).
rests_text: `plans/FS58-four-colours.md` R-B1's empirical confirmation over `ℚ(√11)` (399 of 427 quotients refuse three colours; the 21 that accept admit exactly one linear form up to sign), which is this theorem's consequence realised on the field's actual direction pools — the route-C screen (D3.7, FS58-T6) is therefore structurally blind on 3-integral pools, which is exactly what R-B1 found and P1 (0.8 confidence) lost against.
kernel: declined — `FS38-D2-A`'s own kernel status governs; no separate target.

title: Periodic 3-colourings of the 3-integral graph factor through a tensor product of the 3-adic tower and the stable residue planes
statement: Let `F = ℚ(√d)`, `d ≡ 2 (mod 3)` squarefree, `G₃` the unit-distance graph on 3-integral unit vectors of `F²`, `S` the 3-integral unit circle, `Λ₃ = ℤ[S]` the group it generates. Every periodic 3-colouring of `G₃` factors through a finite quotient of `Λ₃`, and `S` surjects onto `C_m × Π_𝔮 C_𝔮` (weak approximation on the conic, over the 3-adic levels `C_m` and the conjugation-stable primes `𝔮` of `F(i)`), so every such finite quotient graph is a **tensor product** `S_m × Π_𝔮 P_𝔮` of a level of the 3-adic tower and levels of the stable residue planes.
grade: hand; corrected 2026-09-17 from an erroneous first version
verdict: closes for the factorisation and the surjectivity (the group-theoretic claim). **It does NOT close for the further claim this theorem is used to support** — that every 3-colouring of such a tensor product is itself pulled back from one factor (needed to conclude every periodic 3-colouring of `G₃` is affine): the text explicitly marks this "not derived", a multiplicativity-type property of `K₃`-colourings of a product graph whose prior art (Häggkvist–Hell–Miller–Neumann-Lara 1988; Greenwell–Lovász 1974, for `K_n` factors) is unread. §0 O7's measurement (`q = 7, 11, 19, 23`: every 3-colouring of `S₁ × P_q` found is pulled back from `S₁`, with the `q = 3` positive control separating at once) is evidence for this further claim, not a proof of it — filed as a measurement in § "Readings and measurements", with **FS-67** as the open general theorem it is an instance-hunt for.
rests_text: row 73's "every periodic 3-colouring of the 3-integral pools tried is affine" rests on FS58-T2 (the tower alone) plus this unclosed multiplicativity claim wherever a stable residue factor is present — the affine conclusion is therefore proven only where the tensor factor is trivial (pure 3-adic tower) and measured (not proven) wherever a residue-plane factor is mixed in.
kernel: declined — the open half (FS-67) is what would need a kernel target, not this factorisation lemma. *[Correction at FS-89's close, 2026-09-25, from the products reader (`plans/PA-products-GL1974-LT2002.md` §3–§4): Greenwell–Lovász 1974 is now read in full, so "unread" is stale for it (Häggkvist–Hell–Miller–Neumann-Lara 1988 stays unread). It does not reach the claim here: its Theorem 1 settles `K_n × G` for connected gap-free `G`, hence FS-67 for tight factors `K_k^s` (among them `UD(𝔽₃, 2) ≅ K₃ × K₃`), but `S₁` (81 vertices, degree 8) is no direct power of `K₃` (`K₃⁴` has degree 16).]*

title: The finite/infinite forcing dichotomy, by compactness
statement: For the countably infinite graph `G₃` (3-integral unit vectors of `F²`) with an exhausting chain of finite subgraphs: a difference `δ` is forced equal at three colours by *some* finite subgraph of `G₃` if and only if no proper 3-colouring of the whole of `G₃` separates the pair — i.e. a finite forcer exists iff `G₃` itself is rigid at `δ`.
grade: hand
verdict: closes (a routine compactness argument in the style of de Bruijn–Erdős, over a countable graph — no ultrafilter or choice needed beyond König's lemma).
rests_text: the phase B/C decision procedure (§3): "no finite forcer at this direction pool" is read directly off a quotient colouring of the infinite graph (D3.7, FS58-T6), never from an exhaustive finite search; the open status of `ℚ(√167)` (FS-59) is stated in exactly this vocabulary ("is `G₃` rigid?").
kernel: **in the kernel at every colour count** (FS-73, `Proofs/HadwigerNelson/Kempe.lean`): `forces_iff_exists_finite` — a pair is forced iff some finite induced subgraph forces it — over `exists_coloring_ne_of_forall_finset`, which is Mathlib's `Finset.rado_selection` (de Bruijn–Erdős); Mathlib also holds `SimpleGraph.nonempty_hom_of_forall_finite_subgraph_hom`, the subgraph form. FS-39's phase A can cite the same two lemmas.

title: The direction-set quotient screen
statement: Let `W₀` be a finite symmetric set of unit vectors, `Λ₀ = ℤ[W₀]`, `L ≤ Λ₀` a finite-index subgroup with `W₀ ∩ L = ∅`. If the finite quotient Cayley graph `Cay(Λ₀/L, W₀ mod L)` admits a proper 3-colouring `c̄` with `c̄(0̄) ≠ c̄(\overline{3u})`, then no unit-distance graph whose edge vectors all lie in `W₀` forces the pair `(p, p + 3u)` equal at three colours, for any `p ∈ Λ₀`: the pullback `x ↦ c̄(x̄ − p̄)` is proper on `Cay(Λ₀, W₀)` and separates every translate.
grade: hand
verdict: closes. *Controls, both reachable (exercised in phase B1):* on `L = 3Λ₀` (the 3-adic quotient) no separation exists, matching FS58-T2 (an affine colouring never separates `3u`); on an `L` where `3u ≡ w ∈ W₀`, the pair is literally an edge, so every proper colouring separates it.
rests_text: R-B1's null over `ℚ(√11)` (0 of 427 lattice records kill the pool — a structural consequence of FS58-T2, not this screen's own limitation); phase B's design (`tools/fs58_chain.py screen`).
kernel: declined — a boundary-free SAT screening tool, no kernel consumer named.

title: A distance-2 virtual edge chains into a forced pair at `3u`
statement: If a finite 3-integral graph over `F` separates `x` from `x + 2u` in every 3-colouring (a virtual edge at `2u`), then any graph containing it plus the four-point run `x, x+u, x+2u, x+3u` (and its translate by `u`) forces `x` and `x+3u` equal at three colours.
grade: hand, three lines
rests_text: reframes the search target as a Moser-spindle-shaped question (a 4-chromatic `{1,2}`-graph with one distance-2 edge over `F`) rather than a direct `3u`-forcing question — the more geometric target D3 recommends; not pursued as a separate route in this milestone (superseded by the direct `ℚ(√11)` forcer, R-B2/B3).

title: The pigeonhole-forcing lemma, generalised from Wormald
statement: For a finite `T ⊂ F²`, call `U ⊆ T` **odd** when the unit-distance graph on `⋃_{u ∈ U} S(u, 1) ∩ F²` contains an odd cycle. If `T` admits no 3-colouring that is proper on `T`'s own unit edges and leaves no odd subset `U ⊆ T` monochromatic, then `χ(F²) ≥ 4`, witnessed by `T`, one odd cycle per odd subset used, and one edge from each cycle vertex to a point of its subset.
grade: hand
rests_text: route W (§0 O6, phase W), which found no independent odd subset of size 3–5 at the heights tried over `ℚ(√11)` or `ℚ(√167)` — closed as a route (§C, "not the reason if χ ≥ 4 is true"), the lemma itself is not refuted, only unfired at this height.

title: `χ(ℚ(√d)²) ≥ 4` certified for `d = 23, 47, 71, 95, 191`
statement: For each `d ∈ {23, 47, 71, 95, 191}`, an explicit finite unit-distance graph over `ℚ(√d)` (297/670 points/edges at `d=23`, 169/385 at 47, 148/346 at 71, 1068/3096 at 95, 483/1203 at 191 — the 95 witness not 1-minimal) has no proper 3-colouring, certified by `tools/fs58_check_witness.py` (standard library, rebuilds every edge in exact rational arithmetic, checks the LRAT proof with an independent RUP checker, refuses twelve planted faults each for its named reason and refuses the same files under the wrong radicand) and by a decorrelated recheck sharing no code with the generator or the checker (all edges re-derived in exact rational arithmetic; Minisat22 and Lingeling — two further solver codebases — refusing three colours; a verified 4-colouring on deletion). So `χ(ℚ(√d)²) ≥ 4` at each; combined with the residue plane at 7 (`[Moorhouse2010]` Cor. 8.3 / `[Fischer1990]`) this gives `χ(ℚ(√d)²) = 4` exactly at `d = 23, 71, 95, 191` and `4 ≤ χ(ℚ(√47)²) ≤ 5` (the plane at 11 gives the upper bound 5, since 47 has no usable plane at 7).

title: No rational diamond chord over `ℚ(√d)`, `d ≡ 7 (mod 8)`, is a 2-adic unit
statement: A *diamond* is a unit rhombus `0, v, v̄, v + v̄` on a unit vector `v = x + iy`, `x, y ∈ ℚ(√d)`, `v ∉ ℚ(i)`; its long chord `v + v̄ = 2x` is rational iff `x ∈ ℚ`, and then `y = s√d` with `s ∈ ℚ` and `x² + d s² = 1`. Writing `x = a/m`, `s = b/m` with `gcd(a, b, m) = 1`, `a² + d b² = m²`. For `d ≡ 7 (mod 8)` the residues mod 8 leave two cases: `m` odd, whence `a` odd and `4 ∣ b`; or `4 ∣ m`, whence `a` and `b` odd (`m ≡ 2 (mod 4)` is impossible — this is row 74's dyadic lemma in chord form). So the chord `2x = 2a/m` has 2-adic valuation `+1` (first case) or `≤ −1` (second), **never 0**: no rational diamond chord is a 2-adic unit. Over `d ≡ 3 (mod 8)` one can be — `ℚ(√11)`'s `v = (−5 + i√11)/6` has `m = 6 ≡ 2 (mod 4)` and chord `−5/3`, the unit that closes the chain `1/3 = 1 + 1 + v + v̄` behind row 73's forcer. *"Odd parity" in the source means exactly "a 2-adic unit" (odd numerator and odd denominator in lowest terms).*
grade: hand; stated in one sentence by the FS-58 implementer ("no diamond chord is a rational vector of odd parity"); re-derived and sharpened by the owner, 2026-09-22
rests_text: the *reading* — not filed as a theorem — that `ℚ(√11)`'s "diamond plus three rational steps" mechanism cannot transfer to any `d ≡ 7 (mod 8)` field, which is why `ℚ(√23)`'s route used a saturated 3-non-integral lattice (R-B5) and why `ℚ(√167)` is not landed by the direct route; whether the mechanism *needs* a unit chord is that reading's content.
kernel: declined — a corollary of FS61's dyadic lemma, whose kernel decision it follows.

title: Eight new certified lower bounds for real quadratic planes, five of them exact values
statement: For `d ∈ {59, 119, 239, 359, 431}`, `χ(ℚ(√d)²) = 4` (the lower bound is this milestone's; the upper bound `≤ 4` is prior art — the dyadic bound `[Fischer1990]` Thm 10(i) at `d = 59` (`d ≡ 3 mod 8`), the residue plane at 7, `[Moorhouse2010]` Thm 8.1, at `d = 119, 239, 359, 431` (`d ≡ 7 mod 8`, `L = 4`)); for `d ∈ {143, 311, 335}`, `4 ≤ χ(ℚ(√d)²) ≤ 5` (the lower bound is this milestone's; the upper bound `≤ 5` is prior art via the residue plane at 11, since `L(ℚ(√d)) = 5` at these three). Each lower bound is witnessed by a finite unit-distance graph (`data/fs61/witness-<d>/witness.json`, sizes 456–2,360 points, 1,122–6,639 edges) certified `CERTIFIED` by a standard-library-only checker sharing no code with the generator, which (i) re-derives every unit-distance edge from the coordinates in exact integer arithmetic and refuses unless it equals the file's edge list, (ii) checks a pinned edge is real, (iii) rebuilds the CNF from its own edge set and replays an LRAT refutation of 3-colourability, (iv) is refused when asked about the wrong radicand, (v) passes twelve planted-fault controls each refused for its own named reason, (vi) is independently re-derived in exact `Fraction` arithmetic against three solvers outside the generator's own, and (vii) carries an explicit proper 4-colouring verified on every edge (so each graph is exactly 4-chromatic). title: The dyadic law's other half: no primitive unit vector of `ℚ(√d)²` has denominator `≡ 2 (mod 4)` when `d ≡ 7 (mod 8)`

title: Cross-field non-transfer: an integral shape's unit vectors over two distinct fields share only the rational ones
statement: Fix a rank-4 integral shape `Λ ⊆ ℤ⁴` (a sublattice, in coordinates `(a,b,c,e)` standing for `((a+b√d)/M, (c+e√d)/M)` at a fixed common denominator `M`). For squarefree `d`, let `W_d = {(a,b,c,e) ∈ Λ : a²+c²+d(b²+e²) = M², ab+ce = 0}` be `Λ`'s unit vectors over `ℚ(√d)`. For distinct squarefree `d ≠ d′`: `W_d ∩ W_{d′} = {(a,b,c,e) ∈ Λ : b = e = 0, a² + c² = M², ac = 0}` — exactly the *rational* unit vectors of `Λ` (those independent of `d`), whichever two distinct `d, d′` are chosen.
grade: hand; the FS-61 implementer, stated as the mechanism behind `tools/fs61_owner_shape_iso.py`'s search

title: The four census same-generator-count shape pairs admit no linear lattice automorphism carrying one field's unit vectors onto the other's
statement: For the four pairs of (shape, field, field) found in the census with equal unit-vector counts on both sides — `L8a8b1603` (`d=95` vs `d=119`, 28 = 28), `Lb0a7206c` (`d=23` vs `d=191`, 36 = 36), `L54356af8` (`d=95` vs `d=191`, 52 = 52), `L3e1c94c6` (`d=239` vs `d=359`, 52 = 52) — there is no `T ∈ GL_4(ℤ)` fixing the shared lattice `Λ` with `T(W_{d_1}) = W_{d_2}`. **Method, cheapest first:** for the first three pairs, the odd girths of the two fields' graphs on `Λ` already disagree (7 vs 5, 9 vs 5, 7 vs 5), and odd girth is preserved by any graph isomorphism, so no such `T` (which by FS61-T3's converse would BE a graph isomorphism `Cay(Λ, W_{d_1}) → Cay(Λ, W_{d_2})`) can exist — no search needed. For the fourth pair (`d=239` vs `d=359`), where the odd girths agree (7 = 7), an exhaustive exact search over `T ∈ GL_4(ℚ) ∩ \text{End}(Λ)` (Gaussian elimination in `Fraction` arithmetic, pruned level by level along a greedy basis of `W_{239}`) found **0** valid maps `T(W_{239}) = W_{359}`, against a **positive control** — the identical search run with `d_1 = d_2 = 359` on its own 52 unit vectors — which correctly recovers **16** linear self-automorphisms (the group of `Λ`'s own symmetries fixing `W_{359}` setwise).

title: The disc-overlap fraction, and the bidisc degree-prediction formula built from it
statement: (a) **Exact geometric fact.** For `R > 1/2` let `φ(R) = [2R²·arccos(1/(2R)) − (1/2)·√(4R²−1)] / (πR²)`. Then `φ(R)` equals the fraction of the area of a disc of radius `R` that is covered by that disc's own translate by any vector of length 1 (equivalently: the area of intersection of two radius-`R` discs whose centres are distance 1 apart, divided by `πR²`) — the standard circle–circle intersection ("lens") area, `2R²·cos⁻¹(d/2R) − (d/2)√(4R²−d²)`, evaluated at separation `d = 1` and normalised by one disc's area `πR²`; `φ(R) = 0` for `R ≤ 1/2` (the discs are disjoint) and `φ(R) → 1 − 1/(πR)` as `R → ∞`. This is elementary, standard plane geometry (the two-circular-segment decomposition of the lens), reproduced here because it is nowhere else derived in this project's files, only asserted. (b) **The degree-prediction heuristic**, which uses (a) but is not itself a theorem: a rank-4 lattice `Λ` over a real quadratic field, holding `g` unit vectors of a fixed class set, has a ball `B_R` (points of `Λ` within radius `R` of the origin under BOTH real embeddings — a "bidisc" region, since `ℚ(√d)²` has two real places). Each point of `B_R` has `g` candidate unit-vector neighbours; if a candidate's landing inside `B_R` under each embedding independently has probability `φ(R)` (translating a disc by a unit vector covers a `φ(R)`-fraction of it, in each embedding separately, by (a)), the predicted fraction landing in `B_R` under both is `φ(R)²`, giving predicted average degree `g·φ(R)²`. The independence assumption is NOT proven — the two embeddings' offsets need not be independent for a specific finite set of lattice points — and the formula is accordingly a heuristic, not an identity: its accuracy is a *measurement* (observed/predicted ratio has median 1.0000 and range 0.715–1.184 over 775 asked balls across the census's 40 fields plus 7 controls, 0 outside ±30%; the un-squared alternative `g·φ(R)` reads median 0.584 on a 60-ball sample, the planted control that shows the square is load-bearing).
grade: hand; the FS-61 implementer, credited in the tool's own comment as "the owner's addition" (`tools/fs61_census.py` line 3296)
verdict: closes for (a); (b) is explicitly NOT filed as a theorem (see this file's "Readings and measurements" section) — its accuracy is measured, not proven, per this audit's kind-before-grade rule (`CLAUDE.md` G65 is graded `[measured]` for exactly this reason).

title: Three mechanism theorems constrain the colour count of every structured colouring this project builds, and 6 is excluded by all three
statement: Every *structured* colouring this project has ever produced constrains its colour count to a specific number-theoretic form: **(i)** a residue colouring (Theorem A) colours by the size of a residue field, hence a **prime power**; **(ii)** a coset colouring of the triangular lattice by a rotation-stable sublattice colours by the index of an ideal of the Eisenstein integers, hence a **Loeschian number** (`a² + ab + b²`); **(iii)** the same construction on the square lattice colours by the index of an ideal of the Gaussian integers, hence a **sum of two squares**. **6 is the smallest positive integer that is none of the three**, for three independent number-theoretic reasons: it is not a prime power (2·3); in the Eisenstein integers, 2 is inert and 3 ramifies, so no ideal has index 6; in the Gaussian integers, 2 ramifies and 3 (≡ 3 mod 4) is inert, so likewise no ideal has index 6.
grade: derived
verdict: closes for each of the three named mechanisms as a mathematical fact (classical algebraic number theory: ideal norms in `ℤ[i]` are exactly the sums of two squares by unique factorisation and the splitting of rational primes; ideal norms in the Eisenstein integers are exactly the Loeschian numbers by the analogous factorisation; a residue field's size is a prime power by definition) — the specific claim that a *coset* colouring's colour count is always such a norm is this project's own recognition (row 34, G62), not independently re-derived here beyond citing the classical fact.
rests_text: the norm reading (below, explicitly **not** a theorem); row 34's "2, 5, 6 are not `a² + ab + b²`" observation, of which this is the completed three-mechanism form.

title: The independence-number normalisation and the six-colour threshold
statement: Write `c(q) = α(UD(𝔽_q,2)) / q^{3/2}`. Since these graphs are vertex-transitive, `χ_f = q²/α = √q/c`, and `χ ≥ ⌈χ_f⌉`, so a plane needs six colours only if `c(q) ≲ √q/6` — **a threshold that grows with `q`**, against an observed maximum near a constant (0.756 to 0.918 across `q = 7, 11, 19` at the time of writing). The threshold crosses the observed maximum (0.92) at `q ≈ 30.5`.
grade: derived

title: No uniform bound `c(q) ≤ C` with `C < 0.799` can close the window member at `q = 23`

Since excluding six at `q = 23` by such a uniform bound needs `C < 0.799` (23's own threshold, from `FS62-T5` with `q = 23`: `√23/6 ≈ 0.799`, refined to the exact fractional form `529/6/23^{3/2} = 0.799` in the source), **no uniform bound of this shape can close 23**.

title: Theorem E: equal-characteristic towers are impotent
statement: Let `A` be a local ring with maximal ideal `𝔪` and residue field `𝔽_q` (any `q`), containing a subring mapping isomorphically onto `𝔽_q` (e.g. `𝔽_q[[t]]/t^k`). Then for every `k`, `UD(A/𝔪^k, 2)` and `UD(𝔽_q, 2)` are homomorphically equivalent, so `χ`, `χ_f` and the independence ratio are constant up the tower — (C-α), (C-χ), (C-m) all hold. **Corollary:** if `O` is the ring of integers of a finite extension of `ℚ_p` with ramification index `e ≥ 2` and residue field `𝔽_q`, then `O/π^k ≅ 𝔽_q[ε]/ε^k` for `k ≤ e`, so the first `e` levels of the tower at a ramified place are impotent.

title: The spectrum above level one is small
statement: Fix `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` and `k ≥ 2`. Let `G_k = Cay((ℤ/p^k)², S_k)`, `S_k = {(a,b) : a²+b² ≡ 1 (mod p^k)}`. Every eigenvalue of `G_k`'s adjacency operator, restricted to the orthogonal complement of the functions constant on the fibres of the reduction map `G_k → G_1`, has absolute value at most `2p^{k-1}` (against degree `p^{k-1}(p+1)`).
