title: The fibre-density inequality
statement: Let `I` be an independent set of `G_k`, `k ≥ 2`, and `φ(x) ∈ [0,1]` the share of the fibre over `x ∈ V(G₁)` that `I` occupies. Then `φ` satisfies `⟨φ, A₁φ⟩ ≤ 2·Σ_x φ(x)(1-φ(x))`, and `|I| = p^{2(k-1)}·Σφ`.

title: Symmetrised moments of a feasible fibre-share vector obey the box and localiser inequalities
statement: Let `Γ` be the group generated by the translations of `V = 𝔽_p²` and by every bijection `h` with `h(x+s) - h(x) ∈ S` for all `x, s ∈ S` (a property closed under composition and inverse, so `Γ`'s closure need never be verified — only that each generator has it). For a feasible `φ ∈ [0,1]^V` with `q(φ) ≥ 0` (`q(φ) := 2Σφ(1-φ) - ⟨φ,A₁φ⟩`, FS66-L2's inequality), define the symmetrised moment `ȳ(m) = |Γ|⁻¹ Σ_{γ∈Γ} Π_{x∈m} φ(γx)` for a monomial `m` (a multiset of points of `V`, degree ≤ 4). Then: `ȳ([]) = 1`; `n·ȳ([0]) = Σφ`; `ȳ(γm) = ȳ(m)`; `ȳ(m) ≥ 0` and `ȳ(m∖x) - ȳ(m) ≥ 0`; for positive semidefinite `𝒵` indexed by monomials, `Σ 𝒵_{ij}ȳ(m_i m_j) ≥ 0`; and with `Q(m)` the linear form "the moment of `q` times `m`" written from `q`'s definition, `Σ 𝒵_{ij}Q(m_i m_j)(ȳ) = q(φ)·Σ 𝒵_{ij}ȳ(m_i m_j) ≥ 0`.
grade:

FS-66 phase-2 planner

title: Positive definiteness by fraction-free elimination (Sylvester + Bareiss)
statement: A symmetric integer matrix `R` all of whose leading principal minors are positive is positive definite, and walking fraction-free (Bareiss) elimination without pivoting — where the `k`-th pivot *is* the `k`-th leading principal minor and every division is exact — is exactly that test, performed in integers with no rounding.

title: From the bound to the colours
statement: If `Σφ ≤ U` for every `φ ∈ [0,1]^V` with `q(φ) ≥ 0` (FS66-L4), then `α(G_k) ≤ U·p^{2(k-1)}` for every `k ≥ 1` (FS66-L2); and if `m·U < p²`, no `G_k` is `m`-colourable at any level `k`, and `χ_f(G_k) ≥ p²/U` (vertex-transitivity).

title: Lemma T: twist-blindness

statement: Let `G` be a graph, `q(φ) = 2Σφ(1-φ) - ⟨φ,Aφ⟩` (the bare form, constant `c = 2`), `J` a maximum independent set (size `α`) with an outside vertex `v` having exactly one neighbour in `J`. title: Lemma W: the weighted form of the tower-never-rises conjecture is false at every prime
statement: Let `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, and let `I = {(a,b) ∈ ℤ/p² : b ≡ 0 (mod p), a` even as an integer in `[0, p²-3]}`. Then `I` is independent in `G₂ = UD(ℤ/p², 2)`, its fibre shares `φ_I` are supported on the level-one line `ℓ = \{(j,0)\}` (an induced `p`-cycle of `G₁`), and `Σ_ℓ φ_I = (p²-1)/(2p) > (p-1)/2 = α(G₁[ℓ])`. Consequently `φ_I ∉ STAB(G₁)` (the stable-set polytope) and `max_I w·φ_I > α_w(G₁)` for `w = 1_ℓ`: **the fibre shares of a level-two independent set need not lie in level one's stable-set polytope, so no pointwise or local transfer argument can prove the unweighted conjecture (C-α) — any proof must be global.**

title: The periodic Kempe screen
statement: Let `c` be a proper four-colouring of `Cay(Λ/NΛ, U mod N)` (`U` the complete unit-vector set, `N` admissible), `C` its pull-back, `a = C(0)`, `b ≠ a`. Let `Q` be the quotient's two-colour subgraph (classes coloured `a` or `b`; one edge per `(ȳ, s)`, `s ∈ U`, carrying the voltage `s`), `Q₀` the component of `0̄`, `p(x̄)` the voltage of a spanning-tree walk `0̄ → x̄`, `V` the ℤ-span of the fundamental-cycle voltages `p(ȳ) + s − p(ȳ + s̄)`. Then the `(a, b)`-Kempe component `K₀` of the origin **in the infinite lattice graph** satisfies `K₀ ∩ (class x̄) = p(x̄) + V`, so **`δ ∈ K₀ ⟺ δ̄ ∈ Q₀ ∧ δ − p(δ̄) ∈ V`**. Corollaries: **(T10.1)** if `δ ∉ K₀` for some `b`, the swap `a ↔ b` on `K₀` is a proper four-colouring of every graph on `Λ` separating `(0, δ)`, so `¬ Forces` at `δ` on `Λ` at every radius; **(T10.2)** `V ⊆ NΛ`, and `[NΛ : V]` is the deciding invariant (81 on the rank-6 L3 at N = 2); **(T10.3)** the `Q₀` conjunct is redundant where the `V` test passes (`δ ∈ V ⟹ δ̄ = 0̄`); **(T10.4)** `c(δ̄) ≠ c(0̄)` separates outright; **(T10.5)** `c(δ̄) = c(0̄)` refutes `Separated` at `δ` on every graph on `Λ` — one periodic colouring kills one of the two compulsions at every target; **(T10.6)** with `U` a generator set only, the escape is sound for graphs whose edges lie in `U`. T2 is the additive case (`V = R_b`); phase 1d's fan gap (T6) is the case `Q₀ = {0̄}`.

statement: `Λ₁₀ = 5Λ₅₀`, so `F ⊇ 15Λ₅₀` by monotonicity, every colouring is `15Λ₅₀`-periodic, and the loop at `N = 15` (50,625 classes) returns `P₁₅ = 3Λ₅₀`.

title: The fixed-prime gap lemma, and its scope
statement: If a prime `𝔓` of a CM field `E` is fixed by complex conjugation and its residue target `Cay(O_E/𝔓, circle)` has a gapped `k`-colouring, every lattice of `E` generated by unit vectors is loose at `k`: `F = P = 0`. **Scope:** it reaches only lattices inside a CM field that has such a prime; `ℚ(√3,√5,i)` has none (its primes above 2, 3, 5 are swapped by conjugation, and a fixed odd unramified prime needs residue field 𝔽_p with `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` and 3, 5 squares — `p = 11, 59, …`, targets at least 5-chromatic), so it reaches no lattice spanning that field.
grade: hand; B; scope F
rests_text: every loose verdict in the table; T15; the owner's P4 brief was wrong to cite it for rank 6.
kernel: stub-worthy with FS70-T6's composition (the kernel already holds both halves).

title: At five colours the circle targets at `q = 3, 5, 7, 11, 19` have gapped colourings, and 25 of the 28 quartic CM subfields of K(√7)(i) are loose
statement: Each gapped colouring of `Cay(𝔽_{q²}, μ_{q+1})` is verified from the colouring (13 and 17 ran to 300 s, UNKNOWN, and decide no subfield); the survivors `ℚ(√3,√−77)`, `ℚ(√7,√−33)`, `ℚ(√11,√−21)` have only ramified fixed primes up to 23 or are inert at 23, where Γ₂₃ refuses five; the pilot `ℚ(√3,√−77)` is loose anyway, by a gapped colouring at `N = 7`.
grade: tools + derived; B

At 43 (up to 6 pairs) the smallest refusing sets have 5 pairs, and every colourable set is gapped.

title: The height lift and the slope fibre
statement: Every proper 3-colouring `c` lifts to a height `h : ℤⁿ → ℤ` with steps `±1`, `h ≡ c∘π (mod 3)`, and a winding homomorphism `w : R → 3ℤ` with `|w(ρ)| ≤ ‖ρ‖₁`; the slope fibre `A(c) = {a ∈ [−1,1]ⁿ : a·ρ = w(ρ) on R}` is a nonempty rational polytope.
grade: hand; de Bruijn (L1–L2) and Coxeter (Lemmas 1–3), independently; second route to L2 Poros's

title: The three-colour criterion: `Cay(Λ, S)` is 3-colourable iff some `θ ∈ Hom(Λ, ℝ)` has `‖θ(s)‖_{ℝ/ℤ} ≥ 1/3` on every generator, iff it has a periodic 3-colouring
statement: (⟸) `⌊3{θ(x) + β}⌋` is proper (and periodic for rational `θ`); (⟹) T21's fibre maps onto a cell of `Θ₃ = {θ : θ(s) ∈ [1/3, 2/3] + ℤ}`, a finite union of rational polytopes, which has a rational vertex. The same proof gives `Cay(Λ, S) → C_{2l+1}` iff some `θ` has `θ(S) ⊆ [l, l+1]/(2l+1)`.
grade: hand; de Bruijn (T0) and Coxeter (H-i), independently
rests_text: C3-aper at three colours for the whole class, answering `[AbrishamiEtAl2025]` Problem 4.6 at `χ = 3` for these graphs; the `Θ` certificate (T26); ℚ(√167)'s survivors (T25, R9). Consistency check: `[FourUnitVectors2025]` Thm 1.2 falls out in one line (Coxeter §3).

title: Tight directions are affine; if every point of `Θ₃` has order 3, every 3-colouring is affine and `F = P`
statement: A generator on which every slope of the fibre is `±1` is tight: some relation `σ` has `w(σ) = ‖σ‖₁` (LP duality; **Stiemke's** alternative in de Bruijn's form, Poros's correction), so every monotone path along `σ` steps `+1` and `c(x + t) − c(x)` is constant. If the fibre is a point at a cube vertex, every step is frozen, `c = φ + const` with `φ : Λ → 𝔽₃` additive, and `F = P = ⋂ ker φ ⊇ 3Λ`.
grade: hand; de Bruijn (T1) and Coxeter (H-ii with its rigidity corollary), independently
rests_text: T25; the rigidity dichotomy (T24).

title: Periodic 3-colourings are dense; so `P = F` (C3-inherit) and C3-aper hold at three colours for every such Cayley graph, and `F` has finite index iff every cell of `Θ₃` is a point
statement: For every 3-colouring `c` and finite `B`, a McShane-type extension `ĥ(m) = min_{β ∈ B̃, ℓ ∈ L} [h(β) + a*·ℓ + ‖m − β − ℓ‖₁]` with `a*` rational in the relative interior of `A(c)` and `L = R + Nℤⁿ` gives an `NΛ`-periodic colouring agreeing with `c` on `B`, for `N` even, a multiple of `6·den(a*)`, **and a multiple of the exponent of the torsion of `ℤ^F/pr_F(R)`** — the choice that kills de Bruijn's unsaturated-frozen residual case (his dB-T2's `sat(Λ_J) ∖ Λ_J`), since `NΛ ∩ sat(Λ_T) ⊆ Λ_T`. H-iv: points ⟹ finitely many colourings; a fat cell's rational interior points are distinct invariants of periodic colourings, so infinitely many; `F` of finite index ⟺ `X` finite. **No arithmetic of the lattice enters.**
grade: hand; Coxeter (H-iii, H-iv); the closing step checked by Poros and the owner
rests_text: row 79's headline; C3 is open only from four colours up; H-iii supersedes de Bruijn's dB-T2 (C3 when every frozen sublattice is saturated, with the lemma dB-L4), which stays proved.
kernel: declined for now (the analytic extension is the costly part); the stub for T22 records it as the second target.

title: `Θ₃(Λ₁₀) = 16` isolated points of order 3, so `F = P = 3Λ` at ℚ(√11) with no forcer and no solver
statement: The exact trees (de Bruijn: Fraction simplex with Bland's rule, 1,803 nodes, 24 leaves; Coxeter: sympy's exact simplex, 651 nodes) find 16 points, each fully tight (an additive `φ : Λ → 𝔽₃` with `φ(U) ∌ 0`) and of zero extent; by T23 every colouring is `c(0) + φ`, 48 in all (T12's count), and the 16 functionals have rank 4 over 𝔽₃ and common kernel `3Λ`.
grade: tools exact + hand; de Bruijn and Coxeter, independently
rests_text: T12 re-derived; row 79; B's tight-prime reading half-explained (G54).

title: The `Θ`-emptiness certificate: an exact tree plus a Fraction-only checker
statement: At every node the tree records rational multipliers bounding the next unit vector's `θ`-value (the box handled by `u = max(0, −(yA + c))`), its children cover every integer band the certified range meets, and an infeasible node carries a Farkas vector; the checker recomputes every bound and child list and **re-enumerates the lattice's unit vectors from its key**. Instance: FS-61's shape `60|5,1,5,3;0,2,0,2;0,0,10,2;0,0,0,4` over ℚ(√47) — 2,997 nodes, 0 leaves, 653 KB, `CERTIFICATE OK … Θ EMPTY` — an independent proof, with T22, that the lattice is not 3-colourable (`χ(ℚ(√47)²) ≥ 4`, row 73's known value) with no LRAT file. E's certificate: `Ld65c8ee8` over `d = 11`, 20,843 nodes, 4.9 MB.
grade: cert; Coxeter; E added one over `d = 11`

title: `Ld14c588b` over ℚ(√167) is 3-colourable with period index 1,080

title: Four colours have no linear criterion and no height
statement: In rank 1 four sets `D ⊂ {1..10}` are 4-colourable with no `θ` having `‖θd‖ ≥ 1/4` (e.g. `{1,3,4,5}` by the period-8 word `0,1,0,1,2,3,2,3`); structurally, labelling colours by `V₄`, every closed 4-walk of `K₄` lifts through the cube `Q₃`, whose square complex is a sphere, and `K₄ = Q₃ / antipode`, so `K₄`'s square complex is `ℝP²`: a 4-colouring carries only a winding in `Hom(R, ℤ/2)` — no integer height, no slope, no fibre, no McShane extension. So **no `Θ`-type two-sided certificate exists at four colours**; a two-sided finite certificate scheme exists iff 4-colourability of Cayley graphs of ℤ^r is decidable (refusals by compactness; colourability iff C3-aper holds at four).
grade: tools + hand; Coxeter (C-5, §6), de Bruijn (§4)
verdict: closes (the decidability equivalence is a reduction, not a decision).

title: P-D3 is refuted: forced differences compose
statement: If `G` forces `(0, a)`, then `G ∪ (G + a)` forces `(0, 2a)`. With Harder's `a = 8/3`, the pair `(0, 16/3)` is forced at 2-adic depth 4 at both primes of `E = ℚ(√−3,√−11)` above 2; `16 = 6·(8/3)` and `48 = 18·(8/3)` follow by longer chains.
grade: hand; A

title: Rank-1 walls at four colours, and the wall criterion
statement: A wall between two rigid phases of a common period `p` separates `p ∈ P`, so it is a rank-1 counterexample to C3 (sufficient, not necessary); at three colours there are no walls (`max D ≤ 10`, as T24 requires); at four the first walls appear at `max D = 10` (`{1,5,7,10}`, `{3,5,9,10}`, `{3,7,9,10}`, `{5,7,9,10}`) and in the triangle-chain family (three sets) — every one with `P = F = 0`.

title: L3 is loose at four colours without a gap: `F = P = 0`

L2 and L6: `F = P = 0` from their gapped colourings at `N = 5` (7 of 7 read `KPer = 0`). L3 has 96 ℤ/4 and 216 `(ℤ/2)²` additive colourings and no `5L3`-periodic colouring.

title: The fibre-collision sandwich: `D_Q ⊆ V_Q`, and `V_Q/D_Q` is the image of `Q`'s cycle space
statement: With `R(Q)` the residues of `U mod W` carried by an edge inside the two-colour component `Q`, `Δ_ρ` the differences of unit vectors in one residue fibre and `D_Q = Σ_{ρ ∈ R(Q)} Δ_ρ`: out along `u` and back along `−u′` is a closed walk of voltage `u − u′`, and changing a lift moves a voltage within `D_Q`, so `V_Q = D_Q + (one lift of a cycle basis)`. A target escapes iff `e ∉ V_Q`: membership, not the index. On L3 at `N = 2` (all 2,304 colourings): the rank-deficient components are exactly the single-residue ones (`V = Δ_ρ`, rank 4); the cycle correction lies in `(ℤ/2)²`; so the odd part of `[2Λ : V]` is that of `[2Λ : D]`, and Poros's 81 = 3⁴ is colouring-free arithmetic of L3's unit vectors mod 2.
grade: hand; F; measured on L3
rests_text: the plan's T10.2 re-wording; P-R2 (the index as an ideal norm) answered by mechanism.

title: KR6: de Grey's lattice with the ζ₆-orbit of ρ₁₅ has rank 6, 78 unit vectors, `F ⊇ 8Λ_dG`, and no periodic colouring at any `N ≤ 6`

statement: C3-inherit at `Λ` ⟺ `P = F`; it needs `rank F = rank P`; if `P` has finite index, C3 at `Λ` ⟺ `F` has finite index ⟺ every colouring is periodic (both proved instances are therefore instances of rigidity, as both competitors observed); `P_found ⊇ lcm(N)·Λ` only when every voltage group has full rank; the census confirms C3 at a lattice and never refutes it.

title: The invariant-measure subgroup: `F ⊆ F_μ ⊆ F_meas ⊆ F_clopen = P`
statement: `F_μ = {δ : μ{c(0) ≠ c(δ)} = 0 for every invariant probability measure on X}` is a subgroup containing `F`, inside `P` (a periodic separator's finite orbit carries a uniform invariant measure); the periodic colourings are the continuous colourings of the odometer `Λ ↷ Λ̂`. So C3-inherit splits into a walls half (`F = F_μ`: fails iff some colouring separates only on a set of zero upper Banach density, by the Furstenberg correspondence) and a recurrent half (`F_μ = P`: holds when periodic-orbit measures are weak-* dense).
grade: hand; the modeling planner at the owner's amendment A4

V2's route, written before reading E, branches on relation values rather than on `θ` (the box `[1/3, 2/3]^30`, 39 relations): 45,516 nodes, 30,344 leaves, 149 KB gzipped, checked in 4 s by the Fraction/int-only `tools/fs73v2_check.py`, which enumerates `U` itself; a structurally different rerun on the 26 basis relations alone also passes (34,398 leaves). The owner re-ran V2's checker (PASS) and planted five faults, each refused for its own reason; E planted eight faults on route 1 and six on route 2, all refused; a fake-empty certificate for a colourable lattice is refused.

title: The product structure of `L21cc6506`, and the rational pattern's rotation set
statement: `U = {1, v, v̄, z, z̄}·U_R` exactly, with `U_R` the 12 rational unit vectors, `v = (83+i√167)/84` and `z = (1+i)(15−i√167)/28`; `span U = (1/210)ℤ[i] ⊕ (v/5)ℤ[i]` (the whole key lattice); `θ ∈ Θ₃` iff `μ_b(w) ∈ Θ_R` for the five maps `μ_b`, with `μ_v̄ = (83/42)μ₁ − ν`, `μ_z = (1−i)((7/2)μ₁ − 3ν)`, `μ_z̄ = (1+i)(3ν − (17/7)μ₁)` (V2 re-derived them from `m_{cb} = c̄·m_b`); and `Θ_R = (5/2, 5/2) + (D0 ∪ F4) + 5ℤ²`, `D0` the dodecagon `{|⟨δ, x⟩| ≤ 1/6 on U_R}`, `F4 = {(±5/6, ±5/6)}` four isolated degenerate points — exactly one 12-vertex cell and four point cells per period (V2's exact cell enumeration, `tools/fs73v2_thetaR.py`). The torus is `(ℝ²/210ℤ²) × (ℝ²/5ℤ²)`: `μ₁` sees 42² = 1,764 periods of `Θ_R`, which is why a first-cell search in a reduced basis could not finish.

title: A half-page proof: the 36 unit vectors `{1, v, z}·U_R` already have `Θ₃ = ∅`, and they are a minimal obstruction
statement: Writing `μ₁ = c0 + 5k + δ₁`, `ν = c0 + δ₂` with `δᵢ ∈ D0 ∪ F4`, the third condition reduces mod `5ℤ[i]` to `η = (1−i)((7/2)δ₁ − 3δ₂)` hitting `(5/2)·(i or 1) + (D0 ∪ F4)`, and the four cases (both in `D0`; `δ₂` a point; `δ₁` a point; both points) close by the coordinate bounds `1/6`, `13/12`, `7/6` and the residues of `(5/6)σ`. Among the ten 3-subsets of `{1, v, v̄, z, z̄}` exactly `{1, v, z}` and its conjugate `{1, v̄, z̄}` give an empty `Θ₃` (a 1,050-leaf certificate, 5.7 KB), every other tested sub-configuration colours (an exactly checked `θ` each), and deleting any one of its 18 ± pairs makes `Θ₃` nonempty. So, modulo the criterion's ⟹ direction, **`χ(ℚ(√167)²) ≥ 4` has a half-page proof**: 36 vectors, a 2-D rotation set checkable by hand, four inequality cases.
grade: hand, checked line by line by V2; cert + tools; E (P3b-T4), V2 (T6, T7, T9)

title: The criterion's ⟹ direction by a forward lift, with no parity step and no generation hypothesis
statement: For `Λ` torsion-free, `S = −S` finite with `0 ∉ S`: lift colour steps to `{1, 2}` (the two two-step sums around a square lie in `{2, 3, 4}` and agree mod 3, hence agree), average the resulting cocycle over Følner sets for a mean slope in `[1, 2]^m` that equals the winding on the relation lattice, descend through the direct-summand property of `R` (torsion-freeness is essential: `ℤ/3` with `S = {±1}` is 3-colourable with `Hom(ℤ/3, ℝ) = 0`), and extend from `⟨S⟩` to `Λ` by divisibility of ℝ — so `S` need not generate. And the relation form: `Θ₃ ≠ ∅` iff some `x ∈ [1/3, 2/3]^N` has `r·x ∈ ℤ` for every relation `r` (⟹ for any set of relations, ⟸ for a basis), which is what V2's certificate branches on.
grade: hand; V2, independently of both competitors

title: C1 complete: a non-trivial four-colour edge-local height exists iff `S` has a sum-closed half, and every such graph is four-colourable — so the edge-local format accepts no certificate on any graph of 𝒞 at four colours
statement: On the split presentations the height is Moore–Newman's, generalised: `A_s(a, b) = σ(s)·E(a ⊕ b)` with colours in `V₄` and `E` the three vectors of an equilateral triangle. Four-colourability of the split forms: two colours, three colours, a Θ₃ point, and for a dependent `±{a, b, a+b}` (a distance graph `G(ℤ, {p, q, p+q})`) a direct stripe colouring descended from the triangular lattice, which replaced a recalled, unread lonely-runner citation. Among unit-distance lattice graphs of rank ≥ 2 only ℤ[ζ₆] has a non-trivial one; de Grey's lattice has none (C1(c)). Coxeter's reading that the format never accepts non-degenerately on a K₄-free graph (its Q1) is this theorem, proved by de Bruijn. **Scope:** the edge-local format only.

De Bruijn's "cross squares" derivation was retracted by him (retraction 2) and replaced; the conclusion stands. **Scope:** presentations with `n ≥ 2` generator classes (`n = 1` has no squares); the edge-local format.

title: L3 and the layer torsion character; L4′: `1/3 ∈ ℤ[U_F]` and `Θ₃(F) ≠ ∅` make `F²` bipartite
statement: - *Statement.* - For `θ ∈ Θ₃(F)`, each layer `θ(b·)|_{R₅}` lies in `Θ(U₅)` (L3). - `τ(x) = lim_k θ(25^{−k}x)` is a character `R_F → (1/6)ℤ/ℤ` taking the value 1/2 on parity-type units and 1/3 or 2/3 on order-3 ones. - If `1/3 ∈ ℤ[U_F]`, then `τ = 1/2` on `U_F`, a bipartition. - *L4 as stated follows:* a relation `1 = Σ c_j u_j` with `3 | c_j` and `Σ c_j` even gives `1/3 ∈ ℤ[U_F]` and contradicts `τ(1) = 1/2`. The two conditions together are equivalent to "`1/3 ∈ ℤ[U_F]` and `F²` not bipartite". - *The field-level step, named:* `λ_e` is never torsion on `R₅`, because every layer contains `5^{−k}` for every `k`. -

title: The field-free form (P-F3), sharpest verified shape, with F-T4 as its corollary
statement: - *Statement.* For every multiplicatively closed `U` in the unit circle with `U₅ ⊆ U`, `1/3 ∈ ℤ[U]` and an odd closed walk in `Cay(ℤ[U], U)`, that Cayley graph, and hence the unit-distance graph on `ℤ[U]`, is not 3-colourable. - *Sharpest instance:* for squarefree `d ≡ 11 (mod 12)` the **listed five layers `{vᵏ : |k| ≤ 2}·U₅`**, `v = ((2n−1) + i√d)/(2n)`, already have empty `Θ₃`. The relation `1 = 2n − nv − nv̄` supplies both hypotheses. - *Corollary (F-T4):* - every `F ⊆ ℝ` with `1/3 ∈ ℤ[U_F]` and `F²` not bipartite has `χ(F²) ≥ 4`; - in particular **`χ(ℚ(√d)²) ≥ 4` for every squarefree `d ≡ 11 (mod 12)`**, which is T4 (G61) for the whole family; - **`χ(ℚ(√2, √7)²) ≥ 4`**, an instance with no √3 and no four-chromatic quadratic subfield: `1/3 = 1 + u + ū` with `u = (−1 + 2√2 i)/3`, and L4's relation is `1 = 12 + 3u + 3ū − 6v₇ − 6v̄₇`. -

title: The contrapositive: for every real number field `F`, `χ(F²) = 3` ⟹ some prime of `F` above 3 has odd residue degree

No additive colouring passes through such a prime (Hilbert 90 and `χ(Γ₂₇) ≥ 6`). **Stub candidate.** -

title: The finite threshold for the listed configurations
statement: - *(a) The rational layer at every level.* `Θ_K = c_K + (D_K ∪ F_K) + 5^Kℤ²`, with `D_K = ⋂_{|m|≤K−1} wᵐD0`. This proves P0.1's reading for all K; the polygons match P0.1 vertex for vertex at K = 1..6. - *(b) Configuration A.* `A = {1, v, v̄}·U^(5^K)`, listed. It is NONEMPTY at every K for `d ≡ 11 (mod 24)`, by the field-level point `(θ₂, θ₂, χ)` on `R₅ + vR₅ + v̄R₅`, whose relations are exactly `R₅·(2n−1, −n, −n)`. At `d ≡ 23 (mod 24)` it is EMPTY at the field level, hence at finite K. - *(c) Configuration B, and A at `d ≡ 23 (mod 24)`.* - EMPTY whenever `5^K > √2·r_K·d` (a norm bound on the torsion residual, after Gauss's lemma). - NONEMPTY whenever `5^K ≤ √2·h_K·d` (the alternating point `g_k = (−1)^k c_K/d`). - Hence `K_B(d) = min{K : d < 21·5^{K−1}}` exactly for `d < 65,625`, and as an upper bound for every d. - In the milestone's variable: `5^K ≳ (0.94–0.99)·n`. The planner's `5^K ≳ 2n` is implied, and twice too large. - *Checked:* - against every phase-0 A/B row: 7 listed rows agree, and the saturated rows lie outside the statement; - against phase 0's tree at d = 11 (B EMPTY at K = 1), and at 11, 23, 47, 59 (NONEMPTY); - against six explicit certificates lifted by V2's `theta_from_x` and passed by `tools/fs81_theta_check.py`, with the threshold's edge at 491/527 (K = 3) and 2603 (K = 4) behaving as predicted, and a planted point refused. -

verdict: closes: one mind (the verifier), checked by exact computation against every phase-0 row it covers, six explicit points and a planted point. -

The census used saturated lattices of its own, not configuration A. title: The embedding lemma: a B₃ (or balanced-base) embedding of a finite graph `H` into a distance graph on ℤ, congruent to a proper `k`-colouring of `H` mod `k`, keeps `χ ≤ k`, keeps triangle-freeness, and makes every `k`-colour compulsion of `H` translation-invariant (= Coxeter's FS85-C1, the free embedding)
statement: de Bruijn: `λ = 4μ + t` with `μ` a base-8 B₃ set; Coxeter: `n_i = f(i) + kK·B^i`, `B ≥ 7` odd, `kK > 6(k−1)`, balanced base-`B` digits. Triangle-freeness: a triangle `s + t = r` in `±D` is a relation among six `λ`'s that the B₃ (resp. base-`B`) condition makes formal, i.e. three edge vectors of `H` summing to zero — a triangle of `H`. Translation invariance is free: a Cayley graph contains every translate of its finite subgraphs, and forcing is monotone upward.

title: The roots of unity of the coordinate field, and the pentagon exclusion
statement: Let `F = ℚ(√3,√5,√7,√11)` (the field of every object M18 built; the argument uses only that `F` is real multiquadratic and `2 ∉ ⟨3,5,7,11⟩` in `ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2}`). Then `μ(F(i)) = ⟨ζ₁₂⟩`: a primitive `n`-th root of unity lies in `F(i)` iff `n ∣ 12`. **Consequences.** (a) A regular unit-sided `n`-gon with vertices in `F²` exists iff `n ∣ 12`: the ratio of two consecutive edge vectors is `ζ_n` (up to sign) and lies in `F(i)` when the vertices do; so the only odd order is 3 — "1/3 is the only class that closes an odd regular cycle" is a theorem about the field. (b) In particular the classes at `r² = (5 ± √5)/10`, which close into unit pentagons over ℝ, hold no five points of `F²` at 72° spacing (`cos 72° = (√5−1)/4 ∈ F`, but the rotation `ζ₅` is not in `F(i)`). *Not claimed:* anything about odd cycles of the unit-distance graph that are not regular polygons (the Moser spindle in `F²` has 5-cycles).

title: The quadrature law
statement: For seam-field material in `K = ℚ(√3,√11)` (rank 4 over ℚ: `1, √3, √11, √33`), let `R = s·W` be a unit rotation with `s` a "seam decoration" (`|s| = 1`, both coordinates in `K`) and `W` a word in the new-field generators `√ρ₁₅ = (√15+i)/4`, `√ρ₆₃ = (3√7+i)/8`. For a detuned-copy point `R·(anchor+u)` and a base point `anchor+v` (`u, v` seam-field offsets from a common rotation centre), write `z = s·u·v̄`; the unit-cross-chord condition `|u|² + |v|² − 2·Re(W·z) = 1` splits — because `K`, `√15·K`, `√7·K`, `√105·K` are ℚ-linearly-independent radical blocks — into one equation per block: **(1)** if `W` is an even power of `ρ₁₅` ("full spindle"), `Im(z) = 0` (`u` and the `s̄`-twisted `v` are collinear through the anchor) and the radii `t = |u|, r = |v|` lie on the conic `t² + r² − 2·Re(W)·(±t·r) = 1`; **(2)** if `W` is an odd power of `√ρ₁₅` ("half spindle"), `Re(z) = 0` (perpendicular through the anchor) with conic `t² + r² ± 2·Im(W)·t·r = 1`; **(3)** likewise with `√ρ₆₃`/`√7` in place of `√ρ₁₅`/`√15`; **(4)** if `W` carries nontrivial content in BOTH families, all four blocks vanish, forcing `u·v̄ = 0` — no genuine cross chord exists at all (other than through the anchor itself).
grade: hand; the M31 implementer; confirmed at 26 exact censuses
verdict: closes (elementary linear algebra over four independent radical summands; every predicted conic/collinearity/perpendicularity was found exactly on the predicted locus at every census point).
rests_text: the stacking law (M32-T1, the copy↔copy analogue of this same argument); row 27's "the mitotic hexagram is 4-chromatic" and "the 1581's gen-1 closure is 5-colourable" findings; G12; the kernel instance `quadrature_rho15` (`Quadrature.lean`, row 28, M32), which formalises only the `W = ρ₁₅` even-word case.
kernel: partial — the even-word instance at `W = ρ₁₅` is **kernel** (`quadrature_rho15`, `Quadrature.lean`, M32); the general law across all words (odd words, `ρ₆₃` words, mixed words) was explicitly deferred to instruments-only status at M31 ("Kernel certification of the ρ₁₅ instance is DEFERRED to M32 ... M31 stays instruments-only") and never generalised past that one instance in any later milestone found in this audit — the general law is **declined** (owner, 2026-09-22): no row or kernel statement consumes it, and G12 reads it as a design rule (rank rotations by their conic); the instance already in the kernel is the one the certified witness needed.

title: The stacking law
statement: For a stack `H ∪ R₁·H ∪ R₂·H` of seam-field material (`Rᵢ = sᵢWᵢ` about anchors `aᵢ`, in M31-T1's vocabulary): **(a)** *same anchor* (`a₁ = a₂`): the pair `(R₁H, R₂H)` is isometric to `(H, R₁⁻¹R₂·H)`, so copy↔copy coupling is exactly M31-T1's single-word law at the relative word `R₁⁻¹R₂` — same-anchor stacks are thin by the same mechanism, however many copies are stacked. **(b)** *different anchors, same rotation* (`a₁ ≠ a₂`, `R₁ = R₂ = sW`): writing `A = a₁ − a₂`, `w = u − v`, `ζ = s·w·Ā`, the cross-coupling equation splits, as in M31-T1, into a collinearity condition (`Im(ζ) = 0`, a pin on the DIFFERENCE of the two offsets, not on either point alone) and a quadratic in `|w|` with at most two roots per ray sign. In particular `w = 0` is a root iff `|A| = 1`, giving a translation matching of size `|H ∩ (H + A)|` — O(n) coupling, realised exactly at the unit-separated anchor pairs this project's fabric naturally supplies (e.g. the M23 triangle's pivots); at separation `|A|² = 1/3` the quadratic's discriminant carries `√59 ∉ K`, so the channel is empty at that separation.
grade: hand; the M32 implementer; confirmed by census
verdict: closes for cases (a) and (b) as stated: every point prediction of the a-priori algebra was confirmed exactly by the census, including the sign of the discriminant at the sterile separation.
rests_text: the "mechanism, named" reading recorded alongside it in the plan — that a perfect matching (1-regular coupling) "carries no colour pressure", even composed into forced-rainbow triangles — is a SEPARATE, weaker claim (see § below, not filed here). G14.

title: The coset ladder on the triangular lattice: an exact enumeration at index ≤ 5
statement: Sublattices of `ℤ[ζ₆]` of index `N` correspond exactly to the Hermite-normal-form bases `{(a,0), (b,d)}` with `a·d = N`, `0 ≤ b < a` (hex coordinates `a + bζ₆`, norm `a² + ab + b²`). Over the complete enumeration of such bases at `N = 4` and `N = 5`: every index-4 sublattice contains a lattice vector of norm 1 or 4 (so no coset 4-colouring of the triangular lattice avoids the distance pair `{1, 2}`); every index-5 sublattice contains a vector of norm 1 or 3 (so no coset 5-colouring avoids `{1, √3}`, hence none avoids the compound `{1, √3, 2}`); but exactly three of the five index-5 sublattices (the `(5,1)`-type at `b = 1, 2, 3`, e.g. `⟨(5,0), (1,1)⟩`) avoid norms `{1, 4}` with minimum norm 3, so coset 5-colourings of the LATTICE avoiding `{1, 2}` DO exist.
grade:
tools; exact enumeration,
the M35 implementer
verdict: closes (a finite, exhaustive, exact computation; no sampling).
rests_text: the phase-2 search-design decision that `d = 2` is the "most promising class" for a `k = 5` avoider hunt (the lattice already 5-avoids `{1, 2}`); not consumed by any kernel Lean development found in this audit, and not restated in `LEDGER.md` row 32.

title: The coset-7 brick family is forced boundary-tight, in the separated design regime
statement: For the brick colouring model with table `(i + 3j) mod 7` (the norm-7 coset colouring of `ℤ[ζ₆]` induced by the ideal `(τ)`, `τ = −3 + ζ₆`, `N(τ) = 7`) laid out as `w × h` cells with row shear `s = w/2` on an `m × n` torus, **provided** the `|Δb| = 1` offsets are separated rather than enclosed (`(3w/2)² ≥ 1`, "the design regime"): the self-offset `(0,0)` forces the strictly-separating certificate's upper end `hi = w² + h² ≤ 1`, and the coset offset `(1,2)` forces its lower end `lo = w² + h² ≥ 1` — jointly pinning `w² + h² = 1` exactly. So every member of this one-parameter family has cell diagonal exactly the unit distance, and no *strictly*-separating certificate (`q < lo ∨ hi < q`) can accept any of them; only a *boundary-tight* one (`q ≤ lo ∨ hi ≤ q`) can — which is why M35's phase-2 search (built on the strict check, plus a `diag² < 1` search-grid filter) refused the whole family outright, twice over.
grade:
hand; the M36
implementer; confirmed exactly

title: The exact edge criterion for a scaled constraint graph
statement: Fix the triangular lattice at scale `p`, `T = 1/p`, and its Voronoi cell `C` (a hexagon in address coordinates under the form `Q(a,b) = a²+ab+b²`). For a lattice offset `d ≠ 0`, let `H = C − C = 2C` be the difference body (the hexagon with vertices `2·hole i`). Then the pair of cells at offset `d` realizes exactly the distance-squared set `{Q(addr d + w) : w ∈ H}`, and (since `Q` is convex on `H`) **`max` over this set is attained at one of `H`'s six vertices, and `min` is `0` if `−addr d ∈ H`, else attained on one of `H`'s six edges** (a one-parameter quadratic, minimised exactly in closed form). Consequently `d` is an edge of the constraint graph `G(p)` **iff `min ≤ T² ≤ max`**, and this criterion is **necessary as well as sufficient** (unlike M38's inscribed-disc test, which is only sufficient).
grade:

dense-sampling control
verdict: closes (the convexity argument is elementary and the claimed extremal structure — vertex for max, edge-or-origin for min, of a convex quadratic form over a convex polygon — is standard; the dense-sampling control found no counterexample across the probed grid).

title: The band structure of the constraint graph
statement: For the scaled constraint graph `G(p)` (M39), an offset `d`'s edge-membership interval `[min_H Q(d+·), max_H Q(d+·)]` depends only on `d`'s **dihedral orbit** (not merely its norm: two offsets of the same norm but different point-group class can have different thresholds — first at norm 49, `(7,0)` vs `(3,5)`), so **`G(p)` is one fixed graph on each open interval between consecutive orbit thresholds** ("a band"), and every census/SAT/ball claim is therefore a claim about a band, never a point — boundary scales are tie-break-sensitive and excluded.

title: The torus-wrap Hoffman bound for `G(p)`
statement: `G(p)` is a Cayley graph on `ℤ²` with connection set `S` (a band's edge offsets), so its "spectrum" is the range of the trigonometric polynomial `λ(θ) = Σ_{s∈S} cos(2π s·θ)`, `θ ∈ [0,1)²`, of degree `d = |S|` at `θ = 0`. **Any upper Banach density `δ` of an independent set of `G(p)` obeys `δ ≤ −λ_min/(d − λ_min)`**, hence every proper `k`-colouring (having a class of density `≥ 1/k`) forces `k ≥ 1 + d/(−λ_min)`.

title: The interval-distance bridge
statement: A `G(p)`-edge's two lattice points sit within covering radius `p/√3` of a genuine unit-distance pair, so their scaled distance lies in `[1 − 2p/√3, 1 + 2p/√3]`; hence any colouring of the plane avoiding every distance in that interval restricts to a proper `G(p)`-colouring on the lattice, giving **`χ_{[1−ε,1+ε]}(ℝ²) ≥ χ(G(p))` at `ε = 2p/√3`** — every band theorem is simultaneously a lower bound for the interval-forbidden-distance chromatic number (the genre `[Exoo2005]` opens).

title: Closed-form threshold formulas for the constraint graph's bands
statement: For a lattice offset `d = (a,b)` with canonical representative `0 ≤ a ≤ b`, write `Q = Q(a,b) = a² + ab + b²`. Then the constraint graph `G(p)`'s (M39) threshold interval for `d` has **`depart(a,b) = Q + 2(a+b) + 4/3`** (the max, attained at an `H`-vertex, uniformly across every class including the axis), and **`arrive(a,b)`** is `(b−1)²` on the axis class `(0,b)` (the perpendicular foot lands at an edge midpoint of the difference body `H`, so **every integer `T` is a threshold scale**, `(0,n+1)` arriving exactly at `T² = n²`) or `Q − 2(a+b) + 4/3` on an interior class `1 ≤ a ≤ b` with `a ≤ 2/3`'s in-segment condition failing (the foot leaves the edge, so the minimum moves to the nearest `H`-vertex) — and **non-axis thresholds are always `≡ 1/3 (mod 1)`**.

hand-verified twice"

title: The scaled-shell 7-clique windows are exactly `M ∈ {1, 3, 4}`, and there are no others, ever
statement: A scaled closed shell `z·\text{shell}` (the seven points `0, ±z, ±z(1+ζ₆), ±2z` in address form — difference classes of norm `M = Q(z)`, `3M`, `4M`) is a 7-clique on some band of `G(p)` iff its three class windows overlap, which by M43-T1's formulas reduces to the binding inequality `depart(z) > arrive(2z)` for non-axis `z`, i.e. **`Q(z) < 2·s(z)`** (`s = a+b` of the canonical representative) — satisfied only by `z = (1,1)` (giving `M = 3`) — and to `3k² − 6k − 1/3 < 0` for the axis case `z = (0,k)`, satisfied only by `k ≤ 2` (giving `M = 1` and `M = 4`). **So the complete list of scaled-shell 7-clique windows is `z ∈ {1, 1+ζ₆, 2}`, i.e. `M ∈ {1, 3, 4}` — the classical window (M38), the `√3` window (M39), and the `M = 4` window (M42) — and no others exist at any scale.**

title: No arity-3 pigeonhole exists in the hex-shell's own distance vocabulary
statement: A point set all of whose mutual distances lie in `{1, √3, 2}` has diameter `≤ 2` and minimum distance `≥ 1`, hence (Jung's theorem bounding it in a closed disc of radius `≤ 2/√3`, then a disjoint-open-disc packing argument: the `n` disjoint open discs of radius `1/2` about the points all lie in a disc of radius `2/√3 + 1/2`, so by area `n·(1/2)² ≤ (2/√3+1/2)²`) **at most `⌊4(2/√3+1/2)²⌋ = 10` points**. Since forcing a monochromatic *triple* by pigeonhole at five colours needs `⌈n/5⌉ ≥ 3`, i.e. `n ≥ 11`, **no configuration drawn from `{1, √3, 2}` alone can force a monochromatic triple at five colours by counting** — an arity-3 analogue of the hex-shell's Act One (which uses `n = 7 ≥ 6` for a pair) cannot exist in this vocabulary. Widening to diameter `3` (radicands `4·7−1 = 27`, `4·9−1 = 35`, neither a square, hence non-spindleable) admits up to `19` points, still short of the growth the kill burden would need.
grade: hand; the M48 implementer
verdict: closes (both steps are standard and stated in full; the arithmetic `4(2/√3+1/2)² ≈ 10.95` is a direct computation).

title: Batch-halo composition is sound
statement: Killing is monotone in the point set, and orbit-filtered sub-batch enumeration is sound, complete and one-representative-per-orbit. For a stage graph on vertex set `V` with a cheat (distance-2 edge) set `E₂` and a target pair `(A,B)`: (i) **monotonicity** — if a halo point set `P` kills a separating colouring `c` of the current object (no proper extension of `c` to `P` with `A ≠ B` exists) then so does every superset `Q ⊇ P` (a solution of `Q`'s constraint problem restricts to one of `P`'s, since `P`'s constraints are a subset and the colouring lists depend only on the fixed `c`); (ii) **the sub-batch filter is sound, complete and one-representative-per-orbit** — for a candidate batch `B' ⊇ B`, the palette-canonicalized separating colourings of `(stage − B')` filtered to properness on `B' ∖ B` are exactly the palette-orbit representatives of the separating colourings of `(stage − B)`: (a) *sound* — a filtered colouring is proper on `stage − B` (properness on `(stage−B')`'s edges plus `B'∖B` is properness on all of `stage − B`'s); (b) *complete* — any separating colouring `d` of `stage − B` is one of `stage − B'` too, so its palette orbit has a representative `c` in the canonicalized list of `(stage − B')`, and properness on `B'∖B` together with `c(A) ≠ c(B)` are both palette-invariant, so `c` passes the filter; (c) *one per orbit* by construction of the canonicalization. **Consequence used throughout the milestone's engine:** a single halo, designed against the WHOLE batch's separating-colouring list, may be committed in one certified step removing many cheats at once — composition by construction, no per-edge ordering needed (used to remove 19, then 24, cheats in single commits, §R4/§R6).
grade: hand; the phase-0/2 implementer

title: Cull-by-enumeration is sound and complete
statement: For a candidate kept set `K ⊆ B` of a batch of cheats `B`, the object with standing cheat set `C ∖ (B ∖ K)` still forces the target pair iff every separating colouring of `C ∖ B`, restricted to the live seed block, is monochromatic on some cheat of `K`. Write `Sep(C')` for the proper colourings of the object with standing cheat set `C'` under which the target pair is separated (`f(A) ≠ f(B)`); `S(B) := π(Sep(C∖B))` for their projections to the live seed block; `V(s) := {e ∈ B : s(e₁) = s(e₂)}` for the cheats of `B` a projected colouring `s` wears monochromatic. **Claim:** the object with cheats `C ∖ (B∖K)` (i.e. `B∖K` removed, `K` kept as cheats) forces the target pair **iff** `∀ s ∈ S(B), V(s) ∩ K ≠ ∅`. *Proof, both directions, two lines each:* (⇐) take any colouring `f ∈ Sep(C ∖ (B∖K))` — this is `Sep(C∖B)` with `K` also proper, so its projection `s ∈ S(B)` is proper on `K`, i.e. `V(s) ∩ K = ∅`, contradicting the hypothesis; hence no such `f` exists, i.e. the object forces. (⇒) if some `s ∈ S(B)` has `V(s) ∩ K = ∅`, lift `s` to some `f ∈ Sep(C∖B)` (by definition of the projection); `f` is then proper on `K` too (nothing in `V(s)` — the cheats `s` wears monochromatic — lies in `K`), so `f ∈ Sep(C ∖ (B∖K))`, i.e. the object does not force. **Three engineering consequences drawn from the theorem** (recorded here because they are what the cull driver is built around, though they are not separately proved facts): soundness is checked twice (a numpy re-scan of every `V(s)` against the chosen `K`, and an independent certify-ask that does not depend on the enumerator); an incomplete enumerator can only make `K` too small, a failure the certify ask catches; every cheat kept by an inclusion-minimal `K` is individually necessary (has a witness colouring `s` with `V(s) ∩ K = {e}`, monotone under further removals), so the culler's kept set is 1-minimal by construction.

title: Theorem 7.3: the residue obstruction (the 2-SAT criterion)
statement: For a `K`-point graph `Γ = (V, E₁, C)` with unit edges `E₁`, cheats (distance-2 edges) `C`, and a distinguished pair `A, B`, let `Σ(C′)` be the 2-SAT instance with a boolean `x_v` per vertex, clauses `x_u ⊕ x_v` per cheat in `C′`, `¬(x_u ∧ x_v)` per unit edge, and `¬(x_A ∧ x_B)`. If `Σ(C′)` is satisfiable, then for every finite `H ⊂ K²` the graph on `V ∪ H` with unit edges and cheats `C′` has a proper 5-colouring separating `A` from `B` — so no set of `K`-points, of any size or depth, ever turns `C′` into a forcing set.

title: Proposition 6.1 + Corollaries 6.2, 6.3: the criterion at 2, general number field
statement: For a number field `F` and a prime `𝔮` of `F` above 2: the primes of `F(i)` above `𝔮` are fixed by conjugation iff `𝔮` does not split in `F(i)/F`, iff `−1 ∉ F_𝔮×²`; then there is exactly one such prime `𝔭`, with `N(𝔭) = N(𝔮)^f`, `f ∈ {1,2}` the residue degree of `F_𝔮(i)/F_𝔮`. **Corollary (four colours):** if some prime `𝔮` above 2 has `−1 ∉ F_𝔮×²`, with `N(𝔮) = 2` or (`N(𝔮) = 4` and `F_𝔮(i)/F_𝔮` ramified), then `χ(G(F²)) ≤ 4`. **Corollary (necessary for five):** if `F²` holds a 5-chromatic graph, `−1` is a square in every completion of `F` above 2 with residue field `𝔽₂`.

[hand; the original 2026-09-05 by Kooshi's parallel session, self-corrected 2026-09-06 (§10.1) and by a further correction 2026-09-11 (§10.2)]** For `F = ℚ(√d : d ∈ S)` real multiquadratic, all 2-adic completions are `ℚ₂(√e : e ∈ S)`, and `−1` is a square there iff `S` contains an odd element `≡ 7 (mod 8)`. **Original §6.2:** "if no odd element of `S` is `≡ 7 (mod 8)`, `χ(F²) ≤ 4`; the bound improves to 2 when the completion of `F(i)` has residue field `𝔽₂`" — **wrong**: the two-colour clause is too narrow (`ℚ(√5)` is bipartite by `[Fischer1990]` Thm 8, but its completion has residue field `𝔽₄`, so the original clause put it under "four"). **Corrected form (§10.2, 2026-09-11), = `LEDGER.md` row 63 / FS-36's theorem:** with `V ⊆ ℚ₂×/ℚ₂×²` the image of `S`: (a) `[−1] ∉ V ⟹ χ ≤ 4` (unchanged); (b) `[−1] ∉ V ∧ [3] ∉ V ⟹ χ = 2`; (c) `[−1] ∈ V ∨ [3] ∈ V ⟹ χ ≥ 3` — together, `χ(F²) = 2` exactly when no odd element of `S`'s square-class group is `≡ 3 (mod 4)`.

title: Corollary 6.5: real quadratic fields under the 2-adic criterion
statement: For `d > 1` squarefree, `F = ℚ(√d)`: the 2-adic completion of `F(i)` contains `√−1` iff `d ≡ 7 (mod 8)`, and a primitive cube root of unity iff `d ≡ 3, 5 (mod 8)`. **Corrected verdicts** (§10.1, replacing the file's own original which put `d ≡ 5 (mod 8)` under "≤ 4"): bipartite for `d` even or `d ≡ 1 (mod 8)` — **and, per `[Fischer1990]` Thm 8's exact criterion `N ≢ 3 (mod 4)`, also for `d ≡ 5 (mod 8)`**; at most 4-chromatic for `d ≡ 3 (mod 8)` (Thm 10); 3-chromatic for `d ≡ 3, 7 (mod 12)` (Thm 9, giving the exact values `χ(ℚ(√3)²) = χ(ℚ(√7)²) = 3`); beyond the residue method for `d ≡ 7 (mod 8)`, where the note itself exhibits an explicit unit 5-cycle in `ℚ(√7)²` (`0, −1, −1+ζ, −1+2ζ, −1+2ζ+(w/2)(−1+i)`, `ζ = (3+i√7)/4`, `w = (1+i√7)/2`), giving `χ(G(ℚ(√7)²)) ≥ 3` with no equilateral triangle.

title: Theorem A′ + Corollary 6.6: the linear (additive-subgroup) refinement and the 3-adic wall
statement: Let `𝔭` be a conjugation-fixed prime of `F(i)` with residue field `k`, `k₀` the residue field of `𝔮 = 𝔭 ∩ F`. Every unit vector's residue lies in the norm-one group `C = {c ∈ k× : c c̄ = 1}`; if `H ⊆ k` is an additive subgroup with `H ∩ C = ∅`, then `z ↦ (z mod 𝔭) + H` is a proper colouring with `[k:H]` colours. **Corollary 6.6 (the 3-adic wall):** if `F` has a prime above an odd `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` of residue degree one, `χ(G(F²)) ≤ p` — such a `𝔮` has residue field `𝔽_p` (no square root of `−1`), so it is inert in `F(i)`, `C` has order `p+1`, exactly `(p+1)/2` of the `p+1` lines of `𝔽_{p²}` over `𝔽_p` meet `C`, and a line avoiding it gives `p` colours.

The **residue chromatic number** `χ_res(F)` (the least `[k:H]` over all conjugation-fixed primes and admissible `H`) is defined here, with `χ_res(ℚ) = 2`, `χ_res(ℚ(√3)) = χ_res(ℚ(√7)) = 3`, `χ_res(K) = 4` (each exact), `χ_res(ℚ(√3,√5,√11)) = 11` (Heule's field — above the plane's own 7, hence uninformative there).

title: Lemma 7.5: one gluing step stays multiquadratic
statement: For `a, b ∈ F²` at distance `d`, `0 < d < 2`, the two points at unit distance from both are `p± = (a+b)/2 ± v√(4/d²−1)`, `v = i(b−a)/2`, lying in `F(√r)²` with `r = 4/d²−1 ∈ F`, and in `F²` iff `r` is a square in `F`. Iterating from a `K`-point set therefore produces only multiquadratic extensions of `K` (never a cubic field, e.g. Haugland's).

title: D1: the critical-set localization theorem
statement: Let `χ(G) = k+1` and `C(G) = {v : G − v is k-colourable}` (the critical set). If `(p,q)`, `p ≠ q`, is forced equal at `k+1` colours, then `C(G) ⊆ N(p) ∩ N(q)` (in particular `p, q ∉ C(G)`); if `(p,q)`, `p ≁ q`, is forced distinct, then `C(G) ⊆ N(p) ∪ N(q)` (again `p, q ∉ C(G)`). The spare-colour lemma is the special case `C(G) = V` (impossible, since `V ⊄ N(p) ∩ N(q)` — `p ∉ N(p)`). **In the plane:** two distinct points have at most two common unit neighbours and none beyond distance 2 (`PartnerLattice.eq_gluePoint_of_unit_pair`), so a finite unit-distance graph forcing a pair equal at `χ(G)` colours has at most two critical vertices, none if the pair is more than 2 apart; for a virtual edge, `|C(G)| ≤ deg p + deg q`.

title: The forcing-critical set reduces a spindle union's critical-set census to one ask per base vertex
statement: For `W⁺ = U ∪ R(U)` (a spindle union with fused centre `x`, ring chord `y–R(y)`), define `F ⊆ U`, the *forcing-critical set* of `(x,y)` in `U`: `v ∈ F` iff `U − v` no longer forces `x = y`. Then `C(W⁺) ⊆ F ∪ R(F)` — if `v ∈ U ∖ F` then `U − v` still forces `x = y` in `U`, so `W⁺ − v ⊇ (U−v) ∪ R(U)` still refuses four colours (the copy `R(U)` still forces `x = R(y)`, and the ring chord separates `y` from `R(y)`).

title: D1: the extension principle (Extends)
statement: Say `A ⊆ V` *extends* at `k` colours if every proper `k`-colouring of `G[A]` is the restriction of a proper `k`-colouring of `G`. Then for `p, q ∈ A`: `Forces G k p q ↔ Forces G[A] k p q` and `Separated G k p q ↔ Separated G[A] k p q`; consequently, if `A` extends at `k` and `G[A]` is `(k−1)`-colourable, no pair compulsion at `k` colours lives among `A`'s vertices — the spare-colour lemma *relative to a piece*.

title: D2: hub-and-matching absorption

Then `A` extends at `k+1` colours. **Hypothesis (iii) is load-bearing**: a `k`-colourable piece need not be `k`-*choosable*, so a matching attachment with adjacent endpoints can refuse to extend (`K₂,₄` attached by a matching at three colours is the planted red, exhibited in §7 and kernel-checked as `k4MinusEdgeHub`/`k33Pendants`).

title: D3: degree absorption (the `(k+1)`-core)
statement: A vertex `b` of degree `≤ k`: every `(k+1)`-colouring of `G − b` extends (its neighbours use at most `k` colours, leaving one free). Iterating (peel every vertex of degree `≤ k`, then every vertex whose degree in the remainder is `≤ k`, …) leaves the `(k+1)`-core; every pair compulsion at `k+1` colours among the core's vertices is the core's own, and nothing outside the `(k+1)`-core is ever visible at that colour count.

title: L1, the exponent-divisibility lemma (chunk form)
statement: Let `X` be a finite unit-distance graph with points in `F(i)`, `Λ = Λ(X)` the ℤ-span of its unit edge vectors, `φ : Λ → G` a homomorphism into an abelian group of exponent `e`. Then **`φ(p) = φ(q)` whenever `p − q ∈ e·Λ`** (the base case, kernel — `addMonoidHom_apply_eq_of_sub_eq_nsmul`, `addMonoidHom_apply_eq_of_sub_eq_exponent_nsmul`), and more sharply **`φ` vanishes on `Λ ∩ e·Λ₍ₑ₎ = {d ∈ Λ : n·d ∈ eΛ for some n coprime to e}`, and this set equals `eΛ` exactly** (the localization collapses because `Λ/eΛ` is `e`-torsion and `n` is invertible on it — not kernel, an `addOrderOf` argument). *Corollary (Fischer's obstruction, chunk form):* if some unit vector `u ∈ k·Λ₍ₖ₎`, `X` has no additive `k`-colouring.

title: L2, the direction of every certificate

title: L4, what L1 says on the bed
statement: On `U` (the four-colour fabric, 1,953 points), the M53 rigidity dial's forced-equal classes at 2-adic valuation 2 (`4/3, 4, 12`) and valuation 4 (`16/3, 16`) read FREE (0 of 2,145 and 0 of 179 respectively), while valuation 6 (`64/9, 64/3`) reads forced (163/178, 8/11). By M56-T1 (L1), a pair at squared distance `4u` with `u` of 2-adic depth `≥ 2` in `Λ` is forced in **every** additive 4-colouring; since the dial shows valuation-4 classes free, **the 4-colourings separating them on `U` must be non-additive, and the additive-rigidity conjecture is false on `U`** at that valuation — the freedom is carried entirely by non-additive colourings.

title: L5, what L1 says at five
statement: At `k = 5` the only group is `ℤ/5`, so an additive 5-colouring of a chunk `X` is `φ : Λ/5Λ ≅ 𝔽₅^r → 𝔽₅` nonzero on every unit class, up to the scalar action of `𝔽₅ˣ`. For any unit vector `u` and `m ∈ {2,3,4}`: `φ(mu) = m·φ(u) ≠ 0` and `φ(5u) = 0`. **Hence in every additive 5-colouring, every pair at distance `2u, 3u` or `4u` along a lattice direction `u` is separated, and every pair at distance `5u` is forced equal.** Instance: the Exoo–Ismailescu seed's forced pair `(205,206)` sits at distance `5u`; its 446 cheats are `2u`-pairs; M50's 148 absolute virtual edges sit at `3u`/`4u`.
grade: hand; the M56 implementer
rests_text: M57-T2 (D2's "free classes at k=5" restates this exactly, generalizing to the "free/forced/mixed" trichotomy at general `k`); the seed's P3′ prediction (M57-R2).

title: L6, Fischer's obstruction as the field-as-input statement
statement: For the plane `F²`, `1/k ∈ Σ₀(F²)` kills every additive `k`-colouring, and `Σ₀` is a ring, so `1/2 ∈ Σ₀` kills every `2ᵃ`-colouring and `1/3` every `3ᵇ·(…)`-colouring, with `1/5 ∈ Σ₀` always. `1/2 ∈ Σ₀(F²)` holds exactly when the 2-adic wall is broken (a unit vector of even denominator) and fails when a conjugation-fixed prime above 2 exists (`Σ₀` lies in its local ring); likewise `1/3` against the 3-adic wall. **Consequently, over every wall-broken field this project holds (Heule's, de Grey's, F₂₄₇) the plane has no additive `k`-colouring for any `k ∈ {2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,12,…}` — the first open value is 7** — while over `K` itself `1/2 ∉ Σ₀` (the residue colouring's local ring) and `1/3, 1/5, 1/7 ∈ Σ₀`, so `K²` admits additive colourings only at `k` coprime to 105.
grade: hand; the M56 implementer
rests_text: M56-T7 (L8, the additive spindle theorem, which needs the wall-broken fields' `1/2 ∈ Σ₀` half); the standing statement in row 50 ("no 5-chromatic witness has an additive 4-colouring").

title: L8, the additive spindle theorem
statement: Let `(c,q)` be a pair forced equal at four colours on K-fabric with `q − c ∈ 4Λ_fabric` (2-adic depth `≥ 2`), and let `R` be the rotation about `c` with `|Rq − q| = 1` (the spindle). Then the chord vector `Rq − q = (Rq − Rc) − (q − c)` is a difference of two elements each in `4Λ` (one in the copy's lattice, one in the fabric's), hence lies in `4Λ` of the union. **Every spindle over an additively-forced pair has its chord in `4Λ`, so no additive 4-colouring of the union exists.** Confirmed on both spindle witnesses held: de Grey's 1581 (its unique unit vector in `4Λ` is exactly its single cross edge `(11,802)`, at depth 2) and `W = core ∪ R(core)` (its unique unit vector in `4Λ` is exactly its spindle chord `(565,1152)`, at depth 3, `8u/3 ∈ 8Λ`). Heule-510 (a SAT-shrinking of de Grey's construction) has lost the `4Λ` chord but not the `2Λ` ones.
grade: hand; the M56 implementer, derived after the witnesses were read
rests_text: the standing reading in row 50 ("no 5-chromatic witness has an additive 4-colouring"); M56-T6's wall-broken-field obstruction (L8's converse direction — the union's field must be wall-broken for the spindle to exist at all).

title: D1, the reduction theorem
statement: On a chunk's vertex set `S` (a finite subset of a lattice `Λ`), if every proper `k`-colouring is constant on the cosets of some subgroup `H ⊇ k·Λ` (`IsAdditive`), then for `p, q ∈ S` with `p − q = k·w ∈ H`: `Forces Γ k p q` — hence, via the spindle theorem (`add_one_le_chromaticNumber_unitDistance_of_additivelyRigid`), a unit-distance drawing with `|p − q| ≥ 1/2` gives `χ(ℝ²) ≥ k + 1`; the numeral form at `k = 5` is `six_le_chromaticNumber_plane_of_additivelyRigid`. Non-vacuous: the unit path `(0,0)–(1,0)–(2,0)` is additively 2-rigid, drawn at unit spacing gives `χ(ℝ²) ≥ 3` (`three_le_chromaticNumber_plane_of_pathGraph`); the hexagon `ℤ/6` at three colours is the red (`0 1 0 1 0 2` separates `0` from `3 = 3·1`, `cycleGraph_six_not_additivelyRigid`), and `pathGraph_not_additivelyRigid_three` pins the other direction (at three colours the path's unique-up-to-symmetry colouring is `3·V`-periodic without being a coset colouring). **What the theorem does not do:** "every colouring is additive" is a universal over all colourings supplied by an untrusted enumeration; at a jackpot the kernel certificate is the pair's forcing by refutation, never the additivity census — the module docstring is explicit about this.
grade: hand + kernel; the M57 implementer
rests_text: every `AdditivelyRigid`/`Forces` reading in `data/m57/`; row 51's own citation.
kernel: kernel (`IsAdditive`, `AdditivelyRigid`, `isAdditive_of_addMonoidHom`, `IsAdditive.apply_eq`, `forces_of_additivelyRigid`, `add_one_le_chromaticNumber_unitDistance_of_additivelyRigid`, `six_le_chromaticNumber_plane_of_additivelyRigid`, `pathGraph_additivelyRigid`, `three_le_chromaticNumber_plane_of_pathGraph`, `cycleGraph_six_not_additivelyRigid`, `pathGraph_not_additivelyRigid_three`, `AdditiveRigid.lean`) — already row 51's citation, filed here with its full quantified statement and its two reds per FS-71's shape. **Note the plan's own naming (`IsAdditiveOn`, `additivelyRigidOn`) differs from the shipped declarations (`IsAdditive`, `AdditivelyRigid`); the `On` suffix was dropped during implementation — confirmed by `rg` against the actual module, not by memory of the plan's prose.**

title: D2, the free classes
statement: On `A_k = Λ/kΛ` the admissible homomorphisms' kernels split the nonzero classes three ways: *forced* (in every kernel), *free* (in no kernel — every additive colouring separates them), *mixed*. At `k = 5` (prime), every `m·u` with `u` a unit class and `m ∈ 𝔽₅ˣ` is free (`φ(mu) = mφ(u) ≠ 0` for every admissible `φ`) — **this is M56-T5 (L5) restated as a class trichotomy** rather than a per-pair statement; at `k = 4` freeness is not automatic (`2u` with `φ(u) = 2` in `ℤ/4` vanishes). A free class is one where a new unit direction or lattice point's edges can be added at zero cost to the additive family; a mixed class costs some homs but not all.
grade: hand; the M57 implementer
rests_text: M57-T4 (D4, the richness/sparseness tension); the seed's cheats and M50's distance-3/4 virtual edges (free by this classification, per plan text).

title: D3, the Kempe obstruction to additive rigidity, exact (G42's gauge characterisation)
statement: Let `c_φ` be an admissible additive colouring, `a ≠ b` colours, `c = a − b`, `K` a component of the `{a,b}`-subgraph (edges = units `u` with `φ(u) = ±c`; `K` lies in one coset of `Λ_c^φ = ⟨u : φ(u) = ±c⟩`, M56's Kempe localization, M56 §M1.5). (i) The swap `a ↔ b` on `K` is a proper colouring. (ii) A colouring is additive iff its same-colour relation is induced by a subgroup, in particular translation-invariant. (iii) If the `{a,b}`-subgraph has two components `K₁ ≠ K₂` with `p ∈ K₁`, `p' ∈ K₂` same-coloured, and `S` holds an untouched pair `(r,s)` at the same difference `p' − p` (both outside `K₁`), the swap on `K₁` separates `p` from `p'` while leaving `r,s` equal — not additive. (iv) **Hence, on a chunk rich enough to hold such a witness pair: additive `k`-rigidity requires every `{a,b}`-subgraph of every admissible hom's colouring to be connected** — this is `CLAUDE.md` G42's gauge characterisation, `γ(X,k) = Σ (components − 1)` over `(hom, colour pair)`, with `γ = 0` iff rigid. Instances (v): no hexagonal ball of radius `≥ 2` is additively 4-rigid (parallel same-colour lines give disconnected subgraphs); K-fabric `U` is not rigid (M56 measured `Λ_c^φ ⊊ Λ`, 2,321 pairs separated by the sublattice mechanism); at five colours (`ℤ/5`, `c ∈ {±1,±2}`) connectivity needs the units with `φ(u) ∈ {±c}` to span `Λ` **and** to connect `S` — a per-hom, millisecond check.

implementer, correcting the pre-subplan stub's mechanism
rests_text: M57-T6 (R1's K-fabric non-rigidity census, an instance of (v)); M57-T8 (R3's witness census); FS70-T2 and FS70-T10 (the Kempe screen, FS-70's generalisation of this same mechanism to a lattice-wide, not just chunk, statement).

title: D4, the richness dial tension
statement: A chunk loses its `ℤ/5`-homs two ways: a unit vector enters `5Λ` (M56-T1/T5's obstruction), or the hyperplane cover closes (every functional on `𝔽₅^r` vanishes on some unit class). For `s` unit classes in general position, **the expected number of surviving functionals is `5^r·(4/5)^s`**, vanishing past `s ≈ 7.2r` — a probabilistic estimate under a genericity assumption, not an exact count for a specific object (the plan's own table, R5, measures the real objects against it: Heule-510, `r = 8`, keeps 96 of an estimate near zero, because its 60 direction classes are far from generic). The design tension: richness (D4) kills homs while sparseness (D3) leaves disconnected Kempe subgraphs, so the additive-rigidity principle can only live where a small nonzero family has connected subgraphs.
grade: hand + reading; the M57 implementer
verdict: closes for the expectation formula under the stated genericity model; **the formula's real-object predictions are a reading, not a theorem** (R5 measures the real objects far off the generic estimate — see § "Readings" below).
rests_text: M57-T9 (R5's richness census, which finds the formula inapplicable to crystalline material).

title: D5, the additive kill census
statement: A point `p` added to a chunk `X` with unit neighbours `N(p) ⊆ S` kills a colouring `c` iff `c(N(p))` uses all `k` colours. For an **additive** colouring: if `p` is in-lattice (`p − p₀ ∈ Λ`), `φ(p − p₀)` is its own colour and no neighbour wears it (`φ(p − y) ≠ 0` for every unit `p − y ∈ Λ`) — **an in-lattice point never kills an additive colouring by coverage**; it can only kill the homomorphism itself, by a new unit vector landing in `ker φ`. If `p` is out-of-lattice in a genuinely new direction, `φ` extends with one free value and survives iff some choice avoids the neighbours' colours (the ordinary rainbow condition); if `p − p₀ ∈ ℚΛ ∖ Λ`, the extension must satisfy `φ(m(p−p₀)) ∈ m·G` for `m` coprime to `k`.
grade: hand; the M57 implementer
rests_text: M57-T9 (R4's family-delta census on `W`'s depth-one cross points, which confirms the theorem's prediction exactly — 65 of 67 in-lattice points leave the family unchanged).

title: Exoo–Ismailescu's `G` is exactly additively rigid at five colours, and rigidity is far from necessary for forcing
statement: On `G`'s `{1,2}`-graph (205 points, 966 unit + 423 distance-2 edges), the additive family is 18 colourings and `γ = 0`: all 180 `{a,b}`-subgraphs connected, and the complete enumeration of `G`'s colourings returns exactly those 18, all additive (35 total on `G`'s unit-attachment `H`: 18 additive + 12 at defect 1 + 5 at defect 2). **But rigidity is sufficient, not necessary, for forcing**: of `M49`'s 19 separating edge-deletion lists, 6 of 19 admit colourings at the random baseline (defect 79–90 of 214) with no additive structure at all, and the 252-cheat forcing subset (M49's `ddmin` survivors, still forcing `A = B`) has a colouring space above 5,000 up to palette in three defect regimes (1,701 within 14, 2,167 at 16–28, 576 at 94–105 — the random baseline) — **a forcing subset can keep the forced pair while losing additivity almost entirely.**

title: The richness dial: `F₂₄₇`'s thickening kills the additive family before it could close it; de Grey's crystalline closure never dies
statement: `W`'s 71 depth-one cross points in `F₂₄₇` all extend the family (67 in-lattice — by M57-T5 (D5), unchanged at 65 of 67; 4 of index 5, killing a third of the homs); by 63 points (1,238 total) **500 of `W`'s own unit vectors become 5-divisible**, so the family dies outright — the exact mechanism (M56-T1/L7's obstruction realised at depth one), not the hyperplane-cover heuristic of M57-T4 as originally registered. By contrast, de Grey's gen-1 half-spindle closure (24,065 points, 358 distinct directions, rank 32) **keeps at least 300 `ℤ/5`-homs at every radius measured, including the whole closure** — no unit vector ever enters `5Λ`, because the crystal's direction set (329 within radius 1) grows far slower than its point count.

title: The Kloosterman spectral identity, and the Weil–Hoffman refusal of five from 59 up
statement: For `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, `UD(𝔽_p, 2)`'s adjacency eigenvalues are `λ(c) = −K(1, c/4)` for each nonzero norm class `c ∈ 𝔽_p^×` (`K(u,v) = Σ_{t ∈ 𝔽_p^×} e((ut + v/t)/p)` the classical Kloosterman sum), checked numerically to residual `≤ 5.7·10⁻¹⁴` against the full 2-D DFT at every `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` below 600. Weil's `|K(u,v)| ≤ 2√p` and Hoffman's `χ(G) ≥ 1 + λ_max/(−λ_min)` then give `χ(UD(𝔽_p, 2)) ≥ 1 + (p+1)/(2√p)`, hence **`χ > 5` for every `p ≥ 62`** (so every usable `p ≥ 67` refuses five colours with no computation beyond Weil), with the exact spectrum extending the refusal down to `p = 59` (Hoffman `5.022`, margin `0.022` against a float error `≤ 10⁻¹²`).

opening session, from the finite-Euclidean-graph spectrum (Medrano–Myers–Stark–Terras) plus Weil's bound and Hoffman's
ratio bound

title: The field profile for F ⊇ K: 6-open ⟺ wall broken ∧ 11 inert
statement: For a number field `F ⊇ K = ℚ(√3,√11)`, the usable primes (those `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` at which every radicand of `F` is a square mod `p`) are a subset of `{p ≡ 11 (mod 12)} ∩ {p mod 11 ∈ {2, 6, 7, 8, 10}}` — **the only usable prime below 67 for any field containing K is 11** — so with M58-T1, `F ⊇ K` is 6-open (no usable prime seals it at 5) exactly when the 2-adic wall is broken (Theorem B fails to four-colour it) and 11 is inert (some radicand a non-residue mod 11).

elementary quadratic reciprocity, generalized here from the multiquadratic case

title: The exact 2-adic wall criterion over K, correcting the stub
statement: For `F = K(√d)`, `d` odd squarefree, the 2-adic wall (Theorem B's colourability criterion) breaks iff one of the four square classes `{d, 3d, 11d, 33d}` is `≡ 7 (mod 8)` — equivalently **`d ≡ 5` or `7 (mod 8)`** (the `d ≡ 5` case works through `3d ≡ 15 ≡ 7 (mod 8)`), correcting the pre-milestone stub's D3′, which had listed only `d ≡ 7 (mod 8)`. The smallest new member is `d = 13` (`13 ≡ 5 mod 8`, `(13/11) = (2/11) = −1`, non-residue mod 11, hence 6-open by M58-T2).

title: The level-p² lift theorem
statement: Setting: `𝔭` a degree-one prime of a real number field `F` above `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`; a **lift** of `H ⊆ UD(𝔽_p, 2)` along reference positions `x₀ : V → ℤ²` (reducing to `H`) is `y : V → ℤ_p²` with `x₀ + p·y` unit-distant along every edge. Writing, per edge `e = uv`, `D_e = x₀(u) − x₀(v)`, `w_e = y_u − y_v`, `m_e := (|D_e|² − 1)/p ∈ ℤ`: **`H` lifts modulo `p² ⟺` the system `R(H)·ȳ = b` is solvable over `𝔽_p`, where `R(H)` is `H`'s rigidity matrix (row `uv` carrying `D̄_e` at the `u`-block, `−D̄_e` at the `v`-block) and `b_e = −m_e/2`, ⟺ `⟨λ, b⟩ = 0` for every self-stress `λ ∈ ker R(H)ᵀ`** (the Fredholm alternative over `𝔽_p`).
grade: hand; the M59 opening session
rests_text: M59-T2 (the higher-level dichotomy, built on the same expansion); M59-T3 (the stress-count bound); every kernel instance below.
kernel: **kernel, necessity direction only** (`Lift.lean`'s `stressPairing_eq_zero_of_lift`: a lift implies every stress pairs to zero with the defect, over any commutative ring with a square-zero element `π`, i.e. the contrapositive `not_exists_lift_of_stressPairing_ne_zero` is what every kernel instance below actually uses); the sufficiency direction (`b ∈ im R(H) ⟹` a lift exists) is not formalized — declined, no consumer needs it (every instance either finds a nonzero stress pairing, refuting a lift, or Newton-iterates directly in the rigid case, which is M59-T2's separate mechanism).

title: The rigid/flexible dichotomy for a residue framework's lift
statement: For `H` with `rank R(H) = 2|V| − 3` at its residue positions ("infinitesimally rigid"): choosing a Laman basis `E′ ⊆ E` (`2|V| − 3` edges) and gauge-fixing three isometries makes the `E′`-system square with invertible Jacobian mod `p`, so **Hensel's lemma lifts the residue positions to a unique `ℤ_p`-solution of `E′`, up to `p`-adic isometry**; the remaining edges `E ∖ E′` either fail at some finite level (no lift of `H`) or are all unit (a lift exists, **algebraic**: its coordinates generate a number field `F_H ⊂ ℚ_p` with a degree-one unramified prime above `p`, real iff `F_H` has a real place). For `rank R(H) < 2|V| − 3` ("flexible", dimension `f` of infinitesimal flex beyond the three isometries): the `E′`-solutions form a `(3+f)`-manifold and the Hensel tree branches `p^f`-ways per level.
grade: hand; the M59 opening session
rests_text: M59-T5 (adding-a-vertex); the "design in the finite plane, lift to the field" route's closure (§R7: "the route... is closed as a way to FIND a 6-forcer; what survives is its converse"); the measured instances (§R3: the 1581's injective sub-reduction at 131 passes Newton to precision `131²⁰` and agrees with the tower coordinates on 20,000 sampled quadrances).
kernel: declined (§R6: "the kernel form of the rigid dichotomy" is listed among what the milestone did not do) — needs Hensel's lemma over `ℤ_p` for a system with invertible Jacobian, and the recognition of an isolated `ℚ_p`-point as generating a number field; neither is in Mathlib in the needed form.

title: The stress-count bound for a 6-critical residue subgraph
statement: `ker R(H)` always contains the three infinitesimal isometries (two translations, the rotation `v ↦ Jv`, since `⟨D̄, JD̄⟩ = 0`), so `rank R(H) ≤ 2|V| − 3` and `dim(\text{stresses}) ≥ |E| − 2|V| + 3`. A 6-critical `H` has minimum degree `≥ 5` (else a lower-degree vertex could be deleted with `χ` unchanged — the deletion-minimality that "critical" names), so `|E| ≥ 5|V|/2` and **the level-p² test (M59-T1) imposes at least `|V|/2 + 3` independent linear conditions on the defect `b`**; for a "random" `H` each condition fails with probability `1 − 1/p`, so a 6-critical `H` on 100 vertices passes by chance with probability `~ p^{−53}`.

session

title: The finite plane's own geometry, three criteria derived
statement: For `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, `p > 3`, working in `𝔽_p² ≅ 𝔽_p(i)` with quadrance = norm and `C` the norm-one circle (order `p+1`): **(i)** a unit triangle exists (`ω(UD(𝔽_p,2)) = 3`) iff `6 | p+1`, i.e. **`p ≡ 11 (mod 12)`** (else `ω = 2`); **(ii)** the Moser spindle embeds iff `p ≡ 11 (mod 12)` and `11` is a residue or zero mod `p` — **exactly the usable primes of `K = ℚ(√3,√11)`** (the spindle's rotation has trace `5/3`, and its characteristic polynomial's discriminant `−11/9` must be a square or zero on the torus); **(iii)** two spheres of quadrances `c, c′` about a common centre carry unit chords iff `4cc′ − (c+c′−1)²` is a nonzero square (two chords each) or zero (a tangency, one chord); a sphere carries a self-chord iff `4c − 1` is a square — **the spindle-distance condition `4d² − 1` of G12/G37, read verbatim on the finite side.**

opening session

title: The adding-a-vertex corollary
statement: For a lifted (rigid) `H₀` and a residue point `w` with `d` neighbours in `H₀`, the framework `H₀ + w` has stress dimension `d − 2` larger than `H₀`'s, so the level-p² test on `H₀ + w` is `d − 2` new linear conditions: **a degree-2 residue point always lifts** (zero new conditions — the "glue point" of M22's classification, seen from the finite side); **a degree-3 point lifts mod `p²` with probability `1/p` unless it is a shadow.**

title: A field's sealing prime is never its lifting prime
statement: For fields over `K`, the sealing prime is always 11 (M58-T2), but 11 is **ramified** in every field the descent used (`K = ℚ(√3,√11)` itself: `11` ramifies in `ℚ(√11)`), so a `ℤ_{11}`-lift of a K-object would force `√11 ∈ ℚ_{11}` — impossible, since 11's ramification means the residue extension has no room for it. The lift theory (M59-T1/T2) needs an **unramified** degree-one prime, so for fields over K the lift's primes are exactly `83, 107, 131, …` (M58's usable-prime list minus 11) — **the upper bound (M58, via 11) and the lower bound (M59, via an unramified prime) of the sieve use different primes of the same field, structurally, not by coincidence.**

controls; the M59 opening session

title: The compulsion sets of a Cayley plane are unions of norm classes
statement: For `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, the orthogonal group `O(2, 𝔽_p)` (order `2(p+1)`) acts on `UD(𝔽_p, 2)` by automorphisms; its rotation subgroup (the norm-one group of `𝔽_{p²}`, cyclic of order `p+1`) acts **freely and transitively** on each nonzero-norm circle `{quad = c}` (no isotropic vectors, since `−1` is a non-square), so every such circle is one rotation orbit. Hence `F_p(k) ∖ \{0\}` and `S_p(k)` (respectively the differences every `k`-colouring of the plane identifies, resp. never coincides on) are **unions of the `p − 1` norm classes `N_c := \{d : quad\, d = c\}`, `c ∈ 𝔽_p^×`** — so deciding each of the two sets reduces from `p² − 1` individual differences to `p − 1` classes, one representative check each.
grade: hand; the M60 opening session

title: The hex-shell corollary, for every sealing prime `p ≥ 5` at once
statement: Over any field with a usable prime `p ≥ 5` whose residue plane is 5-colourable and pairwise free at five colours (`F_p(5) = \{0\}`, `S_p(5) = N₁`): **no finite unit-distance graph separates a `√3`-pair or a distance-2 pair at five colours, and none forces either pair equal** — each of the two hex-shell gadgets `six_le_chromaticNumber_plane_of_forced_pairs` (row 48, kernel) needs is impossible *separately* over such a field, because `3 ≢ 0, 1` and `4 ≢ 0, 1` modulo every prime `p ≥ 5`.

title: The local bound `L(F)`, and which primes contribute nothing
statement: For a real number field `F`, `L(F) := min` over every prime `𝔭` of `F` at which a residue colouring exists, of that colouring's colour count: at `𝔭 | 2` with conjugation fixing `𝔭` in `F(i)`, the count is `N(𝔭) ∈ \{2, 4\}` (Theorem B / Fischer's bipartite case); at `𝔭 | p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` with residue field `𝔽_{p^f}`, `f` **odd**, the count is `χ(UD(𝔽_{p^f}, 2))`. **Primes with even residue degree, or above `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`, contribute nothing**: the residue field then contains `√−1`, so the homomorphism's `u ≠ v` clause fails (the circle degenerates).

title: The odd-degree face: Weil + Hoffman over `𝔽_q`, `q = p^f`

Measured at `q = 27` (`𝔽₃[t]/(t³−t−1)`, 729 vertices, degree 28): four colours refused in 7 s (the solver's claim), five colours undecided at a 20-million-conflict budget.

title: ϑ = Hoffman on the finite planes, by arc-transitivity: every linear relaxation collapses
statement: `UD(𝔽_p, 2)` is the Cayley graph of `𝔽_{p²}` on the norm-one subgroup `μ_{p+1}`, a **generalized Paley graph** `GP(p², p−1)` with automorphism group containing `𝔽_{p²} ⋊ O(2,𝔽_p)` (order `2p²(p+1)`), transitive on vertices and, since `O(2)` acts transitively on the circle, on arcs. For an arc-transitive graph, `ϑ(G) = n·(−λ_min)/(λ_max − λ_min)` (`[Lovasz1979]` Thm 9) — the Lovász theta number IS the Hoffman ratio bound — and since `ϑ(Ḡ) = n/ϑ(G)` for vertex-transitive graphs, the **whole chain `ω ≤ ϑ(Ḡ) ≤ χ_f ≤ χ` collapses to Hoffman's bound**. Measured (the norm-class LP solved for `ϑ` and Schrijver's `ϑ′` at eleven primes): equal to Hoffman to `2·10⁻¹⁰` everywhere, so **the first digit (`χ ∈ \{5,6\}` at 23, 31, 43, 47) is integrality-carried below `p = 59`: no linear relaxation can reach it, only a cardinality refutation of `α` itself can.**

Lovász's theorem; the M61 opening session

title: The periodic quotient: `χ_per(p) = χ(C_p)`, the circulant of a null direction
statement: A colouring of `𝔽_p²` with nonzero period `d` is constant on the cosets of the line `ℓ = 𝔽_p·d` (the only order-`p` subgroups of `𝔽_p²` are its lines); it is proper only if `ℓ` misses the unit circle (a **null line**, `p+1)/2` of them, all one rotation orbit since `μ_{p+1}` acts on directions with stabilizer `±1`), and then it is exactly a proper colouring of the quotient **circulant** `C_p := Cay(𝔽_p, π(S))` (`π` the projection along `ℓ`, `|π(S)| = (p+1)/2`, symmetric, `0 ∉ π(S)`). Hence **`χ_per(p) = χ(C_p)`, `χ(UD(𝔽_p,2)) ≤ χ(C_p)`, and `α(UD(𝔽_p,2)) ≥ p·α(C_p)`** (an independent set of the circulant lifts to a union of parallel null lines). Measured (`p ≤ 71`): `χ(C_p) = 3, 4, 6, 5, 8, 8, 8, [9,10], [9,10], [9,12], [9,12]` at `p = 3, 7, 11, 19, 23, 31, 43, 47, 59, 67, 71`; at `p = 11` the plane's own five-chromaticity is carried by **non-periodic** colourings only (`χ(C_{11}) = 6 > 5`) — the first prime where that happens; the 19-plane's five is periodic and became a 19-entry kernel certificate.

algebra, the M61 opening session

title: The mechanism of tightness: a spindle escapes its own sealing prime
statement: Over a field `F` sealed at `k` by a usable prime `𝔭` (residue plane `k`-colourable and pairwise free — `F_𝔭(k) = \{0\}`), a pair forced equal at `k` colours has `𝔭 | d²` (M60); its spindle adjoins `√(4d² − 1)`, and since `4d² − 1 ≡ −1 (\text{mod } 𝔭)`, **every prime of the spindled field `F′` above `p` has EVEN residue degree — `p` is no longer usable in `F′`.** So the local bound is attained one level up "because the forcer's own construction removes exactly the prime that gave the bound it beats — never a coincidence of fields." Every attained row of the field table is an instance: the Moser spindle (`d² = 3` over `ℚ(√3)`, sealed at 3; `4·3−1 = 11 ≡ −1 (mod 3)`, and indeed 3 is inert in `ℚ(√11)`); K-fabric's forced pairs at `2, 4, 2√3, 8/3` (all `𝔭₂`-divisible), whose spindles at `2` and `8/3` adjoin `√15` and `√247` (`15 ≡ −1 (mod 16)`, `247 ≡ 7 (mod 8)`, breaking the 2-adic wall). **The consequence at the 6-level**: over a field 5-sealed by 11 (Heule's, K(√247), K(√23)), a five-colour forced pair has `11 | d²`; its spindle adjoins `√(4d² − 1) ∈ \{√43, √131, 5√7, √10, …\}`, each `≡ √−1 (mod 11)`, so the spindled field is 6-open by construction (11 stays inert, every remaining usable prime `≥ 67` by M58-T1) — the 6-level question reduces to ONE: *does any 5-sealed field carry a pair forced equal at five colours?*

title: The rotation-admissibility trichotomy
statement: For a base in `K` (`ℚ(√3,√5,√11,√33)`) and two circle radii `|u|², |v|² ∈ K`, a rotation carrying a unit chord between a point of radius `|u|` and a point of a rotated copy of radius `|v|` exists only for the rotation adjoining `√D`, where `D = |u|²|v|² − k²` and `k = (|u|² + |v|² − 1)/2`, with `D` decided entirely in `K`-arithmetic by an exact tower squareness test (no float in any verdict): **`D < 0`** — no such rotation; **`D` a square in `K`** — the rotation lies in `K(i)`, the union of base and rotated copy stays in `K²`, and **Theorem B four-colours it for free**, so it is never a candidate; **else** — the rotation adjoins `√D` and leaves `K`, a wall-breaking candidate.

title: The pattern-clash correctness theorem for a two-block arena

title: Parts's order-24 symmetry group is `⟨ζ₆⟩ ⋊ Gal(K(i)/ℚ)`, and it preserves both unit distance and the `ρ₁₅` cross-edge law
statement: On coordinates `z = (a + b√33 + i(c√3 + d√11))/12`, the order-24 group closing Parts's base (rotation by 120°, both axis reflections, and "conjugation by `√33`" per his footnote) is `⟨ζ₆⟩ ⋊ Gal(K(i)/ℚ)`: complex conjugation is itself the Galois automorphism `√3, √11 ↦ −√3, −√11` (which fixes `√33` and negates only the imaginary part — the geometric reflection `y ↦ −y`), and the other nontrivial Galois element, fixing `√33` while negating `c√3` and `d√11` individually is impossible over `K(i)` — the two extra order-2 generators beyond `⟨ζ₆, conj⟩` are `√3 ↦ −√3` alone and `√11 ↦ −√11` alone (both arithmetic symmetries of `K` with no direct geometric meaning, since neither alone is an isometry of the plane — they compose to the geometric reflection). Every element is a ring homomorphism fixing `ℚ` applied coordinatewise, hence preserves unit distance; both clauses of the `ρ₁₅` cross-edge law are polynomial identities over `K`, hence preserved too — so the whole type-M arena is equivariant under the order-24 group and **orbit-level selection is sound**.

title: The completeness invariant of the level-enumeration loop
statement: Let `Atoms` be a finite set, `R : 2^Atoms → Prop` upward closed (a *key property*, expressed as `¬ Colorable(W[S ∪ fixed] ∪ C, 4)` for a fixed companion graph `C`), `w` a weight function, `w* = min{w(S) : R(S)}`, and `Y ⊆ Y*` the family of minimal correction sets (complements of maximal `¬R`-sets) harvested so far, with `mhs` the minimum-weight hitting-set functional. Maintaining `E` = the optima of weight `w*` found so far, under the loop that (i) blocks a member of `E` only, never a fresh weight-`w*` set that already satisfies `R`, and (ii) inserts into `Y` only a correction set verified by an actual colouring of its complement: **`E` is exactly `{S : R(S), w(S) = w*}` when the loop halts (MaxSAT returns UNSAT over `Y ∪ {blocked}`).**

title: Expansion cannot raise, and cannot lose, a minimum
statement: Let `A ⊆ A' `be finite point sets sharing the same fixed companion and cross-edge law, and let `R` be a key property expressed as non-4-colourability of `W[S ∪ fixed] ∪ C`. Then every minimum weight-`w*` selection `S` of `A` is still a valid selection of `A'` with `R(S)` holding at the same weight, so `w*(A') ≤ w*(A)`, and no run over `A'` can report a minimum above `w*(A)` or a level `{M}(A')` smaller than `{M}(A)`'s image.

title: Soundness of the incremental and decision MaxSAT hitting-set engines
statement: (i) *Incremental engine.* A core extracted from a MaxSAT instance is an implicate of the hard clauses present at extraction; adding further hard clauses only strengthens the formula, so a core extracted earlier remains a valid core (hence a valid lower-bound contribution) after more correction sets are added — so accumulating cores and relaxations across iterations gives a monotone non-decreasing sequence of valid lower bounds, and the loop halting with the oracle returning SAT at that bound certifies optimality for the current formula. (ii) *Decision engine.* Since the correction-set family `Y` only grows, the previous optimum `w*_{old}` remains a valid lower bound for the new family; asking "is there a hitting set of weight ≤ `w*_{old}`?" and receiving SAT means the optimum is exactly `w*_{old}`.
