title: The expansion loop has no measure, and its improving steps are bounded even so
statement: `A ↦ ⋃{M}(A ∪ Δ)` is not monotone in `A` (M64's overcompression finding — the minimal asymmetric refuser is usually not a subgraph of the minimal symmetric one — is exactly a witness of non-monotonicity), so the fixed-point iteration has no Knaster–Tarski measure: `|W|` is unbounded above (expansion only adds vertices) and `|M|` is not monotone either (`{M}` grows and shrinks as `W` changes). **But** the loop only ever accepts an *improving* incumbent, so at a fixed rung the sequence of accepted minima is strictly decreasing in the positive integers, bounded below by `[Parts2020a]`'s own published `v5 ≥ 28`; hence a run starting at 375 can improve **at most 347 times**.

title: A target ask preserves completeness on success and yields a one-sided bound on failure
statement: Asking `reduce_stage` at a target `t` (is there a refusing selection of weight `≤ t`?) is sound in both outcomes. *Success:* the search returns `w* ≤ t` and enumerates the level at `w*`; the target removed only candidates of weight `> t ≥ w*`, so `M63-T1`'s completeness invariant is untouched and `{M}` is complete at `w*` (the pruning is beat-the-incumbent pruning, independently sound). *Failure:* the MaxSAT lower bound over the harvested `Y` exceeds `t`; since `Y ⊆ Y*` gives `mhs(Y) ≤ mhs(Y*)`, this proves `w* > t` and nothing else — no level, no `A`, no upper bound.

title: The full transfer lattice between a restricted and an unrestricted search over the same stage
statement: For a restricted search (over a subset of atoms, or under a symmetry rung) and the corresponding unrestricted search of the same stage: a **decided ask** transfers both ways, verbatim (colourability of `S ∪ C` depends only on `S` and `C`); a **refusing selection** (an incumbent) transfers upward only (`W'[S] ∪ C = W[S] ∪ C` when `S ⊆ atoms(W)`, the `M63D-T2` argument); **non-criticality** transfers upward only (a superset of a refusing selection still refuses); **criticality** transfers downward only (new material can substitute for an atom that was critical in the smaller stage); a **correction set** transfers downward only (importing one upward can exclude a genuine record, since a selection could satisfy it only through material the larger stage adds).

title: Every rotation with `cos θ ∈ K` carrying a cross edge is realised by a collinear pair, and this is a complete enumeration over the base's lines
statement: Identify the plane with `K(i)`, `K = ℚ(√3,√11)`. For `u, v ∈ K²` and a rotation `ρ = c + is` of modulus 1 with `c ∈ K`, `s ∉ K`: `|u − ρv|² = 1 ⟺ Re(ρ·conj(u)v) = k`, `k = (|u|² + |v|² − 1)/2 ∈ K`; writing `conj(u)v = p + iq` with `p, q ∈ K`, the identity splits over the `K`-basis `{1, s}` into `q = 0` (collinearity with the centre) and `c·p = k`. **Therefore the rotations with `cos θ ∈ K` carrying any cross edge on a given base are exactly `cos θ = k/p` over collinear pairs `(u, v)`, `p = Re(conj(u)v) = ±√(|u|²|v|²)`, `k = (|u|² + |v|² − 1)/2`** — an enumeration over the base's **lines** (`O(Σ_lines n_L²)`), not over point pairs, in exact `K`-arithmetic with no squareness test and no float in any verdict.

title: The endpoint-radius bound `1/|sin θ|`, and its non-existence when `cos θ ∉ K`
statement: For a collinear cross pair at radii `t, s` on one ray through the centre, `1 = t² + s² − 2ts·cos θ`; this quadratic form is positive definite (`|cos θ| < 1`), its solution set (in `s`, for fixed `t`) is an ellipse, and a real solution exists only for `t ≤ 1/|sin θ|`.

title: The general cross-edge law for `cos θ ∉ K`
statement: With `ρ ∈ K(i, √D)` written `ρ = (c₁ + c₂√D) + i(s₁ + s₂√D)`, `c₁,c₂,s₁,s₂ ∈ K`, the identity `Re(ρ(p+iq)) = k` splits over `{1, √D}` into two `K`-linear conditions on a pair `(u,v)` with `w = conj(u)v = p+iq`, `ab = |w|²`, `D = ab − k²`: `c₁p − s₁q = k` and `c₂p − s₂q = 0`, where `ρ = (k + i√D)/w` gives `c₁ = kp/ab`, `c₂ = q/ab`, `s₁ = −kq/ab`, `s₂ = p/ab`. The collinear law (`M63G-T1`) is exactly the degenerate case `c₂ = 0, s₁ = 0` (forcing `q = 0`, `c₁p = k`).

title: The σ-criterion: a one-sided residue elimination for type-M arenas, base-free and radius-free
statement: Let `F` have a conjugation-fixed prime `𝔭` above 2 with residue field `𝔽₄` (so Theorem B's residue colouring applies), and let `ρ` be a rotation with `cos θ ∈ F`, `sin θ ∉ F`. For a collinear cross pair at squared radii `a, b` (`M63G-T1`'s family), write `σ = a + b`; then `d² = |u−v|² = σ − (σ−1)/cos θ`, and the pair is `φ`-monochromatic (invisible to the residue colouring) exactly when `v_𝔭(d²) > 0`. **If every radius sum `σ` realised by a collinear pair of the base satisfies `v_𝔭(σ − (σ−1)/cos θ) = 0`, the type-M arena `L ∪ ρS` is four-colourable — for every base drawn in `F²`, at every radius.**

title: The design-target inversion: which radius sums keep a rotation alive, and the mechanism behind "wall-breaking is necessary, not sufficient"
statement: Given `cos θ` alone (before any base exists), define `Σ_live(cos θ) = { σ : v_𝔭(σ − (σ−1)/cos θ) > 0 at BOTH primes above 2 }` (both, since one free prime already kills the family under `M63G-T4`); each live `σ` names the radius pair a base must contain outright, `a, b` the roots of `x² − σx + ((σ−1)/(2cos θ))²`. **So a base is alive for a rotation only if it realises a live `σ` at both primes above 2 — necessary, not sufficient.** Equivalently, reading from a point of squared norm `n` rather than from `σ`: a ray through a `K`-point of squared norm `n` carries a cross edge at this rotation iff `1/n − sin²θ` is a square in `K`.

title: Gate A, the free-circle theorem: an integer multiplier of a `ℤ`-module scales one realised shell onto another
statement: For a `ℤ`-module `M ⊂ K²` and `k ∈ ℤ`: if `p ∈ M` has `|p|² = m`, then `kp ∈ M` has `|kp|² = k²m`, so `k · shell_M(m) ⊆ shell_M(k²m)` — each point `kp` then carries unit degree at least `|shell_M(1)|` once the arena reaches radius `|k|+1` (its unit neighbours `kp + shell_M(1)` are all in `M`).
grade: hand; the product owner, corrected 2026-09-12
verdict: closes — **as an inclusion, not an "iff"** (see the finding below).
rests_text: M63H2-T1's family screened at `n=4,9,12,16,36,…`; `CLAUDE.md` G52's clause `` `|p|²=n` free iff `n=k²·m` with `m` a squared distance the lattice already realises ``. **Finding (read against G52, per the audit's own rule):** the source's own later correction (`plans/M63-phaseH2-the-family.md` §6, "Gate A is sufficient, not necessary — `n=5` is not a square in `K` and yet Parts's lattice has 60 points at `|p|²=5`") demotes the inclusion above from an "iff" to a one-sided sufficiency; `CLAUDE.md` G52's phrasing "free iff `n=k²·m`…" is either trivially true (take `m=n`, `k=1`) or, read as a genuine discriminating criterion, not established anywhere in this material — the general question ("which `n` are realised at all") is answered only by direct enumeration (M63H2-T6) or ceiling arithmetic, never by this scaling identity alone. Proposed for correction at the close. **Caveat found at FS-71 batch 4d, filed here per the audit's rule that a theorem's caveat belongs in its own entry:** the hypothesis "once the arena reaches radius `|k|+1`" has never been satisfied by any object this project has built — `M63-phaseH3-plan.md` §10 measures that phase H2's own `n=16` arena stops at radius 4.0316 against the `|k|+1 = 5` this theorem needs for the degree-`|shell_M(1)|` conclusion to fire, and `plans/M63H3-derivation.md` T3 derives why: the diagonal circle sits at only `√(1−1/(4n))` of the much smaller endpoint bound, itself short of `|k|+1`. So the theorem's conclusion (full circle degree) is correct and has never once applied — a theorem whose hypothesis no object built satisfies (`CLAUDE.md` G30 failure mode 5).

title: Sealing depends on 11's residue degree alone; a ramified prime seals exactly as a split one does
statement: For `F = K(√d)`, `K = ℚ(√3,√11)`, with `11` **ramified** in `F/K` (`e=2, f=1`): the residue field at 11 is `𝔽₁₁`, `q ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, `i` is absent from it, the prime of `F(i)` above 11 stays conjugation-fixed, and `CLAUDE.md` G43's bound `χ(F²) ≤ χ(UD(𝔽₁₁,2)) = 5` applies — the field is **5-sealed**, exactly as when 11 splits (`e=1,f=1`, same residue field `𝔽₁₁`). Only when 11 is **inert** (`e=1,f=2`, residue field `𝔽₁₂₁`, `q ≡ 1 (mod 4)`) does `i` enter the residue field, the prime of `F(i)` split, no bound survive, and the field become 6-open.

title: Wall-breaking, for this family, is exactly `n` even
statement: For `ρ_n` with `cos θ = (2n−1)/(2n)`: the squarefree part `r` of the radicand `4n−1` satisfies `r ≡ 4n−1 (mod 8)` (write `4n−1 = r·k²` with `k` odd, so `k² ≡ 1 (mod 8)`); since `4n mod 8 ∈ {0,4}`, this gives `r ≡ 3 (mod 8)` when `n` is odd (2-adic wall stands) and `r ≡ 7 (mod 8)` when `n` is even (wall breaks) — with `r ≡ 5 (mod 8)` impossible in this family (it would force `4n ≡ 6 (mod 8)`).

title: The Parts-shape emptiness law: a ramification-parity iff (converse-corrected), and its instance on the mission's original target circle
statement: Write a point of `[Parts2020a]`'s lattice as `((a+b√33)/12, (c√3+d√11)/12)`; then `|p|²=n` (rational) iff `P=ab+cd=0` and `S=a²+33b²+3c²+11d²=144n`. In `F=ℚ(√33)` the ideal `(144n)` factors as `𝔮₂^{4+v₂(n)}·𝔮₂′^{4+v₂(n)}·(\text{odd part})` at the two primes above 2, both **inert** in `L=ℚ(√−3,√−11)` with residue field `𝔽₄`; an inert prime at odd exponent kills the shell count. **The Parts-shape shell at `|p|²=n` is empty iff some prime `𝔮` of `ℚ(√33)` that is inert in `ℚ(√−3,√−11)` divides `(144n)` to odd order** — at `𝔮|2` this is `v₂(n)` odd; at an odd `𝔮` it is a prime `p ≢ 1 (mod 3)` dividing `n` to odd order.

title: The shell-counting formula, specialised to this field: prior art `[BaakeGrimm2003]`, the specialisation and its six-fold verification ours
statement: For a module `M` in `K(i)`, `K=ℚ(√3,√11)` (class number 1, pari-confirmed both for `K` and `K(i)`): the number of points of `M` on the circle of squared radius `r² ∈ O_K` is `|U_M| · ∏_{𝔭 \text{ split}, 𝔭 | r²}(v_𝔭(r²)+1)`, zero unless every inert prime divides `r²` to even order, `U_M = \{ζ ∈ μ(K(i)) : ζM=M\}` (`[BaakeGrimm2003]` Theorem 1 and Corollary 1, whose closing Remark extends their `ℤ[ζ_n]` result verbatim to any class-number-one totally complex CM field over a totally real base — exactly this case). Specialised here: `μ(K(i)) = ⟨ζ₁₂⟩` (order 12, since `√3 ∈ K` puts `ζ₁₂=(√3+i)/2` in `K` — derived three independent ways in the source), the two primes above 2 are inert with residue field `𝔽₄` (contributing a factor of exactly 1 at every exponent, hence never obstructing), and the prime above 3 splits — so **count `= |U_M| · (v_𝔮(α_eff)+1)`**, `𝔮` the prime above 3.
grade: derived (prior art BaakeGrimm2003); the product owner and the prior-art gate, 2026-09-12

title: The counting compulsion (`CLAUDE.md` G53): a base-alone floor that can refute a type-M arena
statement: For a type-M arena (base `B` plus a rotated copy sharing the centre `0`, joined by the diagonal cross edges of the free circle) and any colour count `k`: a proper `k`-colouring `C` of the arena gives two proper `k`-colourings of `B` alone, `f(v)=C(v)` and `g(v)=C(Rv)` — `R0=0` gives `f(0)=g(0)`, and each diagonal cross edge `(v,Rv)` gives `f(v)≠g(v)`. With `B(h) = \{$circle $v : h(v)=h(0)\}$}`, any `v ∈ B(f)∩B(g)` would give `f(v)=f(0)=g(0)=g(v)`, contradicting the second fact — so `B(f)` and `B(g)` are disjoint. Hence, with `L = min` over proper `k`-colourings of `B` of `|B(h)|`: **`2L > (\text{circle count}) ⟹ $the arena is not $k$-colourable}`**, a property of the base alone, no arena solve.
grade: derived; the product owner, from a solver-agent measurement, 2026-09-12
verdict: closes (the general theorem is sound; its non-firing on `ρ₆₃` is a correctly reported negative result, not a gap).
rests_text: ledger row 64's mention of the family; `CLAUDE.md` G53 in full. **Not a theorem, demoted here:** the earlier reading "exactly 10 of 30, every time" from twelve *reseeded* colourings — retracted in the same source once pattern-blocking (which forbids, rather than merely re-asks for, a different colouring) exhibited a colouring with all 30 circle points at the centre's colour; the "provisional 10/30" is a floor (`L ≥ 10`) established by a flawed sampling method, not an invariant, and is superseded by M63H2-T10's exact `L=10`.

title: The matching-only arena theorem
statement: If a type-M arena's only non-centre cross structure is the diagonal matching, the arena is **four-colourable** as soon as the base has one proper four-colouring `C` in which no circle point takes the centre's colour: the shared centre forces any colour permutation `π` applied to the rotated copy to fix `C(0)` (since `C(v) ≠ C(0)` already inside the base would force `π(C(v)) = C(0)` to contradict that), so every `π` fixing the centre's colour satisfies every centre cross edge for free, and taking `π` a fixed-point-free permutation of the other three colours (a three-cycle) then satisfies every diagonal cross edge too, since no circle point sits at the centre's colour to begin with.
grade: hand; the advisor Poros, narrowed to its correct scope by the planner, 2026-09-12
rests_text: `ρ₆₃`'s own base **fails** the hypothesis — the solver agent asked exactly this question and got UNSAT in 20 s (no proper four-colouring of the base avoids the centre's colour on all 30 circle points) — so the theorem correctly does not four-colour `ρ₆₃`, and `ρ₆₃` also carries 36 off-diagonal edges the theorem does not reach; `n=20`'s matching-only arena (`120=60+0+60` per M63H2-T1's screen) is a live, untested target for exactly this theorem.

title: The cross-edge law for the type-M family, in closed form; the endpoint bound is its corollary
statement: Setting: `K = ℚ(√3,√11)`, `h(K) = 1`, `𝔭` a prime of `O_K` above 2 (`e = 2, f = 1`, residue field `𝔽₂`); `n ≥ 1`, `ρ_n = cos θ + i sin θ` with `cos θ = (2n−1)/(2n)`; `M = (1/D)·O_K²`. **(H1)** `√(4n−1) ∉ K` (equivalently `sin θ ∉ K`) — load-bearing: if it fails, `ρ_n ∈ K(i)` and `chromaticNumber_seamPlane` (kernel) four-colours the whole arena, so every statement below is vacuous without it. For `u, v ∈ K²` under (H1): `|u − ρ_n v|² = 1 ⟺ det(u,v) = 0 ∧ 2cos θ·(u·v) = |u|² + |v|² − 1` (the split lemma). Given `det(u,v) = 0`, every nonzero `x ∈ O_K²` is `c·x̂` with `x̂` primitive (`h(K) = 1`), and the points of `M` on the line `K·x̂` are exactly `{(g/D)x̂ : g ∈ O_K}` (the line-structure lemma), so a cross edge has a **kind** `t = h/g ∈ K`. With `V := n(g−h)² + gh` (the principal binary quadratic form of discriminant `1 − 4n`, the family's own radicand): `|u|² = ng²/V`, `|v|² = nh²/V`, `σ = |u|²+|v|² = n(g²+h²)/V`, `δ² = |u−v|² = n(g−h)²/V` — homogeneous of degree 0 in `(g,h)`, so coprimality is a normalisation only. **The endpoint bound as a corollary:** with `τ = h/g`, `|u|² = n/(nτ² − (2n−1)τ + n)`, minimised at `τ = cos θ`, giving `|u|² ≤ 4n²/(4n−1) = 1/sin²θ` at every Galois conjugate simultaneously — material outside that disk carries no cross edge at all, whatever the base's own extent.
grade: hand; the cross-edge engineer, 2026-09-12
rests_text: M63H3-T2's two-case criterion; row 65 item (i); the base-free counting law `ν·V = n D²` (§12.4, a corollary of the split lemma, `Sh(nD²/V)` the count of cross edges of kind `t` with no base and no radius — reproduced `ρ₆₃`'s rational family `100/9 ↔ 64/9` out of sample, §12.7).
kernel: declined — depends on `h(K) = 1` and exact valuation arithmetic; no Lean infrastructure built for the construction.

title: Theorem (the two-case monochromaticity criterion)
statement: With `g, h ∈ O_K` coprime, both nonzero, `g ≠ h`, `e = v_𝔭(g−h)`, `V = n(g−h)²+gh`: `v_𝔭(δ²) = 2e + v_𝔭(n) − v_𝔭(V)`, and the cross edges of kind `t = h/g` are monochromatic (invisible to the residue colouring) iff that is `> 0`. Exactly two cases arise (coprimality forbids `𝔭 | g` and `𝔭 | h` together): **Case A** (`v_𝔭(g) = v_𝔭(h) = 0`): `e ≥ 1`, `v_𝔭(V) = 0`, so `v_𝔭(δ²) = 2e + v_𝔭(n) ≥ 2 > 0` — **monochromatic for every `n`, odd `n` included**, and `v_𝔭(|u|²) = v_𝔭(|v|²) = v_𝔭(n)`. **Case B** (exactly one of `g,h` divisible by `𝔭`): `e = 0`, monochromatic iff `v_𝔭(gh) < v_𝔭(n)` — **needs `n` even**, since `v_𝔭(n) = 2v₂(n) = 0` for odd `n`.
grade: hand; the cross-edge engineer, 2026-09-12
verdict: closes. **§12.6 states what it does NOT say** (kept as scope, not a separate theorem): it classifies a given kind, not which kinds a base realises (the gap that sank the family screen of `plans/M63-phaseH3-plan.md` §9); it is not a colouring claim — 24 monochromatic off-diagonal constraints is not a refusal of four colours; one prime at a time; the base must lie in `(1/D)O_K²` over this `K`.

title: The base-growth monotonicity theorem, and the circle's position on the endpoint bound
statement: Every proper four-colouring of a larger base `B' ⊇ B` restricts (via `G.induce`) to one of `B`, so the set of interface patterns a base can present on a fixed circle is monotone **non-increasing** as the base grows, while the circle count is fixed (every circle point lies inside the endpoint-bound disk: `√n / (2n/√(4n−1)) = √(1 − 1/(4n)) < 1` for every `n`). Consequently, in G53's counting compulsion (`CLAUDE.md`), `L = min_h |B(h)|` over proper four-colourings `h` of the base is monotone **non-decreasing** as the base grows, so `2L > (circle count)` moves strictly the right way and never back: **growing a base past the endpoint bound is a free lever for a refutation and can never hurt one.** **Corollary (the corollary nobody predicted):** the diagonal circle sits at exactly `√(1 − 1/(4n))` of the endpoint-bound radius in every member of the family (93.5% at `n=2`, 96.8% at `n=4`, 99.2% at `n=16`) — **so the circle is essentially on the arena boundary by construction**, and the free-circle theorem's hypothesis (`M63H2-T2`, full circle degree "once the arena reaches radius `|k|+1`") has never been satisfied by any object this project has built (G30 failure mode 5 — a correct theorem over a domain nothing meets; the caveat is now carried in `M63H2-T2`'s own entry, `plans/M63H2-derivation.md`, added by this batch).

hand;
the arithmetic engineer, 2026-09-12

title: Theorem (the free-circle kill), and the additive-pair route theorem it produces
statement: **(the free-circle kill)** If every point of a type-M arena's diagonal circle `|p|² = n` lies in `2L` (`L` the ℤ-span of the base's unit vectors), then every additive four-colouring `φ` of `L` (a homomorphism `L → (ℤ/2)²` nonzero on every unit vector) sends the whole circle to the centre's colour (the colour group is 2-torsion, so `φ(2w) = 0`), so every diagonal cross-edge constraint `f(v) ≠ g(v)` fails for every additive pair `(f,g)`, and **no additive pair can four-colour the arena.**

title: Parts's coordinate shape is a `ζ₆`-submodule, not an `i`-submodule, and dropping it doubles the symmetry order without changing the ring
statement: Parts's shape (`p₁ ∈ ℚ(√33)`, `p₂ ∈ √3ℚ ⊕ √11ℚ`) is stable under `ζ₆ = (1+i√3)/2` and the whole order-24 group (verified: multiplying `p₁+ip₂` by `ζ₆` sends `p₁ ↦ (p₁−√3p₂)/2`, `p₂ ↦ (√3p₁+p₂)/2`, and both slots return to where they started), but **not** stable under multiplication by `i` (which swaps the two coordinate slots; `i·ℚ(√33) ⊄ ℚ(√33)`), so it is rank 4 inside a rank-8 module — not an index-4 submodule, an infinite-index one — and its own rotation group has order 24 against the shape-free module's order 48 (`⟨ζ₁₂⟩`, verified `i`-stable). **Dropping the shape IS adjoining the quarter turn.** **The closure/ring distinction:** the maximal `ζ₆`-stable (order-24-stable) module in Parts's shape has index 4 in `ℤ⁴` — four times denser than his own index-16 congruence lattice — but his congruences are the conditions for **multiplicative** closure (a ring, `R̄₂`), verified over 3,418,801 products with zero failures, while the denser index-4 module fails multiplicative closure at its second product tested; **so Parts's congruences are necessary for the ring and only sufficient (not necessary) for the group.** And generation — the ℤ-span of the unit vectors, the operative condition for a unit-distance graph's edge set — coincides with his lattice exactly (index 16 both ways) but not with the denser index-4 module (span index 16 ≠ module index 4).
grade: hand + tools; the arithmetic engineer, 2026-09-12, correcting the product owner's own P-H3-3
rests_text: the shape-free module's construction throughout the phase (16,309-point base, index 256 in `ℤ⁸`); the prior-art reading (`M63H3-T7`, `T8`) that dropping the shape is adjoining `i`, credited to David Speyer.

title: The `n = 2` shell is empty over the whole shape `M`, at every denominator, by Hasse local norms — an independent re-derivation of phase H2's Fact 2
statement: For `p = u + v√−3 ∈ M` (Parts's shape), `|p|² = 2` means `u² + 3v² = 2` over `ℚ(√33)`, i.e. `2` is a relative norm from `M/ℚ(√33)`. Since `33 ≡ 1 (mod 8)`, `2` splits in `ℚ(√33)` with each completion `≅ ℚ₂`; since `−3 ≡ 5 (mod 8)`, `ℚ₂(√−3)` is the **unramified** quadratic extension of `ℚ₂`, whose norms all have even valuation, while `v₂(2) = 1` is odd — so `2` is not a local norm at either place above 2, hence not a global norm, and **the `n = 2` circle is empty over all of `M`, at every denominator.**
grade: hand; the prior-art agent, 2026-09-12

title: The coincidence-rotation identity: the type-M family is, up to a half-turn, the `Σ = n` coincidence-rotation family of an imaginary quadratic order
statement: With `w = (1 + i√(4n−1))/2` (the standard generator of the ring of integers of `ℚ(√−(4n−1))`, valid since `4n−1 ≡ 3 (mod 4)`): `|w|² = n` and **`w̄/w = −ρ_n`** exactly. Verified symbolically for general `n`, and numerically at `n = 2, 3, 4, 16`: `−3/4 − i√7/4`, `−5/6 − i√11/6`, `−7/8 − i√15/8`, `−31/32 − 3i√7/32`. Since `−1` is the coincidence rotation of index 1, **`ρ_n` is, up to a half-turn, the coincidence rotation of index `Σ = n` of the planar lattice `ℤ[w]`** — the imaginary-quadratic non-generic case of `[BaakeZeiner2017]` Theorem 5.14 (crediting `[BaakeScharlauZeiner2011]` Props. 2.3, Thm. 2.6).
grade: hand + tools, verified symbolically; the prior-art agent, 2026-09-12; G62's core
rests_text: `CLAUDE.md` G62 in full (the entry's core identity); `M63H3-T8`'s commensurate/bounded corollary and Σ7 instance; G7's family theorem (M63H2-T1), now identified as a classical coincidence-rotation family rather than a construction with no name in the literature.

title: Commensurate ⟹ periodic ⟹ bounded by the base field's local bound, and the `Σ7` instance
statement: A twist is *commensurate* with a module when the two layers share a finite-index sublattice, equivalently when `√(4n−1)` already lies in the module's field; then the bilayer is periodic under that shared sublattice, so the arena graph on it is a pullback of `Cay(finite quotient)`, and its chromatic number is bounded by the quotient's — **a commensurate twist cannot raise the colour count above its base field's local bound.** Instance: `n = 3` (the Moser twist, `Σ3`, radicand 11 already in `K`) is commensurate and can never reach five; `n = 4` (`Σ4`, radicand 15 → `√5`) and `n = 16` (`Σ16`, radicand 63 → `√7`) are incommensurate and generate new fields, screened by the 2-adic wall test. **The `Σ7` instance:** the plane's own 7-colouring (`Instances/Seven.lean`, kernel, M36) colours by cosets of the norm-7 Eisenstein ideal `(−3 + ζ₆)`; its index-7 sublattice is identified as the coincidence site lattice of the 21.79° twist — the `Σ7` coincidence rotation, the textbook twisted-bilayer-graphene commensurate angle.
grade: hand; the owner, synthesised from M63H3-T7 and already-kernel facts, 2026-09-17
verdict: **closes — re-derived by the owner at acceptance (2026-09-22), the proof now on disk here.** Let `Λ` be the base's lattice with `ℚ`-span the CM field `E` (rank 4 for the Moser lattice, `E = ℚ(√−3,√−11)`), whose points have coordinates in the real field `F` (`Re z, Im z ∈ F` for `z ∈ E ⊂ F(i)`; `F = K` for the Moser lattice), and `ρ = ρ_n` the twist, `cos θ = (2n−1)/(2n) ∈ ℚ`. **(i) Commensurate ⟺ `ρ ∈ E` ⟺ `√(4n−1) ∈ E`:** two full lattices are commensurable iff they have the same `ℚ`-span; `ρΛ` has `ℚ`-span `ρE`, equal to `E` iff `ρ ∈ E`, and `ρ = cos θ + i sin θ` lies in `E` iff `i√(4n−1) ∈ E`. **(ii) Periodic:** `M = Λ ∩ ρΛ` has finite index in both; translation by any `m ∈ M` maps `Λ` to `Λ` and `ρΛ` to `ρΛ`, so the infinite unit-distance graph on `Λ ∪ ρΛ ⊆ L = Λ + ρΛ` (a lattice) is `M`-periodic, and every finite arena is a subgraph of it. **(iii) Bounded:** `L` is a finitely generated free abelian group and the graph on it is `Cay(L, U)` with `U` its unit vectors; for any `N` with `U ∩ NL = ∅` it maps homomorphically onto `Cay(L/NL, U mod N)`, so its chromatic number is at most the finite quotient's (row 56, `unitQuadrance_colorable_of_quotient`); and since every point of `L` has coordinates in `F`, the arena lies in `F²` and `χ(arena) ≤ χ(F²) ≤ L(F)` — a commensurate twist never leaves the base field, which is the sentence claimed. **(iv) The `Σ7` instance:** for `w ∈ ℤ[ζ₆]` primitive with `N(w) = |w|² = 7` (`w = −3 + ζ₆`), the rotation `R = w/w̄` has `cos θ = Re(w²)/7 = 13/14`, the hexagonal `Σ7` angle `21.79°`; `wΛ ⊆ Λ ∩ RΛ` (as `wΛ = R·(w̄Λ)` and `w̄Λ ⊆ Λ`), and `[Λ : wΛ] = N(w) = 7`, so the coincidence site lattice `Λ ∩ RΛ` is exactly the ideal `(w)` of index 7 — the sublattice whose cosets `Instances/Seven.lean` colours. The batch-4d implementer's *unsure* was right on the record: no written chain existed until this one.

title: The local-freedom product is a certified lower bound on a base's achievable interface-pattern count, and it is a one-sided kill test for the interface reduction
statement: Let `W` be an independent set of vertices in a base `B` (no induced unit edges — the "interface"). Fixing any one proper colouring of `B ∖ W` and letting each `w ∈ W` independently take any colour outside `c(N(w))` gives a family of colourings realising **at least `∏_{w∈W}(4 − |c(N(w))|)`** distinct patterns on `W` — a certified lower bound, computable in milliseconds from one colouring, no search. **It is one-sided**: on phase H2's `ρ₆₃` and on the record's own lattice the product evaluates to exactly 1 (no interface vertex has local colour freedom in *any* colouring, since each already sees three colours in its neighbourhood), while their TRUE achievable-pattern counts are 552 (enumerated, `M63H2-T10`) and unmeasured respectively — **a value of 1 is the instrument going silent, not evidence of rigidity**, and "large interface pattern count" (this instrument, large) and "four-colourable by an additive pair" are demonstrably independent properties (the `n=4` shape-free arena has the product `≥ 4.1 × 10³`, unaffordable by the phase-H2 route, and is still killed by no additive pair).
grade: hand; the solver engineer, 2026-09-12
verdict: closes. **Instance:** at `n=2`'s endpoint-bound arena the product is `≥ 3.83 × 10²¹` against phase H2's exact 552 — nineteen orders of magnitude, certifying the interface reduction was never affordable here without a solver.

title: `χ(ρ₆₃ arena) = 5` exactly: the upper half, by an explicit additive homomorphism

Every one of the 96 has the identical colour-class multiset `(10182, 10182, 10225, 10272, 10272)`. So `χ(ρ₆₃ arena) = 5`: `≥ 5` is `M63H2-T11` (already filed, batch 4c), `≤ 5` is this witness — a one-line certificate (`φ` on eight basis vectors) rather than a 51,133-entry table, needing no solver.

title: The superset-neutrality theorem: a `D`-reducible deletion cannot change the achievable interface pattern set
statement: Let `I` be an interface (vertex set) of a graph `G`, `S` a deleted set with `S ∩ I = ∅`, `A = V ∖ S`, and `P(H)` the set of patterns proper four-colourings of `H` present on `I ∩ V(H)`. **If `Extends G A 4` holds (`Absorb.lean`), then `P(G) = P(G − S)`.**
grade: hand; the phase H4 implementer, 2026-09-12
verdict: closes. **Two qualifications carried as scope, not separate claims:** the deletion must be certified against the graph *as it currently stands* under iterated peeling (`ExtensionOrder`'s `cons`, already the shape `Absorb.lean` builds), not against the original graph's degrees — the degree-≤3 case is safe either way, but a general `Extends` certificate can be destroyed by a co-deleted vertex; and if `S` touches the interface, pattern equality is meaningless (the two pattern sets live on different vertex sets).

title: The recognition: `Absorb.lean`'s absorption IS classical D-reducibility, and its exact boundary on a unit-distance graph is degree ≤ 4 excluding Gallai trees
statement: Written on a general graph with ring `R = N(S) ∖ S`, D-reducibility ("every proper four-colouring of the ring extends into the configuration `S`") **is `Extends G (V∖S) 4` verbatim**, so `extends_of_extensionOrder` and the 4-core peel are the degeneracy corner of the classical reducibility machine (`[Steinberger2010]`, tracing to Appel–Haken and Robertson–Sanders–Seymour–Thomas). **Singleton case, a two-line theorem, not a measurement:** any graph on `≥ 4` vertices has a surjective proper four-colouring (split a colour class in two), so `{v}` is D-reducible **iff `deg(v) ≤ 3`** — the 4-core peel is not an approximation to singleton D-reducibility, it *is* singleton D-reducibility. **The sharp general boundary (Borodin 1977; Erdős–Rubin–Taylor 1979, independently, cited via `[Steinberger2010]`):** a connected graph is degree-choosable iff it is not a Gallai tree (every block a complete graph or an odd cycle); applied to absorption, every free-by-degree deletion at four colours needs a connected piece all of whose vertices have degree `≤ 4` **and which is not a Gallai tree** — degree `≤ 3` alone (the greedy bound) is the *only* case degree information alone can buy past that. **Applied here:** `ρ₆₃`'s minimum degree is 6, so the sharp theorem gives zero with two full degrees of margin (not an artefact of stopping the peel early); and a claim that `[Parts2020a]`'s base (minimum degree 4) would benefit is **refuted by measurement** — its 18–24 degree-≤4 vertices are pairwise **non-adjacent**, so every candidate piece is a single vertex, and a single vertex **is** a Gallai tree (controls: `C₄` correctly not a Gallai tree; `K₃`, `P₃`, `K₁` correctly are), so the reusable screen is "do the degree-≤4 vertices touch each other in a piece containing an even cycle?", not "minimum degree ≤ 4" — zero on both objects this project holds.
grade: hand, prior art; the phase H4 implementer, 2026-09-12
rests_text: `M63H4-T4`'s exact non-existence bound; the decision to retire the classical-reducibility direction for `ρ₆₃` entirely (§10.4). **What is theirs and what is ours, stated in the discipline's own vocabulary (the audit's per-theorem procedure):** D-reducibility, the Appel–Haken/RSST/Steinberger machine, and the Borodin/Erdős–Rubin–Taylor degree-choosability theorem are **classical, [Steinberger2010]'s and its predecessors'**; the *recognition* that `Absorb.lean`'s `Extends` already is D-reducibility, the singleton two-line theorem, and the application of the degree-choosability boundary to a unit-distance graph (measuring `ρ₆₃`'s and Parts's own base's minimum degree against it) are ours.
kernel: declined — the recognition and the singleton theorem are short and could be formalised (`{v}`-D-reducibility iff `deg ≤ 3` is a two-line consequence of existing `Absorb.lean` lemmas); not pursued, since the direction is retired for the object at hand.

title: No D-reducible configuration of ≤ 27 vertices exists anywhere in the `ρ₆₃` arena — an exact closure, not a search
statement: From `M63H4-T3`(b), any D-reducible `S` with `|S| ≤ m` has every member `v ∈ S` satisfying `deg(v) ≤ m + 2` (since `|N(v) ∩ S| ≥ deg(v) − 3` and `deg_S(v) ≤ m − 1`). Peel the graph to the fixed point of "delete `v` when `|N(v) ∩ C| < deg(v) − 3`", started from `C = {v : deg(v) ≤ m+2}`: every admissible `S` of size `≤ m` survives this peel, so an **empty fixed point is a proof of non-existence**, not a failed search. Measured exactly on the `ρ₆₃` arena: at `m = 14` (the classical Appel–Haken/RSST ring-size ceiling), `m = 20`, and `m = 27`, the closure is empty (16,428 of 51,133 candidates survive the initial degree filter at `m=14`, all eliminated by the closure); at `m = 28` (the smallest size the necessary condition permits at all) 51,132 of 51,133 vertices survive. **So no configuration of 27 or fewer vertices exists anywhere in the arena**, against classical rings of size `≤ 14` (Appel–Haken, RSST) or `≤ 16` (Steinberger); the smallest admissible non-singleton ring measured is **77** (at `|S|=7`, the closed neighbourhood `N[v]`), where a ring of 14 has `199,291` colourings up to permutation and a ring of 77 has `≈ 2×10³⁵` — at `[Steinberger2010]`'s own stated four-fold-per-ring-unit cost scaling, about `4⁶¹ ≈ 5×10³⁶` times "a few minutes".
grade: hand + tools; the phase H4 implementer, 2026-09-12
rests_text: the retirement of the classical-reducibility direction for `ρ₆₃` (§10.4); `M63H4-T3`'s degree boundary.
kernel: declined — an exact combinatorial closure computation on a 51,133-vertex graph, `decide`-grade in principle, not pursued.

title: The orbit-closure equality theorem
statement: Let `R` be an upward-closed family of subsets of a finite atom set `A`, and let a group `H` act on `A` (no equivariance with `R`, with any colouring, or with any geometry is required — `H` need only act on the atoms). Write `cl_H(M) = ⋃_{h∈H} h(M)` for the orbit closure of `M ⊆ A`, and `min(R)` for the **inclusion-minimal** members of `R` (not the minimum-*size* ones, `{M}`). Then: > **`M_H := min{ |S| : S ∈ R, S` is `H`-invariant `} = min{ |cl_H(M)| : M ∈ min(R) }`.**

title: The subgroup-lattice monotonicity theorem
statement: For upward-closed `R` and a group acting on the atoms, `H ≤ K` implies `cl_H(M) ⊆ cl_K(M)` for every `M ⊆ A`, hence `H ↦ M_H` is **monotone non-decreasing on the subgroup lattice, always** (no equivariance hypothesis, and no dependence on the group order alone — two rungs of different order can be incomparable).
grade: hand; the M64 implementer, per Poros's §R10(c)
rests_text: resolves M62's own apparently non-monotone symmetry ladder (582 vertices at symmetry rung 1 against 558 at rung 3, `plans/M62-evolutionary-type-m.md` §R23) as a **search** failure rather than a mathematical anomaly — since rung 1 admits every rung-3 selection, its true minimum is provably `≤ 558`, so 582-at-rung-1 was never optimal; explains why an earlier reading of "+4 at order 4 against +10 at order 3" as non-monotone was a category error (Klein-four and `C₃` are incomparable subgroups, not points on one chain).

title: The independence complex of the correction-set hypergraph is not a matroid
statement: For the M63 L-side (402 atoms, complex = droppable sets = the independence complex of the minimal correction sets `Y`) and S-side stages, the basis-exchange axiom fails: **sampled violations exhibited in 3,296 of 4,000 trials on the L side and 1,029 of 1,128 on the S side** — an exhibited failure of the exchange axiom on a concrete pair of maximum droppable sets is a decisive refutation (one verified counterexample suffices; the sample size only measures how common failures are, not whether one exists). Consequently `{M}` is not, in general, the basis set of a matroid, so `Prof` (its orbit-coordinate profile image) is **not** a linear image of a matroid base polytope — consistent with, and independent confirmation of, `plans/M64-orbit-filling-polytope.md` §PA(c)'s a priori argument that `Prof` is merely semilinear (a projection of `{M}`, via Ginsburg–Spanier/Barvinok–Woods) and was never going to be a polytope's integer points.

title: The parity law
statement: Let `ρ` be the Moser twist (`cos = 5/6`, `sin = √11/6`), hub at the origin, `q_j = √3·w·ρ^j` walking a radius-`√3` circle. The chord from step 0 to step `j` satisfies `d_j² = m_j / 3^(j−1)` with `m_1 = 1`, `m_2 = 11`, `m_{j+1} = 5m_j − 9m_{j−1} + 2·3^j`, and modulo 2 the recurrence is Fibonacci (`m_{j+1} ≡ m_j + m_{j−1}`, seeded `1,1`), so **`d_j²` is even iff `3 | j`**. Since Theorem B's residue colouring identifies two points exactly when their difference has positive 𝔭-adic valuation (even squared distance, for a rational `d²`), **a pair forced monochromatic at four colours on the Moser ladder sits at a step divisible by 3; the first is `d_3 = 8/3`.** Equivalently, `ρ ≡ −ζ₆ (mod 8)`: the Moser twist has order 3 modulo 8.
grade: hand + tools; the mascot-challenge session, 2026-09-08
rests_text: MASCOT-T4's sieve (which chords are field-6-open); the M53 rigidity dial's independent confirmation (163/178 forced-equal pairs at `8/3`, none at 2 or 4, over 15,230 pairs — recorded there as an unexplained regularity that this law explains).

title: The one-case dichotomy under Parts's discharged lemma
statement: Write `z = m + nζ₆` for `L = ℤ[ζ₆]` (`n` the row). Under `[Parts2020hv]`'s discharged lemma (no monochromatic `√3`-triple, his 481-vertex computer part), every proper 4-colouring of `L` is **striped**: `c(m + nζ₆) = P_{n mod 2}[(m + φ_n) mod 2]` for a colour-pair partition `P₀, P₁` and a phase sequence `φ_n ∈ {0,1}`. **Theorem (exhaustive dichotomy):** either (i) no phase wall (`φ_n` constant on each row parity), in which case `c` is the residue colouring and MASCOT-T8's `ρ₄` spindle closes it (`χ ≥ 5`); or (ii) some `n` has `φ_n ≠ φ_{n+2}`, which is **not one monochromatic `√3`-pair but a whole lattice line of them** — for every `m ∈ ℤ`, `(m + nζ₆, (m−1) + (n+2)ζ₆)` is monochromatic at distance `√3`, since the connecting vector `−1 + 2ζ₆` (norm 3) joins two points of the same row-parity class, which wear the same colour pair exactly when `φ_n ≠ φ_{n+2}`. **The dichotomy itself closes; case (ii)'s impossibility is explicitly reported as not closed** ("I have not closed it, and I am not going to write that it nearly is", §11). Three sharpening remarks recorded with it: case (ii) is invisible to Parts's own lemma (no striped colouring has a monochromatic `√3`-triple at any phase, so his computer part cannot reach it even in principle — proved by MASCOT-T11 below); MASCOT-T7's cross-edge budget between `L` and `ρ₄L` is exactly six, the same count Parts uses to close his analogous case at `d = 2`; and case (ii) is "strictly easier than the problem the literature is stuck on" (Poros's reading, §11a, adopted) — it hands over an infinite, translation-invariant family of monochromatic pairs at one known vector, buying a local-contradiction target, a free choice of `m`, and several pairs at known relative positions inside one gadget, none of which the general "kill some monochromatic `√3`-pair, location unknown" problem offers.

title: No `√3`-triangle of `ℤ[ζ₆]` has all three vertices in one row-parity class
statement: The `√3`-vectors of `ℤ[ζ₆]` are the six solutions of `m² + mn + n² = 3`: `±(1,1), ±(2,−1), ±(1,−2)`; row parity is `n mod 2`, and only `±(1,−2)` has even `n`. A `√3`-triangle needs `v, w, v−w` all of norm 3; with `v = −w = ±(1,−2)` the difference has norm 12, not 3 — checked by exhaustion over all 12 candidate triangles, zero survivors. **Consequence:** this is the mechanism behind a gap in `[Parts2020hv]`'s Table 1 (non-mono-pair gadgets listed at `3, 7/3, 5/3, 1/3, √(11/3)`, none at `√3`) — de Grey and Parts both route through monochromatic-`√3`-*triples*, and no striped colouring has one at any phase, so **the entire triple-based apparatus is structurally blind to case (ii)** of MASCOT-T10, which is why a new ingredient is needed to close it rather than an extension of the known methods.

title: The chord-ratio identity
statement: Let `ω` be a rotation with `cos θ = c`, walking a circle by repeated `ω`. Since `ω̄ = 1/ω`: `ω² + ω + 1 = ω(2c+1)`, hence `ω³ − 1 = (ω−1)·ω·(2c+1)`, so **the step-3 chord is `|2c+1|` times the step-1 chord**; normalised to unit steps, the step-3 chord is exactly `2c + 1`. A pair forced monochromatic at four colours over `K` needs 2-adic valuation `≥ 2` (𝔽₄-residue arithmetic gives `> 0`; the six `ℤ/4`-type additive colourings of the Eisenstein lattice raise it to `≥ 2`), so the rotation must satisfy **`4 | (2c+1)` two-adically**. For the Moser twist `c = 5/6`: `2c+1 = 8/3`, valuation 3; the radius making steps unit is `r = 1/√(2−2c) = √3`; the spindle radicand is `4(8/3)² − 1 = 247/9`.

rests_text: MASCOT-T3's uniqueness search (which enumerates rotations against this exact criterion); MASCOT-T1's parity law, of which this is the general (non-Moser-specific) form.

title: Uniqueness of the Moser twist among low-height pinning rotations
statement: Among all `c = p/q` with `q ≤ 400` satisfying {unit steps, drawable in `K`, `4 | 2c+1` two-adically}, exactly nine rotations qualify; exactly two have base field equal to `K` itself rather than a proper subfield — `c = 5/6` (chord `8/3`, radicand `247/9`) and `c = −139/150` (chord `64/75`, radicand `10759/5625 = (7·29·53)/5625`). **`c = 5/6` is the one of least height, and it is the only one whose first two rungs are the Moser spindle itself.**

title: The deep-chord sieve, and minimality versus 6-openness in direct opposition
statement: (a) **Every spindle over a deep pair (a 2-adically deep chord on the Moser ladder) breaks the 2-adic wall automatically**: the radicand `4d² − 1` is `≡ 7 (mod 8)` at every deep step `j` with no exceptions, because `d²` is 2-adically deep — 6-openness is then decided purely by the Legendre symbol of the radicand mod 11. Sieving every deep ladder chord, **the 6-open/5-sealed status alternates**: `j = 3` sealed (`√247`), `j = 6` **6-open** (`√33063`), `j = 9` sealed, `j = 12` 6-open, and so on — correcting Poros's same-day claim ("every distance the law can select lands in a 5-sealed field") as stated too broadly. (b) **But minimality and 6-openness are in direct opposition**: the minimal forcing shape (`K₅ − e` in the `{1,√3}`-distance graph, §2 of the same file — itself retracted, see below) can only target the *first* deep chord, because a configuration whose target is a later deep chord contains the earlier deep pairs too, turning the pigeonhole into a disjunction over several candidate monochromatic pairs rather than a single forcing. On the Moser ladder the first deep chord (`j = 3`) is `8/3`, whose field is sealed — so the conclusion "K-fabric's Moser-ladder forcer can never reach a 6-open field" survives Poros's correction, for a structural reason rather than an arithmetic accident.

title: The Moser recipe's sharp threshold: the mascot challenge is impossible as posed
statement: The Moser spindle's recipe — take the smallest graph forcing two non-adjacent vertices to share a colour at `k` colours (a `(k+1)`-clique minus one edge), hinge two copies at a common vertex, pick the hinge angle so the forced vertices land at distance 1 — stops at `k = 3`, provably. **General form:** a host graph with no `k`-clique draws no minimal forcing gadget at `k` colours (`not_forces_of_drawing`), with the clique number the entire hypothesis. **Plane instance:** four points of the plane are never pairwise at distance 1 (`no_four_unit_points`, a Gram-determinant argument: any three plane vectors are dependent, forcing the Gram determinant to be simultaneously `1/2` and `0`), so **no five points of the plane carry a pair forced to share a colour at four colours, for any `k ≥ 4`** (`not_forces_of_unit_drawing`). **The threshold is sharp:** at `k = 3` the rhombus (`ζ₆, 0, 1, ζ̄₆`, injective, every edge exactly one unit) is drawn and forces its far corners (`exists_forces_of_unit_drawing_three`). **The contrast is the content:** at three colours the minimal gadget (`K₄ − e`) *is* a unit-distance graph (the rhombus); at four colours the minimal gadget contains `K₄`, and the plane's unit-distance clique number is 3 — the plane's clique number equals the colour count only at `k = 3` and falls below it forever after, which is why every 5-chromatic unit-distance graph ever built has hundreds of vertices and a computer behind it.

title: The rigidity theorem: a √3-clean 4-colouring of K-fabric is one of Theorem B's two residue colourings, and the dichotomy this forces
statement: *Hexagon lemma:* if a hexagonal unit shell about a point `O` has no monochromatic `√3`-pair, its rim is a proper 3-colouring of `C₆` with exactly one alternating pattern, forcing all three diameters monochromatic (`c(O + 2u') = c(O)`) — verified exhaustively over the six clean rim colourings. *Corollary:* a 4-colouring of `Σ₀` (the K-fabric unit-vector group) with no monochromatic `√3`-pair factors through `Σ₀/2Σ₀`. *The quotient:* `R/2R ≅ 𝔽₄ ⊗_{𝔽₂} 𝔽₄ ≅ 𝔽₄ × 𝔽₄` (the two projections being reduction at the two conjugation-fixed primes above 2), and the unit vectors surject onto `𝔽₄ˣ × 𝔽₄ˣ` (verified: 9 of 9). **Theorem:** every proper 4-colouring of the K-fabric with no monochromatic `√3`-pair is one of Theorem B's two residue colourings up to relabelling — because the quotient graph is `K₄ × K₄`, which has exactly 48 proper 4-colourings, every one a coordinate projection (the Greenwell–Lovász phenomenon: `K_n` is uniquely `n`-colourable in the categorical product — classical, self-attributed as such by the source, no novelty claimed for that step). **What is new is the identification**: the quotient of K-fabric by its own doubling *is* `K₄ × K₄`, with the two factors being the two primes above 2. **Dichotomy corollary:** in every proper 4-colouring of K-fabric, either some `√3`-pair is monochromatic, or every pair whose difference lies in `2Σ₀` is monochromatic simultaneously — `2Σ₀` contains `2, 4, 8/3, 8/√3, 2√3, 4/3, 4/√3, 2/√3`, so this explains in one line the shape of `[Parts2020hv]`'s published mono/non-mono table (§4 of the source).
grade: hand; Coxeter, 2026-09-08
verdict: closes — re-derived by the owner at acceptance (2026-09-22): the rim of a √3-clean shell is forced to the pattern `a,c,b,a,c,b`, so antipodal rim points agree and, shifting the shell to `O + u`, `c(O + 2u) = c(O)`; `R` here is the rank-4 Moser lattice `ℤ⟨1, ζ₆, ω₃, ζ₆ω₃⟩`, an order of the CM field `ℚ(√−3,√−11)` in which 2 splits (`33 ≡ 1 (mod 8)`) into two primes of residue field `𝔽₄` (each inert from `ℚ(√−3)`), so `R/2R ≅ 𝔽₄ × 𝔽₄`, the unit vectors land in `𝔽₄ˣ × 𝔽₄ˣ`, and the quotient graph is `K₄ × K₄`, whose proper 4-colourings are the two projections up to relabelling — the two residue colourings; the statement's "K-fabric" means that rank-4 lattice, not the rank-8 order `Σ₀` of `K(i)` — **with a scope correction the source records against its own first reading**: an early message claimed "the strata stand or fall together" (that the 2-adic depth stratification is not a hierarchy of difficulty), refuted by Poros against M56's own measured table (depth 2 free, depth 3 forced, simultaneously on one fabric) — the theorem itself is unaffected, but it constrains only the `√3`-**clean** colourings; the stratification lives among the `√3`-**dirty** ones, about which this theorem says nothing (§8, lines 212–243).

The check owed above is paid: the citation holds, as Corollary 3.]*

title: The cross-edge theorem of a twisted lattice pair, and the forced field of the pinning gadget
statement: Let `d > 0` with `d²` a Loeschian integer, `ρ_d = (2d²−1 + i√(4d²−1))/(2d²)`, `L₀ = ℤ[ζ₆]`, `L₁ = ρ_d L₀`. **Theorem:** the unit-distance edges between `L₀` and `L₁` are exactly the six pairs `(w, ρ_d w)` with `|w| = d`, together with the star of the shared centre `0` — no other cross edges exist.

title: The `ρ₄` theorem: an unconditional `√3`-pigeonhole realised inside `K(√7)`-fabric

title: The nine-point carrier of `core9_plane`'s pigeonhole is intrinsically a `ℚ(√5)`-object, and cannot be drawn in `K(√7)²`

title: The finite-plane bound, odd residue degree
statement: Let `F ⊂ ℝ` be a number field, `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` a rational prime, and `𝔭` a prime of `F` above `p` with residue field `𝔽_{p^f}` for odd `f` (so `−1` is a non-square there). Then every finite unit-distance graph in `F²` maps homomorphically to `UD(𝔽_{p^f}, 2) = Cay(𝔽_{p^f}², \{(a,b) : a² + b² = 1\})`, hence `χ(F²) ≤ χ(UD(𝔽_{p^f}, 2))`.

title: `χ(ℚ⁴) ≤ 4`: Theorem A's reach is not limited to the plane
statement: Theorem A (`colorable_of_residue`, kernel) asks only for an abelian group `M`, a subgroup `A`, and an additive map `ψ : A →+ G` nonzero on every edge difference — no ring, no metric, and (because `colorable_of_residue`'s statement never invokes commutativity) **no commutativity**, so it takes a quaternionic input unchanged. With `M = ℚ⁴` the rational quaternions, `A` the Hurwitz order localised away from 2, and `ψ` the reduction at the unique two-sided prime `𝔓 = (1+i)H` above 2 (`H/𝔓 ≅ 𝔽₄`): **(H1)** every rational quaternion of norm 1 lies in `A`; **(H2)** every one has nonzero residue (a norm-one element of a σ-stable subring is a unit of it — Theorem A's own mechanism, `isUnit_of_mem_normOne`); **(H3)** `ψ` is well-defined and additive on `A`, `|G| = 4`; **(LB)** four rational points pairwise at distance 1 exist (the rational unit tetrahedron `0, 1, (1+i+j+k)/2, (1+i+j−k)/2`), giving `χ(ℚ⁴) ≥ 4`. Together: **`χ(ℚ⁴) = 4` exactly**, `[BendaPerles2000]`'s value.

title: The valuation law is invariant under `d ↦ 1/d`, answering the necessary half of a posed duality question
statement: Over `K = ℚ(√3, √11)`, the kernel-checked 2-adic law (`residueColouring_eq_iff_psiA_zero`, `not_forces_of_residue_ne_zero`, `not_separated_of_residue_eq_zero`) says: a pair is a four-colour **virtual edge** (forced distinct) at distance `d` iff `d` lies at 𝔭-adic valuation zero (`v_𝔭(d) = 0`), and **forced monochromatic** iff `v_𝔭(d) > 0`. Since `v_𝔭(1/d) = −v_𝔭(d)`, **the "virtual edge" condition (`v_𝔭 = 0`) is invariant under `d ↦ 1/d`** — exactly the duality `[Heule2021]` conjectured and `[PartsOdd2022]` asked to have made precise: *"if an odd distance `d` is a `k`-virtual edge… then distance `1/d` is a `k`-virtual edge as well… does this duality work in the general case?"* `[PartsOdd2022]` §4 raised doubts after finding a finite counterexample at `d = 5` and reports Heule clarifying he meant the statement over the *field* `ℚ(√−3,√−11)` (read as points of the plane, this lies inside `K²`), not a finite graph. **This entry answers the necessary half**: over `K`, valuation-zero is `d ↦ 1/d`-invariant, so the duality holds as a *field-level* statement (never claiming anything about which finite graphs realize it) — it is necessary, not sufficient, and Parts's finite counterexample does not touch it (a finite graph can fail to realize a virtual edge at valuation-zero `d` without the law being false). **Open**: whether valuation zero is *sufficient* for a virtual edge in some finite `K`-object — row 59's own "Open" clause.

title: Theorem C over the real fields of S2: every translation-invariant Borel probability measure on `X₄(F)` whose spectral measure is carried by `T + A + Fin_S`, for a finite set `S` of split places, is carried by Pull; the real place enters only as an input, through `m₁(ℝ²) ≤ 0.2470 < 1/4`. (= J28V-4; J28D TC.)
statement: **Scope, exactly.** J28D proves the class form — "`F` real; one stable place `𝔓` whose tower is row 67's (tight at four colours at every level, every minimiser killing `𝔓⁴`); every other stable place of all-levels ratio `< 1/4` (this is S2); `S` a finite set of split places" (J28D §3.2 TC-class). J28V proves it over the three type-(B) fields (J28V-4) and records at its stage 5, row V11: "J28D's statement is the wider one, and my route reaches it unchanged" — a verifier's reading from J28D's statement, not a blind derivation of the class form. **Inputs** (the grade line both records give): C14.1–C14.3 and C14.2 (a)–(c) (window lemmas, two derivations at FS-86); `[AmbrusEtAl2023]` Thm 1 (`m₁(ℝ²) ≤ 0.2470`; external, computer-assisted; its certificate re-checked, cert + hand, `m₁(ℝ²) ≤ 0.246989`: exact on H1–H3 and H6 by J26, `plans/PA-ambrus2023-audit.md`, ball arithmetic on H4 and H5 by J49, `plans/FS100-KT1-ambrus-ball.md`); FS-66's certificates at 11 (ℚ(√59)) and 19 (ℚ(√83), ℚ(√131)); Lemmas D and P; FS38-D2-A/B; V3ram; VC-C2; weak and strong approximation; and, in J28D, Lemma R (b) (or J07's Lemma C), Bochner, Doob–Cohn and Lebesgue differentiation on doubling spaces. **Not used:** J21-MX, J21-RED, V3, C14's main count or C14′ as black boxes (J28D §3.1: C14 reads `𝔓` at finite level only and C14′'s conull-`Ω` format is not the edge-a.e. format a random extension produces; J21-MX selects a colouring of the other factors and says nothing about `c`). **Two routes** (J28V §Stage 5, rows V12–V16): both extend the colouring to `G_S` (R88-TC-ext), make it a.e.-proper, split off the finitely many Hoffman-failing stable places (11 or 19) with the real places and `S` into a factor `X` of ratio `< 1/4`, count against a compact tight factor, and propagate by gap-freeness. J28D absorbs every other stable place into the tight factor (R88-TC-Yp), regularises only inside `X` (R88-TC-reg), counts stationarily from the start (R88-TC-count) and returns to `R` by `C(δ) = 1` on `R ∩ 𝔓⁴`; J28V keeps those places as one compact tail factor (R88-J28V-3), regularises on all of `G_S` to a conull `Ω` (R88-J28V-2), counts samplewise and then uses stationarity, and returns to `R` by continuity of `h ↦ P(G(h) = γ(π₄h))`. "Neither uses the other's new steps"; they share the architecture and every transplanted and external input. **Sharp:** at ℚ(√11) the stable 7 (all-levels ratio `≥ 2/7 > 1/4`, `λ_min/d = −0.5617`) fits neither the tight factor nor `X`, and C9's colouring has spectral measure on `T + A` and is no pullback; at K the second tight place has ratio exactly 1/4; replacing `m₁` by Hoffman's 0.2871 at the real place flips the count's sign (J28D §3.4, the mutation audit: each hypothesis is the one a control violates).
grade: hand; over ℚ(√59), ℚ(√83), ℚ(√131): two derivations, J28D and J28V blind, independent routes over common inputs; over the rest of S2 (J28D's TC-class): J28D one mind, J28V's stage-5 reading "my route reaches it unchanged"
verdict: closes, twice over type (B); over the class, once (J28D) with J28V's reading.

title: The stationary Zhang count: a stationary, a.e.-proper four-colouring of `X × Y′`, with `Y′` compact and Hoffman-tight at `1/4` and `X` of window ratio `r_X < 1/4`, has almost every fibre `c(x, ·)` an a.e.-proper colouring of `Y′`; its classes then each have measure `1/4`, lie in the least eigenspace, and the fibre is a pullback `γ_x ∘ π₄`, `γ_x` constant a.e. by gap-freeness. (= J28D TC-count, L-C5, L-C6, C5–C7; J28V's C5–C6, the same count executed samplewise; J28V-11 on L-C5.)

title: The extension lemma: the spectral measure of a translation-invariant random four-colouring is carried by `T + A + Fin_S` iff `P(c(0) ≠ c(y)) → 0` as `y → 0` in `G_S`; then the colouring extends to a `G_S`-stationary process, continuous in probability, `{e_j}`-valued, with a jointly measurable version equal to `c` on `R` a.s., and `P(c̃(x) = c̃(x + w)) = 0` for every `x ∈ G_S` and every `w ∈ T_S`. (= J28V-1; J28D C1–C3, L-C1–L-C3.)
statement: J28D: the hypothesis **is** `τ_S`-continuity of `y ↦ P(c(0) ≠ c(y)) = 3(1 − σ̂(y))/4` (Bochner on `G_S` for ⟸, dominated convergence for ⟹), then uniform continuity in probability and Doob–Cohn; `P(c̃(x) = c̃(x+w)) = (1 + 3C̃(w))/4 = 0` since `C̃ = −1/3` on the closure of `U`. J28V: the cyclic subspace is `L²(Ĝ_S, M)` and the Koopman unitaries extend by multiplication by extended characters; properness at every pair of `G_S × T_S` by approximation from `R` (J28V §4 row V12: "the same extension, proved two ways"). Density of `R` in `G_S` by strong approximation away from a split place outside `S`, with Lemma R for integrality (both).
grade: hand; two derivations, J28D and J28V blind, two routes; the converse (⟸) J28D's, re-derived by J28V from the statement
rests_text: R88-TC, R88-TCA.

title: T-C(A), the type-(A) form: over ℚ(√47), and (J28D) over every real field whose stable places all have all-levels ratio `< 1/4`, no translation-invariant Borel probability on `X₄(F)` has spectral measure carried by `T + A + Fin_S` for a finite set `S` of split places, dyadic ones included; so a four-colouring of ℚ(√47)'s plane, if one exists, has an invariant measure on its orbit closure whose spectrum is carried by no `T + A + Fin_S`. (= J28V-5; J28D TC(A).)
statement: The steps of R88-TC with no tight factor: every factor of `G_S` has ratio `< 1/4` (11 and 19 by FS-66, the tail by Hoffman — the maximum 31's `1/4 − 2.745·10⁻⁶` —, the ramified 47 by Lemma P, the real places `m₁`, split places 0), so four classes cannot cover: `1 ≤ 4 max(α(Y′), r_X) < 1` (J28D) or `1 ≤ 4(r + η(n))` (J28V). The second clause: an orbit closure is compact and invariant and carries an invariant measure. **The asymmetry** (J28V §Stage 5): a split dyadic place in `S` (ℚ(√47)'s place above 2 is split, `ℚ(√47)_v = ℚ₂(i)`) rests on C14.2 (c) at `q = 2`; "for that step, J28D's re-reading is not a derivation; mine is". This is FS86-CL1's count moved from measurable windows to invariant measures with that spectral type, every stable place at once and dyadic split places allowed.
